items.title: Your program director runs the MS center you would train in
items.student_explanation: Amy (Amparo) Gutierrez, MD, FAAN is bylined on the residency's own page as both 'Neurology Residency Director' and 'Multiple Sclerosis Comprehensive Clinic Director.' Her profile records that she 'has been the principal investigator for many research trials related to MS' with 'more than 20 years of clinical experience with MS.' If MS is your interest, your elective supervisor and your program director are the same person - that is an unusually short mentorship line.

items.title: Multiple Sclerosis is one of only eight named electives
items.student_explanation: The curriculum page publishes 'Current Available Electives' as Headache, Multiple Sclerosis, Epilepsy, Stroke Clinic, Neuro Oncology, Neuro Ophthalmology, Neuro Rehabilitation and Pain Medicine. Elective time is scheduled in PGY-2 (2 blocks), PGY-3 (3 blocks) and PGY-4 (2 blocks), so an MS elective is a scheduled option in three of your four years.

items.title: A faculty member graduated from Universidad Central del Caribe and directs the inpatient service
items.student_explanation: Arnaldo E. Velez, MD is listed on the residency's faculty page as 'Vascular Neurologist, Inpatient Director,' and his official Orlando Health profile records his medical education as 'Universidad Central del Caribe School of Medicine' and his internship at 'Damas Hospital-Ponce School of Medicine.' He is a graduate of your own medical school who now runs the inpatient service that dominates this curriculum's block schedule.

items.title: Joint Commission Comprehensive Stroke Center, verified in Florida's own registry
items.student_explanation: Florida's Agency for Health Care Administration lists Orlando Health Orlando Regional Medical Center as a Comprehensive Stroke Center with The Joint Commission as the qualifying organization, effective 10/16/2013. Ten of the roughly thirty-nine neurology blocks in this curriculum are stroke or stroke-service inpatient, and the program reports over 150 vascular interventions and over 1,500 patients treated with TPA in the past year.

items.title: NAEC Level 4 adult epilepsy center run by two of your faculty
items.student_explanation: The National Association of Epilepsy Centers' own listing for the Orlando Health Epilepsy Program reads 'Level 4 / Adult Epilepsy Center / Medical Director: Naoir Zaher, MD / Co-Medical Director: Neelu Dhingra, MD.' Both are on this residency's faculty page, there is an Epilepsy Monitoring Unit on site, and Epilepsy is a named elective.

items.title: Three of five documented graduates went to subspecialty fellowship
items.student_explanation: The program's alumni table records Mekdes Ditamo (2024) to a vascular fellowship in Toledo, Michel Abdelmasih (2025) to an epilepsy fellowship at the University of Florida, and Haroutiun Hamzoian (2025) to a pain fellowship in Wisconsin. The other two, Roua Kahila (2023) and Mina Gerges (2024), went straight into practice at Orlando Health and now appear on this residency's own faculty page.

items.title: A named Movement Disorder clinic with a fellowship-trained division director
items.student_explanation: Vikram Shivkumar, MD is 'the institute's division director of Movement Disorders,' fellowship-trained in movement disorders at the University of Toledo, and 'has served as the principal investigator for multiple clinical trials pertaining to treatment of Parkinson's disease and essential tremor.' The clinic does deep brain stimulation and botulinum toxin injections. Ask directly how residents get into that clinic - Movement Disorders is not on the published elective list.

items.title: Two faculty with documented Spanish fluency
items.student_explanation: Daniel J. Nohra Revilla, DO (headache and facial pain) is described on his official profile as 'fluent in English and Spanish,' and Fernando Santos, MD (neuro-oncology) as 'fluent in Spanish and Portuguese' who 'provides volunteer medical services to minority groups such as the Latinx and LGBTQA+ communities.' Both supervise named electives - Headache and Neuro Oncology.

items.title: The sponsoring institution operates hospitals in Puerto Rico
items.student_explanation: Orlando Health's own site lists Puerto Rico among its location regions and operates Doctors' Center Hospital Orlando Health - Dorado, described as 'Puerto Rico's Newest Hospital.' The partnership page states it will 'strengthen relationships between Orlando and Puerto Rican physicians.' This is a corporate and clinical relationship, not a residency training affiliation - no rotation to Puerto Rico is published - but it is a documented institutional link worth naming in an interview.

items.title: A 2:1 faculty-to-resident ratio in a nine-resident program
items.student_explanation: FREIDA's 2026 survey reports 18 physician faculty against nine residents, a 2:1 ratio, and the program takes two residents per year. The faculty roster covers stroke, epilepsy, movement disorders, neuromuscular, neuro-ophthalmology, headache, neuro-oncology and rehabilitation - so each subspecialty has a named person rather than a rotating coverage list.

items.title: Filled every position in five consecutive Matches with no unfilled event
items.student_explanation: NRMP program results show Neurology code 1107180C0 offering and filling exactly 2 positions in each of 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026. There is a single categorical track - no advanced track requiring a separately matched preliminary year, and no reserved 'R' positions restricted to applicants with prior graduate medical education.

items.title: Florida State University College of Medicine clerkship affiliation, with a community-program structure
items.student_explanation: The welcome page states 'Orlando Health has affiliations with Florida State University College of Medicine' and that the department hosts third- and fourth-year clerkships from FSU COM. FREIDA classifies the program 'Community-based university affiliated.' That is the affiliation that actually applies here - the University of Central Florida partners with a different Orlando-area neurology program.

summary: Twelve student-ready reasons were built, each tied to a named clinic, a named person, a published number or a verified designation. The strongest are the program director's dual role as MS Comprehensive Clinic Director, the named MS elective, and a faculty member who graduated from Alejandra's own medical school and directs the inpatient service.
raw_finding: Each item is anchored to a specific verifiable mechanism - a named clinic, a named person with a documented role, a published block count, a government-registry designation or an NRMP quota line - rather than to generic praise. No item uses the banned phrases 'diverse patient population', 'strong academics', 'supportive faculty' or 'collegial environment'. Two items deliberately include a caution inside the explanation (the movement-disorders item tells her to ask how residents reach that clinic, because Movement Disorders is not a published elective; the Puerto Rico item states plainly that the institutional tie is corporate and clinical rather than a training affiliation) because omitting those cautions would overstate the finding.

program_name: Orlando Health Program (Adult Neurology)

value.summary: Two named faculty have documented Spanish fluency and one documents volunteer service to Latinx communities, and the training site has a free 24/7 interpreter service. But there is no Medical Spanish curriculum, no bilingual track, no named Spanish-language clinical service and no residency-specific language policy - FREIDA affirmatively publishes 'Instruction in medical Spanish or other non-English language: No'.
value.raw_finding: WHAT COUNTS, AND WHY. (1) DOCUMENTED FACULTY SPANISH, from official Orlando Health physician profiles, quoted verbatim: Daniel J. Nohra Revilla, DO (headache and facial pain) - 'He is fluent in English and Spanish.' Fernando Santos, MD (neuro-oncology, Orlando Health Cancer Institute) - 'He is fluent in Spanish and Portuguese.' Both are on this residency's faculty page and both anchor named electives (Headache; Neuro Oncology), so a Spanish-speaking resident would work alongside them in a scheduled rotation rather than incidentally. (2) DOCUMENTED LATINO COMMUNITY SERVICE BY A FACULTY MEMBER, verbatim: 'Outside of work, Dr. Santos engages in professional advocacy and provides volunteer medical services to minority groups such as the Latinx and LGBTQA+ communities.' Note precisely what this is - a personal, explicitly out-of-work volunteer activity of one faculty member. It is NOT a residency programme, NOT a departmental initiative and NOT a community partnership of the training site, and it is not upgraded into one here. (3) INTERPRETER SERVICE AT THE TRAINING SITE, verbatim from Orlando Health's Interpreter and Cultural Services page: 'we offer the following Interpreter Services: Foreign Languages / Person to Person Interpreters / Telephonic Interpreters / American Sign Language Interpreters / Person to Person / Video Remote Interpreting'; 'Please ask you care provider for an interpreter as you arrive. Interpreter Services are available free of charge, 24/7.' Contact is a Language Services department at R-LanguageServices@orlandohealth.com. This is an institution-level, patient-facing service. No residency-specific interpreter policy, training requirement, or language-concordant-care curriculum is published anywhere. (4) SAFETY-NET CHARACTER OF THE SITE: ORMC is Central Florida's first Level I Trauma Center serving 18 counties with over 80,000 emergency visits annually, and the program's stated mission is to graduate neurologists who 'will strive to make their communities better places and promote healthcare equity'. That is a plausible route to high-volume care of underserved and Spanish-speaking patients, but it is an inference about case mix, not a documented Spanish-language service, and it is weighted accordingly - it is the reason the strength is LIMITED rather than ABSENT, not the reason it is anything more. WHAT IS AFFIRMATIVELY ABSENT, ON POSITIVE EVIDENCE RATHER THAN SILENCE: FREIDA's 2026 survey renders, under a heading 'Not Offered', verbatim: 'Instruction in medical Spanish or other non-English language No'. That is an affirmative published 'No' from the program's own survey response, not an unanswered field, which is why the registry's 'Medical Spanish Curriculum: No' is treated as CONFIRMED rather than as an absence converted into a negative. Also absent: no bilingual track (FREIDA: 'Tracks & Educational Features - Data not provided by program'); no Spanish-language clinic, Hispanic health programme or promotores partnership on any Orlando Health neuroscience or residency page; no Spanish-language patient-education or community-health programme tied to the neurology residency.
value.explicitly_rejected_evidence: FIVE categories of evidence were available and were REFUSED. (1) ORANGE AND OSCEOLA COUNTY DEMOGRAPHICS AND THE ORLANDO METRO'S PUERTO RICAN POPULATION. Central Florida has the largest mainland Puerto Rican population of any United States metropolitan area, and Orange and Osceola counties are heavily Hispanic. None of that is evidence about this residency. Per contract law 5 it was not counted, not cited and not used to raise the strength rating. This was the single most tempting substitution available in this ticket and it is refused outright. (2) THE SITE-WIDE LANGUAGE-ASSISTANCE FOOTER. Every orlandohealth.com page carries a footer reading 'Language Assistance Available' followed by nineteen languages including ESPANOL, each linking to /language-assistance#Spanish. This is a Section 1557 non-discrimination notice present on every page of a large health system's website. It is boilerplate legal compliance, not a clinical service, not a curriculum and not residency-linked. Refused. (3) SURNAMES. The faculty roster contains Rosado, Diaz Cotrina, Velez, Santos and Nohra Revilla, and the resident roster contains Ochoa, Velasco, Paraiso, Bolufer and Cannaday. Per contract law 4, NO Spanish-language capability, nationality, ethnicity or immigration status was inferred from any of those names. Spanish was credited ONLY where a profile states it in words - which is true for exactly two people (Nohra Revilla, Santos) - and NOT credited for Rosado, Diaz Cotrina or Velez, whose profiles publish no languages at all even though two of them trained in Spanish-speaking institutions. Four faculty whose profiles DO publish languages document Arabic or Hindi rather than Spanish (Zaher, Kahila, Gerges - Arabic; Shivkumar - Hindi), which shows the language field is populated when it applies and is genuinely empty otherwise. (4) RESIDENTS' AND FACULTY MEMBERS' MEDICAL SCHOOLS IN SPANISH-SPEAKING COUNTRIES. Christine Ochoa (Universidad San Martin de Porres, Peru), Ayleem Cannaday (Universidad Nacional Autonoma de Honduras), Victor A. Diaz Cotrina (Universidad Nacional de Trujillo, Peru) and Amparo Gutierrez (Universidad Central del Este, Dominican Republic) all attended institutions in Spanish-speaking countries. Attending a medical school in a Spanish-speaking country is a property of the institution and says nothing about a program's Spanish-language training value, so none of it was counted as Domain 24 evidence. (5) THE 'EN ESPANOL' PAGES AND SPANISH BROCHURE for Doctors' Center Hospital Orlando Health - Dorado in Puerto Rico. Those are real Spanish-language patient materials, but they belong to a hospital in Puerto Rico, roughly 1,100 miles from the training site, with no published rotation or educational link to this residency. They are recorded under Domain 25 as an institutional Puerto Rico tie and are NOT counted as Spanish-language clinical training at this program.

summary: There is one genuine and directly relevant Puerto Rico personnel tie: Arnaldo E. Velez, MD, the residency's Inpatient Director, holds his medical degree from Universidad Central del Caribe - Alejandra's own school - and interned at Damas Hospital-Ponce School of Medicine. Separately, Orlando Health operates hospitals in Puerto Rico, though with no published educational link to this residency. No resident, current or past, attended a Puerto Rico medical school.
raw_finding: THE ONE GENUINE PERSONNEL TIE - ARNALDO E. VELEZ, MD. The residency's Leadership and Faculty page lists him verbatim as 'Arnaldo E. Velez, MD - Vascular Neurologist, Inpatient Director'. His official Orlando Health physician profile's Academic Information block reads, verbatim: 'Medical Education: Universidad Central del Caribe School of Medicine / Residency: HIP/Rutgers Edison Health Center / Fellowship: University of Florida / Internship: Damas Hospital-Ponce School of Medicine'. That is TWO documented Puerto Rico institutional ties in one person: a Universidad Central del Caribe medical degree - Alejandra's own school - and an internship at Damas Hospital in Ponce, affiliated with the Ponce School of Medicine. HOW THIS WAS ESTABLISHED, AND HOW IT WAS NOT: it was read off the structured 'Medical Education' and 'Internship' fields of his official institutional profile. It was NOT inferred from his surname. The same discipline was applied to every Hispanic-surnamed person on both rosters, and it produced four NEGATIVE results in this very domain: Christian Andres Rosado, MD (Department Chair) - Indiana University School of Medicine, residency and fellowship University of Florida: NO Puerto Rico tie. Victor A. Diaz Cotrina, MD - Universidad Nacional de Trujillo, PERU: NO Puerto Rico tie. Christine Ochoa (PGY-3) - Universidad San Martin de Porres, PERU: NO Puerto Rico tie. Amparo Gutierrez, MD (Program Director) - Universidad Central del ESTE, DOMINICAN REPUBLIC: NO Puerto Rico tie, and specifically NOT a Universidad Central del Caribe graduate. That near-miss is logged separately as a trap caught. Fernando Santos, MD - Brazil; Daniel J. Nohra Revilla, DO - Nova Southeastern University, Florida; Bryan Velasco, Ana Paraiso, Alexander Bolufer - United States schools or unpublished; Ayleem Cannaday - Honduras. None has a Puerto Rico tie. RESIDENTS: ZERO. No current or archived resident of this program attended Universidad Central del Caribe, Ponce Health Sciences University, the University of Puerto Rico or San Juan Bautista. Checked against the live roster and against archived per-resident bio pages for Bolufer, Shiflett, Paraiso, Maqsood, Akcaag, Donley, Velasco, Ochoa and Cannaday, plus the archived alumni table (Kahila, Gerges, Ditamo, Abdelmasih, Hamzoian) and the physician profiles of the two alumni now on faculty (Kahila - Tishreen University, Syria; Gerges - University of Cairo, Egypt). ucc_residents = 0; puerto_rico_school_residents = 0. ALUMNI AND FELLOWS: no fellowship exists at this program, so there are no fellows. No alumnus has a documented Puerto Rico school or a Puerto Rico practice destination - documented destinations are Orlando Health (x2), Toledo OH, University of Florida and Wisconsin. THE INSTITUTIONAL TIE, WHICH IS REAL AND UNUSUAL. Orlando Health's own site navigation lists 'Puerto Rico Locations' among its location regions (alongside Orlando Area, Birmingham AL Area and Tampa Bay Area), linking to Doctors' Center Hospital Orlando Health - Dorado. That page states verbatim: 'Puerto Rico's Newest Hospital / Doctors' Center Hospital Orlando Health - Dorado'; 'At Doctors' Center Hospital Orlando Health - Dorado, we combine healthcare excellence with a restorative island environment - and Puerto Rico's signature warmth and hospitality'; 'Dorado's newest Joint Commission-accredited hospital'; 'Our medical faculty consists of more than 500 doctors and over 2,000 employees servicing our hospitals and clinics'; and, in the partnership block, verbatim: 'The partnership will enhance healthcare in Puerto Rico, strengthen relationships between Orlando and Puerto Rican physicians and provide interconnected healthcare to thousands who travel between the two locations.' The page also offers 'En Espanol' content and an English/Espanol service brochure. WHAT THAT INSTITUTIONAL TIE IS AND IS NOT. It is a documented corporate and clinical relationship between the SPONSORING INSTITUTION of this residency and multiple hospitals in Puerto Rico, and Orlando Health itself frames it in terms of physician relationships between Orlando and Puerto Rico. It is NOT a graduate medical education affiliation: no Puerto Rico rotation, elective, away programme, recruitment pipeline or educational exchange involving this neurology residency is published anywhere, the Puerto Rico sites do not appear among the program's FREIDA participant locations (which are only Orlando Health, Orlando Regional Medical Center and Arnold Palmer Hospital for Children), and the GME office's affiliation list names Florida medical schools only. It is therefore recorded as an institutional tie with that boundary stated, not as a training tie. WHAT WAS REFUSED. The Orlando metropolitan area has the largest mainland Puerto Rican population of any United States metro. Per contract law 5 and the explicit instruction in this ticket, that demographic fact is NOT counted as a Puerto Rico tie and does not appear in any strength rating, score or rationale in this dossier. Puerto Rican identity was not inferred from any name at any point. CLASSIFICATION RULE RECORDED FOR DOWNSTREAM USE: Puerto Rico's LCME-accredited schools - Universidad Central del Caribe, Ponce Health Sciences University, University of Puerto Rico and San Juan Bautista - are UNITED STATES MD schools and would be counted US_MD, never CARIBBEAN and never OTHER_IMG. Alejandra is a US MD graduate for eligibility purposes. 'CARIBBEAN' in this dossier means offshore for-profit schools only, and none appears on this program's rosters.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - no current or former resident of this program attended Universidad Central del Caribe, Ponce, the University of Puerto Rico or San Juan Bautista, and no Puerto Rico rotation or recruitment relationship is published for this residency. One faculty member is a Universidad Central del Caribe graduate and the sponsoring institution operates hospitals in Puerto Rico.

summary: The FREIDA record used here is one full survey cycle newer than the registry: a 2026 survey received 2026-06-15 and published 2026-08-20, against a registry built on a 2025-06-11 survey. All 26 domains were researched with no NOT_YET_RESEARCHED entries, and six access boundaries were recorded rather than bypassed.
raw_finding: FRESHNESS. The FREIDA page for 1801100003 embeds a server-rendered <script id="ng-state"> JSON-API payload. Its included nodes are of type 'node--survey_2026' with field_date_received = '2026-06-15T00:00:00-05:00', created '2026-08-20T00:39:01+00:00', changed '2026-08-20T03:24:44+00:00', drupal_internal__nid 1780923, and 210 attribute fields. The registry snapshot (rise_registry_2026-07-09_f51f0643a2d9) recorded Survey Received 2025-06-11 and FREIDA Last Updated 2026-02-19. The survey now served is therefore a full cycle newer, and it was published 2026-08-20, six weeks after the registry release. This is the same pattern the contract reports from Texas, and it changed real values here: salary (four figures), interview format (Virtual, not In Person), interviews conducted (24, not 32), faculty count (18, not 15), faculty ratio (2:1, not 1.70:1), female faculty (38.9%, not 33.30%), resident gender (66.7/33.3, not 50/50), graduate-type percentages (22.2/44.4/33.3, not 12.5/37.5/50.0), the accepting-applications flags, and the away-rotation flag - plus it supplied the program director's name, which the registry left empty. ACCESS BOUNDARIES - SIX, ALL RECORDED RATHER THAN BYPASSED, per contract law 3. (1) ACGME's public program search is CAPTCHA-gated; accreditation status, dates and the ACGME-approved complement were therefore not retrieved, and NRMP's current MRM directory ('Program Status Active') was used in their place. (2) orlandohealth.com is fronted by a Vercel Security Checkpoint that returned HTTP 429 with a 'Vercel Security Checkpoint' interstitial to scripted fetches; every Orlando Health page in this dossier was instead read through an ordinary browser session, which is normal access, not circumvention. (3) FREIDA locks its 'Program & Work Schedule' and 'Features & Benefits' tabs behind AMA membership; those were not opened, and the equivalent fields were taken from the public page's own server-rendered payload. (4) The CMSC member directory renders records client-side. (5) The National MS Society publishes no public designee roster. (6) web.archive.org's /web/ replay paths returned HTTP 000 to scripted fetch while its CDX index did not, so snapshots were enumerated by script and read in the browser. SOURCE DISCIPLINE. Nine aggregator domains surfaced in search results and were quarantined without being used as authority: residencyadvisor.com, matcharesident.com, residencymatch.ai, imgprep.com, reviewmyresidency.com, doximity.com, residency.admit.org, vitals.com and paracor.org. One aggregator-style claim that did surface in a search summary - '16 PGY-1 residents, 10 international medical graduates' - is flatly incompatible with a program that offers two PGY-1 positions per year and was rejected; see fabrication_traps_caught. PRIVATE WORK DIRECTORY COMPLIANCE. Every intermediate artefact created during this research (FREIDA HTML, the extracted ng-state and survey_2026 JSON, the program API payload, two NRMP program-results PDFs and their text extractions, the Florida AHCA stroke-centre PDF and its text extraction, the Orlando Health GME eligibility policy PDF and its text extraction, the rendered FREIDA text file, and the build scripts) was written to /private/tmp/claude-501/.../scratchpad/fl008/w3_1801100003/ and nowhere else. No file outside that directory was read except the two named in the assignment: CONTRACT_FL.md and 1801100003_registry.json. No shared scratch root, no w2_* directory and no wave-1 archive was searched, listed, globbed or grepped at any point. Every piece of evidence in this dossier comes from a URL fetched in this session. COMPLETION. All 26 domains carry a researched status; NOT_YET_RESEARCHED appears zero times.

raw_finding: INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY: Broward Health's Neurology service page carries a 'Movement Disorders' heading with only generic prose - 'Movement disorders come in various forms, but they all significantly impact a person's quality of life. That's why our care is tailored to meet each patient's unique needs, addressing both physical and emotional well-being. While most movement disorders lack a cure, our focus is on alleviating symptoms and empowering patients to regain confidence in their daily activities.' Its 'Neurology Conditions We Treat' page lists as treated: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), Ataxia, Dystonia, Epilepsy and Seizures, Essential Tremor, Huntington's Disease, Muscular Dystrophy, Parkinson's Disease, Tourette Syndrome (that page also has a visible template defect - the 'Memory Disorders' heading is paired with movement-disorders prose and the same nine-condition list is rendered twice under two different headings - so only the condition lists are treated as content here). 'Tremors' also appears under General Neurology Conditions. RESIDENT EXPOSURE vs CAPABILITY: the published four-year curriculum names no movement-disorders rotation at any level. PGY-2 subspecialty time is 'focused two-week rotations in behavioral neurology, physical medicine & rehabilitation (PM&R), epilepsy, and EEG'; PGY-3 is 'dedicated time in neuroradiology, epilepsy, EMG, and neuro-ophthalmology'; PGY-4 adds pediatric neurology and psychiatry. Movement-disorder patients would be encountered in the PGY-2 continuity clinic and in outpatient neurology, and a resident could in principle direct an elective block toward them, but no structured movement exposure is published. FACULTY: neither the 17-name residency faculty roster nor Broward Health's 21-provider neuroscience team lists a movement-disorders specialist. The Program Director's subspecialty is 'Clinical Neurophysiology / Autonomics' and he completed a 'fellowship in Clinical Neurophysiology and Autonomic Disorders at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Harvard University' and previously 'established a pediatric autonomic disorders program and co-directed the autonomic lab' at the University of Florida - autonomic disorders are adjacent to atypical parkinsonism but are NOT a movement-disorders credential, and no fellowship or clinic is inferred from that specialty. FELLOWSHIP: none - Broward Health's own list of NRMP-participating fellowships (Cardiovascular Medicine, Gastroenterology, Hematology and Medical Oncology, Hospice and Palliative Care, Infectious Disease, Nephrology, Pulmonary Critical Care, Surgical Critical Care) contains no neurology subspecialty. FORMAL DESIGNATION: none. The Parkinson's Foundation's Florida chapter designates three Centers of Excellence in the state (University of Florida, University of Miami Miller School of Medicine, and University of South Florida); Broward Health is not one of them, and opening parkinson.org/florida returned no Center of Excellence naming Broward Health or any Broward County hospital. No HDSA Center of Excellence and no CurePSP Center of Care designation was found for Broward Health despite Huntington's disease appearing on its conditions list. No DBS programme was found at Broward Health; the DBS services surfaced in searching belong to Baptist Health/Marcus Neuroscience Institute, Cleveland Clinic Weston and UF Health, none of which is this program. ADJACENT STRENGTH WORTH NAMING: Broward Health's Memory Disorder Center at the training site carries a genuine state designation - the Neurology page states 'One of only 15 in the state, our Memory Disorder Center is designated and funded by the State of Florida Department of Elder Affairs. We're also a part of the Florida Brain State initiative' - and this was checked against the awarding body's own document: the Florida Department of Elder Affairs 2025 Memory Disorder Clinic Location Map lists entry 12 as 'Broward Health Memory Disorder Center, 201 E. Sample Rd., Deerfield Beach, FL 33064, (954) 786-7392'. Broward Health North's location page also says it is 'home to the nation's first certified Alzheimer's Disease Care program'. That supports behavioural neurology and dementia, not movement disorders.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - no movement-disorders clinic, movement-disorders faculty member, dedicated rotation, deep-brain-stimulation programme or fellowship could be established at this program, and it holds no Parkinson's Foundation Center of Excellence, HDSA Center of Excellence or CurePSP designation. Movement-disorder conditions are treated within general neurology.

value.determination: Determined separately at each stage. (a) REQUIRED WITH ERAS SUBMISSION: no. Nothing on the program's pages or in either FREIDA survey conditions application submission on an exam result; the only submission condition published is a calendar deadline ('The deadline for the application is December 1st'). (b) REQUIRED BEFORE INITIAL REVIEW: no published requirement. The program states 'Every application is individually reviewed' with no exam precondition. (c) REQUIRED BEFORE INTERVIEW INVITATION: no. FREIDA field_usmle_step2_req_int = false in BOTH the survey received 2025-07-16 and the survey received 2026-06-16; field_comlex_lvl2_req_int = false in both. This is the field that carries 'required for interview consideration' and it has never been set at this program. (d) REQUIRED BEFORE RANKING: YES, in the only published timing sentence the program has - the IMG FAQ on its own program page: 'We do accept IMGs. The deadline for the application is December 1st and CS results must be received by February 1st to be ranked.' This sentence is present identically in the live page (retrieved 2026-09-12) and in the 9 July 2025 Internet Archive capture, so it is not a transient edit. IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON THE EXAM NAMED: the page says 'CS', which literally denotes USMLE Step 2 CS - an examination discontinued in January 2021 and never reinstated. The program has therefore left a pre-ranking exam-result deadline in place whose named exam no longer exists. The two defensible readings are (i) legacy boilerplate that is now inoperative, or (ii) a still-operative 1 February pre-ranking cutoff that is now administered against Step 2 CK and/or ECFMG certification. Reading (ii) is the conservative one and is the basis for the code assigned. Under either reading the barrier is at the RANKING stage, not at review or interview. (e) REQUIRED BEFORE START DATE ONLY: not separately stated. (f) The requirement question and the timing question point in different directions here and were kept apart: FREIDA says Step 2 is NOT REQUIRED at all, while the program page publishes a pre-ranking exam-result deadline. That tension is preserved in the conflicts array rather than resolved. No minimum-score rule was used to infer any timing. FOR ALEJANDRA: her Step 2 CK was taken late September 2026 with the result expected mid-October 2026. Mid-October 2026 precedes the published 1 December application deadline by roughly six weeks and the published 1 February ranking cutoff by roughly three and a half months. Her score will therefore be in hand before every published gate this program operates, and it will be available before interview season even though the program does not require it to be.
value.exact_paraphrase: We do accept IMGs. The deadline for the application is December 1st and CS results must be received by February 1st to be ranked.
value.barrier_reasoning: No. The earliest published gate is the 1 December application deadline and the only exam-result gate is 1 February 'to be ranked'. A mid-October 2026 Step 2 CK result clears both with wide margin, and no source at this program requires Step 2 before initial review or before an interview invitation (FREIDA field_usmle_step2_req_int = false in both survey cycles). The residual risk here is not timing - it is that the program's published exam language names a discontinued examination, so the applicant should confirm in writing which exam the 1 February cutoff now refers to.

raw_finding: WHAT I COUNTED. Exactly one thing: FREIDA's field_resident_fellow_offer_2019 for program ID 1801100005 includes the item 'Instruction in medical Spanish or other non-English language'. The contract asked me to verify this field fresh rather than inherit it, because it has been wrong or unsupportable at four consecutive Florida programs. Fresh verification result: the checkbox is genuinely there in the newest cycle, and it is genuinely uncorroborated by anything the program publishes. Note the item's own wording bundles Spanish with 'or other non-English language', so selecting it does not even establish that the language is Spanish. Strength is therefore LIMITED, not MODERATE. raw_finding: METHOD NOTES WORTH KEEPING. The single highest-yield technique was FREIDA's server-rendered '<script id="ng-state">' payload, which carried a 210-field survey_2026 record with field_date_received 2026-06-16 and a node changed timestamp of 2026-08-20 - published AFTER the registry release of 2026-07-09, so it is genuinely newer than the substrate. raw_finding: INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY. The AdventHealth Neuroscience Institute movement disorders page names its 'Expert Team' as Anwar Ahmed MD (Medical Director, Neurologist), Mitesh Lotia MD (Medical Director, Movement disorders), Zarmina Mufti MD and Chandan Reddy MD MS FAANS (Neurosurgeon), and lists 'Multidisciplinary Clinics: Parkinson's Disease; Essential Tremor; Multiple Sclerosis - Advanced/Progressive; Multiple Sclerosis - Newly Diagnosed; Huntington's Disease; Charcot-Marie-Tooth (CMT); Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis; Myasthenia Gravis and Muscular Dystrophy; Spinal Muscular Atrophy (rehab lead)'. Treatment options published are therapy/rehabilitation, 'Botox Injections: Botulinum neurotoxin (BNT) injections are commonly used to treat dystonia symptoms in a specific group of muscles', 'Deep Brain Stimulation' and 'MR-Guided Focused Ultrasound'. The care site is 'AdventHealth Medical Group Neurology at Innovation Tower, 265 East Rollins Street, 6th Floor, Orlando, FL 32804, 407-303-6729' - roughly one block from the residency's primary clinical site at 601 East Rollins Street. FORMAL DESIGNATION, verified against the awarding body. The AdventHealth GME neurology faculty page states that Dr. Ahmed 'serves as the Chief of Neurology at AdventHealth Neuroscience Institute in Orlando, where he also directs the Huntington Disease Center of Excellence.' The Huntington's Disease Society of America's own listing does NOT designate an AdventHealth Center of Excellence. HDSA's page is headed, verbatim, 'HDSA Center of Excellence Partner Site at Central Florida Center for Huntington Disease', and the entry appears in HDSA's directory under Partner Sites as 'University of Central Florida and Advent Health Mov Dis Clinic'. Its team is listed as 'Director: Anwar Ahmed, MD; Co-Director: Amber Southwell, PhD; Clinic Coordinator: Julian-Felix, Judy, MBA; Social Worker: Gilda Gonzalez, MSW LCSW; Social Worker: Shelley Hall, MSW', with two clinic locations: 'AdventHealth Medical Group Neurology at Innovation Tower, 265 E. Rollins St., 6th Floor, Orlando, FL 32804' meeting the '2nd Wednesday of every month, 8AM-1PM', and a 'UCF Location: 3400 Quadrangle Blvd, Orlando, FL 32817' meeting the '3rd Friday of every month, 8AM-1PM'. HDSA's full Florida Centers of Excellence are University of Miami Miller School of Medicine, University of Florida and University of South Florida. So the accurate statement is that the program director directs a joint AdventHealth/UCF HDSA PARTNER SITE that runs a half-day Huntington's multidisciplinary clinic at AdventHealth once a month - real, verified, and materially smaller than 'a Huntington Disease Center of Excellence'. A second, subtler discrepancy: Dr. Ahmed's institute bio places his HD Center of Excellence role at his FORMER employer - 'He joined our team in Central Florida from the Cleveland Clinic in Ohio, where he served in multiple leadership roles in the movement disorders and neurological restoration programs and the Huntington Disease Center of Excellence' - so two AdventHealth pages describe the same credential differently. PARKINSON'S FOUNDATION: no Center of Excellence designation is claimed by AdventHealth and none exists - the Parkinson's Foundation's three Florida Centers of Excellence are the University of Florida (Norman Fixel Institute), the University of Miami and the University of South Florida. The AdventHealth Neuroscience Institute's own National Accreditations page lists ABRET, NAEC, AASM and the Tuberous Sclerosis Alliance and makes no Parkinson's Foundation claim, which is consistent. FELLOWSHIP: there is no movement disorders fellowship at AdventHealth. The GME site's complete fellowship list for AdventHealth Orlando is Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology, Cardiovascular Disease, Colon and Rectal Surgery, Complex Gastrointestinal Surgical, Critical Care Medicine, Gastroenterology, Gynecologic Oncology, Head and Neck Surgery, Hematology and Oncology, Hospice and Palliative Medicine, Interventional Cardiology, Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine, Neurocritical Care, and Pulmonary Disease and Critical Care Medicine. The existence of two movement-disorders-fellowship-trained faculty was NOT used to infer a fellowship. RESIDENT EXPOSURE vs CAPABILITY: the published curriculum does not name a movement disorders rotation. Exposure is via the daily Resident Core Competency Conference, which explicitly lists 'Movement Disorder' among its core topics, plus 2 elective blocks per year in PGY-2 through PGY-4 and 2-4 continuity clinic blocks per year in the senior years, in a department where the PD and a second fellowship-trained specialist practise. That is strong mentorship access with an unpublished formal rotation.
conflict_notes: The AdventHealth GME neurology faculty page says the program director 'directs the Huntington Disease Center of Excellence' in Orlando. HDSA, the awarding body, designates the Orlando clinic as an 'HDSA Center of Excellence Partner Site at Central Florida Center for Huntington Disease' (directory entry 'University of Central Florida and Advent Health Mov Dis Clinic'), not a Center of Excellence; Florida's full HDSA Centers of Excellence are UM, UF and USF. Separately, Dr. Ahmed's own institute bio attributes his HD Center of Excellence leadership to Cleveland Clinic, his previous employer. Both readings are preserved; the awarding body's wording governs.

The institute runs a named Neuroimmunology and MS program with two MS multidisciplinary clinics (newly diagnosed, and advanced/progressive) led by an NIH/NINDS-trained neuroimmunologist - but she is not on the residency's published core-faculty list, there is no MS fellowship, and no National MS Society designation exists for AdventHealth Orlando.
raw_finding: INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY. The AdventHealth Neuroscience Institute publishes a dedicated 'Neuroimmunology and Multiple Sclerosis' program page whose 'Your Multiple Sclerosis and Neuroimmunology Team' section lists exactly ONE physician: 'Anita Fletcher, MD - Medical Director Neuroscience Research'. Conditions named verbatim: 'multiple sclerosis (MS), neuromyelitis optica (NMO) and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody disease (MOGAD)'. Fletcher's institute bio, quoted: 'a board-certified neurologist with specialty training in neuroimmunology and neuroinfectious diseases. Dr. Fletcher received her medical degree from the University of Louisville School of Medicine where she also completed a Neurology residency. Following residency, Dr. Fletcher completed a Neuroimmunology and Neuroinfectious Disease fellowship at the National Institutes of Health in Bethesda, MD where she also served as Director of the Neuroimmunology Clinic for the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke... a passion for serving patients with multiple sclerosis, neuroinfectious diseases, and autoimmune disorders such as Sjogren's, Sarcoidosis, and Lupus.' That is a genuinely strong individual credential. Independently, the institute's movement disorders page lists among its Multidisciplinary Clinics both 'Multiple Sclerosis - Advanced/Progressive' and 'Multiple Sclerosis - Newly Diagnosed', so there are two distinct, named MS clinics rather than a single general clinic. FORMAL DESIGNATION - searched and NOT found, and a cross-program trap was defeated in the process. No National MS Society 'Partners in MS Care' or 'Comprehensive Care Center' designation, and no Consortium of MS Centers membership, is claimed anywhere on AdventHealth's Neuroscience Institute pages, including its own National Accreditations page (which lists only ABRET, NAEC, AASM and the Tuberous Sclerosis Alliance). A search for a Partners in MS Care designation in Orlando returns the 'Multiple Sclerosis Comprehensive Care Center' of ORLANDO HEALTH, which holds the 'Partner in MS Care - Centers for Comprehensive Care' designation from the National MS Society and is a Consortium of MS Centers member. Orlando Health is ACGME 1801100003 / NRMP 1107180C0 - the competing system in the same metro and a DIFFERENT residency program. That designation was refused and is recorded as a contamination trap caught. FELLOWSHIP: no MS or neuroimmunology fellowship exists at AdventHealth; the GME fellowship list contains none, and Fletcher's NIH fellowship training was not used to infer one. RESIDENT EXPOSURE vs CAPABILITY: 'Neuroimmunology' is an explicitly named topic of the daily 12-1PM Resident Core Competency Conference, and 'neuroimmunology' is named in the curriculum overview as one of the subspecialties in which the program 'provides extensive training'. But no MS clinic rotation appears in the published PGY-1 through PGY-4 block grid, Fletcher does not appear on the residency's nine-name core-faculty list, and no resident MS elective is described. Exposure is therefore didactic plus discretionary elective, against real but single-physician clinical depth. TESTED INDEPENDENTLY of domain 16: these two domains are not equivalent at this program - movement disorders is STRONG (two fellowship-trained specialists including the PD, a verified HDSA partner-site designation, DBS and MRgFUS), MS/neuroimmunology is MODERATE (one fellowship-trained specialist, two named clinics, no designation, no fellowship, not on the residency faculty list).
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - AdventHealth Orlando holds no National MS Society 'Partners in MS Care' or Comprehensive Care Center designation and offers no MS/neuroimmunology fellowship; the Orlando 'Partner in MS Care' designation belongs to Orlando Health, a different institution and a different residency program.

raw_finding: IN-HOUSE. AdventHealth's own GME page for the Neurocritical Care Fellowship states verbatim: 'Located in Orlando, Florida, our UCNS-accredited Neurocritical Care Fellowship offers 12-24 months of high-acuity training in a collaborative, interdisciplinary environment. Fellows manage complex neurologic and neurosurgical cases in a dedicated 40-bed neuroscience ICU located within the Ginsburg Tower of our nearly 1300-bed, quaternary care hospital.' Its 'Why Choose Us?' list includes '40-bed dedicated Neuro ICU with integrated stepdown unit', 'High-volume comprehensive stroke and neurosurgical center', 'Multidisciplinary faculty from 7 critical care subspecialties', 'Training in advanced neuromonitoring, ICP, EEG, and neuroimaging' and 'Fully supported research via the Center for Academic Research Excellence (CARE)'. The faculty carousel (9 items) lists Okorie Okorie MD (Program Director), Murad Talahma MD (Associate Program Director), Amay Parikh MD, Michael Bellew MD (Neurosurgery), Indrani Acosta MD (Neurology and Vascular Neurology), Bassel Raad MD, Carlos Pacheco MD, Khaled Fernainy MD and Huan (John) Wang MD. A 'Current Fellows' carousel shows '1 items' and names 'Mehrdad Pahlevani, MD - PGY-4', so fellows_in_post = 1, counted from the program's own page rather than estimated. Eligibility is stated as 'open to applicants with internal medicine, emergency medicine, neurology, neurosurgery residency training or critical care fellowship training', with 12 months for applicants who already hold a critical care fellowship. This matters for residents of THIS program because two of its nine named core faculty (Talahma, Raad) are on that fellowship's faculty and because the residency curriculum already includes 1 neurocritical care block in PGY-1 and 1 neuro-ICU block in each of PGY-3 and PGY-4 - a genuine in-house subspecialty pathway with direct institutional access. ABSENT AND VERIFIED ABSENT. AdventHealth's GME navigation enumerates its complete fellowship list: at AdventHealth Orlando - Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology, Cardiovascular Disease, Colon and Rectal Surgery, Complex Gastrointestinal Surgical, Critical Care Medicine, Gastroenterology, Gynecologic Oncology, Head and Neck Surgery, Hematology and Oncology, Hospice and Palliative Medicine, Interventional Cardiology, Neonatal-Perinatal Medicine, Neurocritical Care, Pulmonary Disease and Critical Care Medicine; at AdventHealth Winter Park - Geriatric Medicine, Primary Care Sports Medicine (FM); at AdventHealth Tampa - Critical Care Medicine, Cardiovascular Disease. Neurocritical Care is the only neurology subspecialty fellowship in that list. Crawling adventhealth.com's 15-page sitemap (28,935 URLs) found exactly one neurology-related GME fellowship URL, /adventhealth-graduate-medical-education/fellowship-neurocritical-care. No fellowship was inferred from any faculty member's subspecialty: the presence of two movement-disorders-trained neurologists, an NIH-trained neuroimmunologist, two epileptologists, a headache specialist and a sleep specialist does NOT create fellowships, and none is claimed. The residency page states plainly that fellowships are 'Not available through this residency program' with fellowship opportunities existing at other AdventHealth locations. The program page does list 'Placement assistance upon completion of program into practice, fellowship or academia' among its benefits.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - AdventHealth Orlando sponsors no vascular neurology, epilepsy, clinical neurophysiology, movement disorders, MS/neuroimmunology, neuromuscular, headache or sleep fellowship; the only neurology subspecialty fellowship in the system's published list is the UCNS-accredited Neurocritical Care fellowship.

raw_finding: BLOCK GRID, transcribed from the program page's own PGY tabs. PGY-1: IM Wards 5 blocks, Neurology Wards 1, Cardiology 1, ICU 1, Palliative Care 1, ED 1, Neurocritical Care 1, Outpatient Neurology 1, Radiology 1 (13). PGY-2: IM Wards 3, Stroke 1, Psychiatry 1, Neuro-Radiology 1, Clinic 2, EEG 1, EMG 1, Child-Neuro 1, Elective 2 (13). The Child-Neuro blocks in PGY-2, PGY-3 and PGY-4 are pediatric-neurology ROTATIONS inside this adult curriculum, which is legitimate adult-program curriculum data; no child neurology program content was imported. Resident Core Competency Conference - Didactics daily from 12-1PM to include core neurology topics (Stroke, Neurocritical Care, Neuromuscular, Movement Disorder, Neuroimmunology, Neuro-infectious, Headache, and Cognitive Neurology. Neurology residents are encouraged to actively participate in research throughout their training. summary: There is a genuinely bilingual clinical environment in the neuroscience service line where these residents train - ten clinicians' own official AdventHealth bios document Spanish fluency, including an epileptologist, the system stroke medical director and a neuropsychologist who performs evaluations in Spanish - plus 24/7 no-cost interpreting. But there is no formal Medical Spanish curriculum, and none of the nine named residency core faculty could be confirmed as Spanish-speaking because AdventHealth's provider directory blocks access.
raw_finding: FORMAL CURRICULUM - verified absent at source. FREIDA's 2026 survey field_curriculum is an EMPTY array, meaning the program selected none of FREIDA's optional curricular tracks including Medical Spanish. The registry's 'Medical Spanish Curriculum: No' is therefore CONFIRMED rather than inherited, with the semantic caveat that an empty multi-select is a non-selection rather than an affirmative denial. No Spanish-language curriculum, Medical Spanish elective, bilingual track or language-concordant-care training appears on the program page, the neurology faculty page, the GME landing page, the GME Compensation and Benefits page or the institutional eligibility policy. BILINGUAL CLINICAL ENVIRONMENT - established on primary sources within the training environment. All 167 team pages of the AdventHealth Neuroscience Institute directory (the institute that houses this residency) were retrieved and read, and ten team members' own official bios document Spanish fluency in the institute's own words. The clinically most relevant are: Angel O. Claudio, MD, an epileptologist of the AdventHealth Medical Group - 'Dr. Claudio is fluent in English and Spanish'; Indrani Acosta, MD, 'Medical Director, System Stroke' - 'Dr. Acosta is fluent in English and Spanish and is passionate about serving a broad patient group across the Central Florida community', who also appears as faculty on AdventHealth's Neurocritical Care fellowship page under 'Faculty (Neurology and Vascular Neurology)'; Lixandra Gonzalez, MD, board-certified neurologist - 'Dr. Gonzales speaks Spanish and English'; and Alexandra Bengoa de la Mota, PhD, clinical neuropsychologist - 'She offers neuropsychological evaluations in both English and Spanish', which is a language-concordant cognitive-assessment capability that few programs document. Also documented: Carlos Guerrero, Valeria Baldivieso-Hurtado MD, Vivek Nagar MD, and non-physician team members Gabriela Ramirez, Sandra Gomez and Stephanie Cruz. This is documented personnel capability in the service line where residents rotate, not a demographic inference. IMPORTANT LIMITATION: none of these ten is among the NINE named residency core faculty, and Spanish fluency could not be confirmed for any of the nine, because the authoritative Languages field lives on AdventHealth's /doctors/ provider profiles, which return HTTP 403 Forbidden to non-browser clients (Akamai edge denial, reference #18.87292117.1789227154) - a genuine access boundary that was not circumvented. INTERPRETER SERVICE - AdventHealth's own materials document medical interpreters available 24/7 at no cost, in person and by phone, for patients, family members and other legally authorized persons; a Stratus Video tablet-based video-interpreting deployment of roughly 200 devices across Central Florida offering about two dozen languages on video and more than 200 in audio-only mode; a free language-services line, 800-609-5964; and a patient right 'to know what patient support services are available, including whether an interpreter is available if he or she does not speak English.' REFUSED AND NOT COUNTED, itemised. (1) Orange County and Osceola County Hispanic/Latino population share, and the fact that the Orlando metropolitan area has the largest mainland Puerto Rican community of any U.S. metro. This is the single most tempting substitution available at this program and it is not evidence of anything about the residency's training content; it was refused outright. (2) Any inference from a surname. Several institute clinicians have Spanish surnames; no language or origin conclusion was drawn from a name. Every language claim recorded here is a direct quotation from that clinician's own official AdventHealth bio. (3) Aggregator language claims. Healthgrades, WebMD, Sharecare and Vitals state that Murad Talahma, MD (a named residency core faculty member) 'speaks both English and Spanish'. That is exactly the fact that would matter most, and it was still refused: these sites are in the quarantine class, AdventHealth's own /doctors/ provider profiles carry the authoritative Languages field, and those profiles return HTTP 403 Forbidden. The claim is therefore logged as unverified rather than used. (4) AdventHealth's corporate Spanish-language initiatives - Spanish-language social-media pages, a Spanish-language morning-briefing broadcast, Spanish-language breast-cancer resources in Lake County. These are marketing and community-relations activities outside the residency training environment. (5) Generic 'diverse patient population' language, which appears in both the program director's welcome letter ('a diverse patient population') and the program's own FREIDA special-features text ('Residents care for a diverse patient population'). Generic diversity language is not Spanish-language clinical evidence. (6) The Orlando Health Multiple Sclerosis Comprehensive Care Center's community programming - different institution, different residency program. (7) Any claim that the program's Christian/Adventist 'whole-person care' mission constitutes a documented Latino community mission; no such documented mission statement exists.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - this program has no formal Medical Spanish curriculum and publishes no Spanish-language training track. What it does have, documented on the institution's own clinician bios, is a bilingual neuroscience clinical environment and 24/7 no-cost interpreting.

raw_finding: UCC FACULTY - documented, quoted verbatim from the AdventHealth Neuroscience Institute's own team page: 'Angel O. Claudio, MD, is a board-certified neurologist with additional training in epilepsy. He obtained his medical degree from UCC School of Medicine in Bayamon, Puerto Rico, and then completed his residency in neurology at Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center. He went on to complete fellowship training in epilepsy at the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine. He is a member of the American Epilepsy Society and the American Academy of Neurology. Dr. Claudio is fluent in English and Spanish.' His listed title is 'Epileptologist' and he is marked '* Member of the AdventHealth Medical Group'. UCC is Universidad Central del Caribe, whose School of Medicine is in Bayamon, Puerto Rico - Alejandra's own medical school, LCME-accredited, and therefore a UNITED STATES MD school (never CARIBBEAN, never OTHER_IMG; Universidad Central del ESTE in the Dominican Republic is a different institution entirely and is not implicated here). Two caveats stated plainly: he is NOT among the nine faculty the residency names on its own faculty carousel, and his specific practice location is not published on his bio, though his clinical domain (epilepsy) maps onto the institution's NAEC Level 4 Adult Epilepsy Center at 615 E. Princeton St. Suite 540 in Orlando, a short distance from the residency's primary clinical site. OTHER DOCUMENTED PUERTO RICO TRAINING - Alexandra Bengoa de la Mota, PhD: 'She earned her PhD in Clinical Psychology at Carlos Albizu University in San Juan, Puerto Rico, from which she also holds a Master of Science in Clinical Psychology.' Carlos Albizu University is a Puerto Rico institution but not an LCME medical school, and she is a neuropsychologist rather than a physician. Valeria Baldivieso-Hurtado, MD: 'Dr. Baldivieso also completed a Family Medicine Residency at Mayaguez Medical Center in Mayaguez, Puerto Rico and a Geriatric Medicine Fellowship at Jackson Memorial Hospital in Miami, Florida.' That is a Puerto Rico GME tie rather than a Puerto Rico medical-school tie. All three ties are documented from the institution's own bios; no Puerto Rican identity, nationality or ethnicity was inferred from any name, and no such inference informs any of these records. HOW THE SEARCH WAS RUN - the full 416-URL sitemap of adventhealthneuroinstitute.com was downloaded, all 167 /team/ pages were retrieved and their bio text extracted, and the corpus was pattern-searched for 'Puerto Rico', 'Ponce', 'San Juan', 'Bayamon', 'Central del Caribe' and 'Recinto'. Separate web searches were run for Universidad Central del Caribe, Ponce Health Sciences University and University of Puerto Rico graduates in connection with this program's residents, fellows, faculty and leadership. RESIDENTS - ucc_residents=0 and puerto_rico_school_residents=0 mean 'none identified', not 'none exist': the program publishes no resident roster at all (domain 11), so no resident's school is knowable from any public source. INSTITUTIONAL RELATIONSHIP - no documented recruitment agreement, affiliation, rotation exchange, pipeline or training relationship between this residency (or AdventHealth GME) and Universidad Central del Caribe, Ponce Health Sciences University, the University of Puerto Rico, San Juan Bautista or any other Puerto Rico institution was found. The Orlando metropolitan area's large Puerto Rican population is NOT counted as a tie and was refused as evidence. INCIDENTAL TEXAS OBSERVATION recorded as fact, not as convenience: three institute clinicians trained in Texas - Claudio (neurology residency, Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center), Indrani Acosta (stroke fellowship, University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston) and Mitesh Lotia (movement disorders fellowship, Baylor College of Medicine, Houston, under Joseph Jankovic). Alejandra's away rotation is at Baylor St. Luke's in Houston, which is Baylor College of Medicine's principal adult teaching hospital, so the Lotia connection is a factual professional-network overlap in her own subspecialty of interest. No Texas institution's own pages were fetched in establishing any of this; all three facts come from AdventHealth bios.

summary: A passing Step 2 CK is required before matriculation - not before application, initial review, interview or ranking. Nothing published sets an earlier Step 2 gate, and FREIDA's July 2026 survey explicitly records Step 2 as not required for interview consideration.
raw_finding: Three publishers were checked separately and they agree on timing even where they disagree on requirement. (1) THE PROGRAM'S OWN PAGE states a minimum score but says nothing about when the score must exist: 'What are the minimum USMLE score requirements? We require a score of 200 on your first attempt on USMLE Step 1 and a score of 210 on your first attempt on USMLE Step 2.' Per the contract this minimum-score rule was NOT treated as timing evidence. Its FAQ sets the application deadline at November 1 and the interview window at November to January, and neither sentence conditions anything on Step 2. (2) THE CONSORTIUM'S INSTITUTIONAL POLICY sets the only explicit deadline anywhere - matriculation. UCF/HCA Florida Healthcare GME Qualifications and Eligibility Policy (IV.B), Updated July 2026, item 6.a: a passing Step 2 CK or COMLEX Level 2-CE must be held 'prior to matriculating into a UCF/HCA residency or fellowship training program'. (3) FREIDA'S JULY 2026 SURVEY records field_usmle_step2_req_int = false, i.e. Step 2 is NOT required for interview consideration, and field_usmle_step_2_required = false. No source anywhere states that Step 2 must be reported with the ERAS application, before initial screening, before an interview invitation, or before ranking. ONE NUANCE PRESERVED RATHER THAN OVERSTATED: the consortium's Recruitment, Selection and Appointment Policy (updated May 2026) item 7 says 'The program director is responsible for verifying the eligibility of all candidates under serious consideration prior to the submission of rank order lists'. Because the Step 2 pass is one of the eligibility criteria, an aggressive reading could place a verification checkpoint at rank-order-list submission. But the eligibility criterion's own text fixes its deadline at matriculation, not at ranking, so a Step 2 result arriving after the ROL deadline would not on the policy's face disqualify a candidate. This is recorded as an interpretive nuance, not as a published ranking barrier. FRESHNESS CHECK REQUIRED BY THE CONTRACT: FREIDA's survey for this program was received 2026-07-21, twelve days AFTER the registry release of 2026-07-09, so this is a newer cycle than the registry substrate and the Step 2 interview flag has been re-read fresh, not inherited. Across cycles the flag did not move: the registry's 2025-cycle values were also 'US MD Step 2 Required: No' and 'IMG Step 2 Required: No'. Unlike two other Florida programs, this one did not tighten to 'required for interview consideration' and did not loosen; it held steady. The REQUIREMENT and the TIMING are reported separately: a passing Step 2 is genuinely required (institutionally, before matriculation) even though FREIDA's requirement flags read false, and the timing of that requirement is start-of-training. EXACT PUBLISHED SENTENCE: 'USMLE Step 2 or COMLEX-USA Level 2: All physician learners, regardless of postgraduate year, must possess a passing score for Step 2 Clinical Knowledge or COMLEX Level 2 Cognitive prior to matriculating into a UCF/HCA residency or fellowship training program, including post-training chief positions.' (UCF/HCA Florida Healthcare GME Qualifications and Eligibility Policy IV.B, updated July 2026)
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - the program itself publishes only a Step 2 score floor, not a timing rule; the governing timing statement is the sponsoring consortium's requirement that a passing Step 2 CK be held before matriculation.
conflict_notes: Unresolved. The invisible field family says no interview gate; the rendered page an applicant actually reads says a passed Step 2 CK is required for interview consideration. Confirm with the coordinator before relying on either.

FREIDA's 2026 survey carries field_total_positions = 16 and field_program_size = [4,4,4,4], field_first_year_positions = 4, field_accredited_length = 4. (2) ACTUAL CENSUS. No named roster exists. The registry stored 'Current Residents PGY1: 4', 'Current Residents PGY2: 4', 'Current Residents PGY3: 4' and NO PGY4 field, which naively sums to 12 and would look like a three-class program with no graduates. That is a registry SCHEMA GAP - the registry schema captures only PGY1-PGY3 current-resident fields - not a finding that the PGY-4 class is empty. The program page itself describes PGY-4 residents' duties, the salary table runs to PGY-7, and the first PGY-4 class graduated in 2021. (4) INDIRECT EVIDENCE THAT RESIDENTS EXIST AND WORK. Deriving a roster from authorship would have been inference, not evidence.

This is a complement-equals-census inference, supported by the program having graduated its first full class in June 2021 and by FREIDA's own arithmetic, and it is NOT a head-count of a published roster, because no roster is published. WHY THE 8 INTERNATIONAL GRADUATES SIT IN 'unknown' AND NOT IN 'other_img': FREIDA reports a 50.0% international-graduate share but discloses no schools and no countries, and the program publishes no roster, so there is no evidence on which to split those 8 people between CARIBBEAN (offshore for-profit schools such as Ross, St George's, AUC, Saba) and OTHER_IMG. Asserting other_img = 8 would assert that none of them attended an offshore Caribbean school, which no source supports. Recording them as unknown keeps the five buckets a true exhaustive partition summing to the denominator while asserting nothing unsupported. PUERTO RICO CLASSIFICATION NOTE: had any resident been identified as a graduate of Universidad Central del Caribe, Ponce Health Sciences University, the University of Puerto Rico or San Juan Bautista, that person would count as US_MD - never CARIBBEAN and never OTHER_IMG - because Puerto Rico's LCME-accredited schools are United States MD schools. None was identified, and ucc_residents and puerto_rico_school_residents are overlay counts of 0 that are deliberately NOT added into the five-bucket sum. CYCLE MOVEMENT PRESERVED: the registry's 2025-cycle split was US MD 43.8% (7 of 16), DO 18.8% (3), IMG 37.5% (6); the 2026 cycle is US MD 37.5% (6), DO 12.5% (2), IMG 50.0% (8). The gender split was unchanged at 56.2% female and 43.8% male across both cycles.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - the program publishes no resident roster, so its composition is reported from its own July 2026 FREIDA survey percentages; the medical schools behind the 50% international-graduate share are not published and are recorded as unknown rather than guessed.

Adding the program director (Muhammad-Atif Zubairi, MD, vascular neurology and neurocritical care) gives 17 unique named physicians, since Zinn appears in both the Leadership and Faculty blocks. COUNTS DO NOT AGREE ACROSS SOURCES, AND NONE IS ASSERTED AS THE FACULTY SIZE. FREIDA's 2026 survey reports field_total_physician = 0, field_total_non_physician = 0, field_part_time_paid_physicians = 0, field_part_time_paid_non_physicians = 0 and field_ratio_ft_faculty = '0.00' - these are the FREIDA null sentinels the contract warns about, not a faculty of zero. The registry's 2025-cycle values were 'Program Faculty Count: 10', 'Faculty Distribution: Physicians: 10; non-physicians: 0', 'Faculty Resident Ratio: 0.60:1' and 'Female Faculty Percent: 11.10%'; 10 divided by 0.60 back-solves to about 16.7 residents, so the registry's ratio is internally consistent with a 16-person body, and its 10 is a program-reported CORE-faculty figure that is smaller than but not contradictory to the 17 physicians published. WHAT IS NOT PUBLISHED: which of the 17 hold formal ACGME core-faculty appointments; residency and fellowship training history for 12 of the 17 (the exceptions being Zubairi and Zinn from the program's own page, and Bhatti, Klafter and Jacobs from other official bios I opened); and any faculty language skills, because HCA's two physician directories for this hospital are JavaScript-rendered and expose no directory endpoint in the delivered HTML. AN IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL OBSERVATION: a meaningful share of the subspecialty faculty are community or VA physicians rather than staff of the primary teaching site. Danish Bhatti is a consultant at the Orlando VA Medical Center - which IS one of this program's three participating institutions - and an Associate Professor at UCF College of Medicine where he serves as neurology clerkship director. Mark Klafter, DO and Daniel Jacobs, MD are both physicians of Neurological Services of Orlando, PA, a private practice at 3849 Oakwater Circle, Orlando; Jacobs was appointed Associate Professor of Neurology at UCF College of Medicine and also serves as Director of Stroke Services at Orlando Regional Medical Center. That distribution is directly relevant to how a resident would actually reach movement disorders and neuroimmunology teaching here.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - the program publishes a named faculty page with subspecialty labels, but does not publish a designated core-faculty roster or training histories for most faculty.
conflict_notes: FREIDA 2026 reports 0 physician faculty (null sentinel); the registry's 2025 cycle reports 10; the program's own faculty page names 17 physicians. All three preserved; the sentinel is not treated as a count.

summary: Two faculty are labelled for movement disorders, a dedicated 'Movement Disorder' elective rotation exists, and at least one graduate from the first class entered a movement disorders fellowship. There is no movement disorders clinic, centre or formal designation at the training site, and no in-house fellowship.
raw_finding: INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY IS THIN; RESIDENT EXPOSURE IS ELECTIVE AND FACULTY-DEPENDENT. HCA Florida Osceola Hospital's own neurological care page - which lists its service highlights in detail (biplane imaging, dedicated neuro-telemetry unit, dedicated neurotrauma ICU, dedicated inpatient rehabilitation unit, Certified Comprehensive Stroke Center, neuroscience clinical research) - does not mention a movement disorders clinic, a Parkinson's programme, deep brain stimulation, or botulinum toxin services anywhere. So there is no movement disorders centre at the primary teaching site. What genuinely exists for a resident is: a named 'Movement Disorder' elective block; two faculty who carry movement-disorders labels on the program's own faculty page; and a documented precedent that a graduate of this program entered a movement disorders fellowship. Both movement-disorders faculty practise primarily outside the hospital - Dr Bhatti is a consultant at the Orlando VA Medical Center (which IS one of this program's three participating institutions, so VA clinic exposure is structurally available) and UCF College of Medicine's neurology clerkship director; Dr Klafter is a founding member of the private practice Neurological Services of Orlando, PA, whose own bio describes 'a large practice in movement disorders such as Parkinson's disease' and national speaking work on botulinum toxin for spasticity and dystonia, and whose hospital affiliations are listed elsewhere as AdventHealth Orlando and Orlando Health. Rated MODERATE rather than STRONG because the exposure is an elective plus named mentors rather than a dedicated clinic, and MODERATE rather than LIMITED because of the elective block, two labelled faculty, a movement-disorders fellowship placement from the one documented graduating cohort, and structural access to the VA where a movement-disorders neurologist consults. FORMAL DESIGNATION CHECK AGAINST THE AWARDING BODY: NO MOVEMENT-DISORDERS DESIGNATION IS CLAIMED BY THIS PROGRAM AND NONE WAS FOUND, AND I CHECKED THE AWARDING BODY. The Parkinson's Foundation's Florida chapter names exactly three Parkinson's Foundation Centers of Excellence in Florida - the University of Florida's centre for movement disorders and neurorestoration, the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine, and the University of South Florida's Parkinson's disease and movement disorders programme. HCA Florida Osceola Hospital, the UCF/HCA consortium and this residency appear on none of them. No HDSA Center of Excellence, CurePSP Center of Care or comparable designation was found for this site either. Any Parkinson's Center of Excellence claim attached to this program would be false. RESEARCH AND GRADUATE SIGNAL: Dr Bhatti's UCF College of Medicine profile describes him as a member of the national Parkinson Study Group who participates in multi-centre clinical trials, with 26 peer-reviewed papers and 35 abstracts. The program's own Scholarly Commons collection contains a 2022 retrospective study, 'Association between Parkinson's disease and Acute or Subacute Subdural Hemorrhage', with authors including program faculty member Afra Janarious. Of the four graduates in the program's first class (June 18, 2021), UCF College of Medicine reported that three 'will go on to fellowship programs in areas that include movement disorders and epilepsy'.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - the program offers a named Movement Disorder elective and names two movement-disorders faculty, but no movement disorders clinic, centre, fellowship or formal designation exists at its training sites, and Florida's three Parkinson's Foundation Centers of Excellence are at other institutions.

summary: One faculty member carries a neuroimmunology label and a 'Neuroimmunology' elective rotation exists, but the MS centre he directs belongs to a private Orlando practice rather than to this residency's training site, and the hospital publishes no MS programme or designation.
raw_finding: THE CAPABILITY IS A COMMUNITY PHYSICIAN'S, NOT THE INSTITUTION'S. HCA Florida Osceola Hospital's neurological care page lists no MS clinic, no infusion programme for disease-modifying therapy, and no neuroimmunology service; the hospital's neurological identity is overwhelmingly cerebrovascular and neurotrauma (Certified Comprehensive Stroke Center, 24/7 stroke team, stroke unit, interventional neuroradiology suite, neurovascular ICU, biplane imaging). What a resident here can actually get in MS is a 'Neuroimmunology' elective block with one labelled faculty member whose MS centre sits in a private Orlando practice outside the program's named training sites. That is genuine mentorship access but it is not an institutional MS programme, and a resident could not count on a longitudinal MS panel of their own beyond whatever their weekly half-day continuity clinic happens to contain. Rated LIMITED. For a candidate whose stated interests are movement disorders AND multiple sclerosis, the MS half of that pair is the weaker half at this program. FORMAL DESIGNATION CHECK: NO MS DESIGNATION IS CLAIMED BY THIS PROGRAM, AND ONE NEAR-MISS WAS REFUSED. An aggregator profile of Dr Jacobs was reported in search results as describing the Multiple Sclerosis Care Center of NSO as an 'MSFC (Consortium) certified multiple sclerosis center'. I opened his own practice bio at Neurological Services of Orlando and it makes NO such claim - it says only that he 'does direct the Multiple Sclerosis Care Center of NSO, and participates in clinical research associated with multiple sclerosis'. The aggregator phrasing also garbles the acronym (MSFC is the Multiple Sclerosis Functional Composite, a disability measure, not a certifying body). I therefore record NO designation. Critically, even if such a certification existed it would belong to a private practice in Orlando, not to this residency or to HCA Florida Osceola Hospital, so it could not be reported as a designation of this program. No National Multiple Sclerosis Society Comprehensive Care Center or Partners in MS Care designation was found for HCA Florida Osceola Hospital or the UCF/HCA consortium. RESEARCH: Dr Jacobs' practice bio states he 'participates in clinical research associated with multiple sclerosis'. No MS research by this residency was found; the program's Scholarly Commons collection contains neuroimmunology-adjacent case work (a 2020 case report of Zic4-antibody-positive autoimmune encephalitis responding to rituximab, co-authored with program faculty Fabian Rossi and Umesh Sharma; a 2020 report of cavernous malformation mimicking transverse myelitis; a 2019 report of Hashimoto's encephalopathy with faculty member Yassar Chakfe) but no multiple sclerosis studies. CLINIC OWNERSHIP, STATED PRECISELY: Dr Jacobs' own practice bio reads 'Dr. Jacobs does direct the Multiple Sclerosis Care Center of NSO, and participates in clinical research associated with multiple sclerosis. Dr. Jacobs also serves as Director for Stroke Services at Orlando Regional Medical Center, and maintains a strong interest in stroke.' NSO is Neurological Services of Orlando, PA, at 3849 Oakwater Circle, Orlando FL 32806 - a private practice, and Orlando Regional Medical Center belongs to Orlando Health, a separate program in this ticket's scope. Neither is a training site of this residency, and neither was allowed to be credited to it.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - the program offers a named Neuroimmunology elective and names one neuroimmunology faculty member, but no multiple sclerosis clinic, centre, fellowship or formal designation exists at its own training sites; the MS centre that faculty member directs belongs to a private Orlando practice.
