raw_finding: WHAT I SEARCHED. The program's four published pages (index with mission, program overview, conference schedule, salary and FAQ; welcome letter; faculty; curriculum), the HCA Healthcare GME location page for HCA Florida Osceola Hospital, the hospital's own neurological care page, UCF College of Medicine's GME landing, programs, admissions, institutional-team, policies, hospital-partners and benefits pages, the consortium's Qualifications and Eligibility Policy (July 2026) and Recruitment, Selection and Appointment Policy (May 2026), FREIDA's complete 210-field 2026 survey record, the program's Scholarly Commons collection, and targeted web searches pairing this program and hospital with 'medical Spanish', 'bilingual', 'interpreter' and 'Spanish-speaking'. WHAT I FOUND. Nothing. The word Spanish does not appear in any program-authored content. FREIDA's 2026 survey for this program has field_curriculum = [] - an empty curriculum array, meaning no curriculum items including medical Spanish are reported for the current cycle. REGISTRY VALUE VERIFIED FRESH, NOT INHERITED: the registry's 'Medical Spanish Curriculum: No' came from the 2025-06-25 survey; I re-read the newer 2026-07-21 survey independently and it likewise reports no medical Spanish curriculum. The contract records that this registry field was wrong at 3 of 16 Texas programs, twice by sibling-program contamination, so it was re-derived rather than accepted - and it survives. THE DESIGNATION-STYLE TRAP I REFUSED. A web search for medical Spanish at this program returned a summary asserting 'The HCA Florida Healthcare Program in Neurology includes instruction in medical Spanish or other non-English language as part of its curriculum offerings.' That sentence describes the HCA FLORIDA HEALTHCARE PROGRAM IN NEUROLOGY AT MIAMI, ACGME 1801100005 - a different program, at a different hospital, in a different HCA division, being researched by a different agent - and it reached me via an aggregator page rather than an official source. Importing it would have been exactly the cross-program contamination the contract warns about. It is refused and logged. WHAT I EXPLICITLY REFUSED TO COUNT: I refused, in order of how tempting each was. (1) OSCEOLA COUNTY DEMOGRAPHICS - the single most tempting substitution available anywhere in Florida. Osceola County has one of the highest Puerto Rican population shares of any county in the United States, and Kissimmee sits at the centre of the largest mainland Puerto Rican community. A Spanish-speaking applicant would obviously encounter Spanish-speaking patients here. That is a fact about a county, not a fact about a residency curriculum, and governance law 5 forbids treating it as evidence. Not counted, in any strength rating, in any domain. (2) THE HOSPITAL WEBSITE'S SPANISH INFRASTRUCTURE - hcafloridahealthcare.com and hcafloridaphysicians.com both ship an English/Espanol language toggle and a 'physicianReferralPhoneNumberSpanish' of (855) 790-3627, and the pages carry a Spanish-language version of HCA's physician-referral disclaimer. This is HCA corporate template applied identically across dozens of hospitals in multiple states; it is marketing localisation, not a clinical service and not a residency curriculum. Refused under contamination guard 4. (3) HCA'S NONDISCRIMINATION NOTICE - present in the footer of every HCA page and containing the boilerplate language-assistance provisions federal law requires. Institution-wide compliance text is not an interpreter policy tied to this residency. Refused. (4) FACULTY AND CO-AUTHOR SURNAMES - the program's faculty page includes Fernando Gonzalez-Portillo, MD, and its Scholarly Commons collection includes co-authors such as Giovanni F. Ramirez and Paola Colon Fugueroa. Governance law 4 forbids inferring language, nationality or ethnicity from a name, so none of these was counted as evidence of Spanish capability, and 'spanish_documented' is null rather than true for every faculty member. (5) THE MIAMI HCA PROGRAM'S MEDICAL SPANISH CLAIM - see the raw finding; a different program, via an aggregator. Refused. (6) GENERIC DIVERSITY LANGUAGE - the program's mission statement says its faculty are committed to 'expanding residents' perspectives to be inclusive of cultures, values and ideals'. That is a values statement with no named clinical mechanism and is not Spanish-language or Latino-community evidence. Refused. WHAT WOULD HAVE COUNTED AND WAS ABSENT: a named Spanish-language clinic or service line, a formal Medical Spanish curriculum or elective, a bilingual track or bilingual-resident designation, an interpreter policy written into this residency's own materials, or a documented partnership with a named Latino community organisation or federally qualified health centre.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - no formal Medical Spanish curriculum, Spanish-language clinical service, bilingual track or residency-specific interpreter policy is published for this residency, and its own July 2026 FREIDA survey lists no curriculum items at all.

value.two_program_question: RESOLVED - two separate accreditations, complements, NRMP codes, PDs and rosters; operationally interlocked via a shared stroke service and shared GME office

summary: ACGME 1801100156 is the Adult Neurology residency at Larkin Community Hospital's South Miami Campus, a 4-year community-based categorical program with NRMP code 1481180C0 and 16 approved positions. It is a genuinely separate program from Larkin's Palm Springs Campus neurology residency (ACGME 1801100158, NRMP 2238180C0, Hialeah) - separate program directors, complements, rosters and NRMP codes - though the two share a GME office and a stroke service.
raw_finding:
ESTABLISHED FINDING: ACGME 1801100156 and ACGME 1801100158 are TWO SEPARATE, SEPARATELY ACCREDITED Adult Neurology residency programs, each with its own approved complement, its own NRMP program code, and its own program director. They are NOT one department presented under two accreditations, although they are operationally interlocked. Nine independent lines of evidence:
(1) TWO LIVE NRMP CODES PUBLISHED SIDE BY SIDE, each cross-walked by NRMP itself to a distinct ACGME ID. NRMP's Main Residency Match program directory shows 'Neurology / Larkin Community Hospital-FL / NRMP CODE 1481180C0 / ACGME CODE 1801100156 / Program Status Active / The program track is participating in the Match / Program Director Wilson Cueva / 7031 SW 62nd Ave., South Miami, Florida 33143 / Institution Code 1481'. Separately, NRMP shows 'Neurology / Larkin Comm Hosp Palm Springs Campus-FL / NRMP CODE 2238180C0 / ACGME CODE 1801100158 / Program Director Kester Nedd / 1475 W 49th Place, Hialeah, Florida 33012'. Different NRMP INSTITUTION codes (1481 vs 2238), not merely different program codes. This is the same class of decisive evidence that resolved the two UT Austin programs in Texas.
(2) TWO SEPARATE FREIDA PROGRAM NODES, each carrying its own independently completed 2026 AMA survey record of 210 fields, recovered from the server-rendered Angular 'ng-state' payload. The two surveys were RECEIVED ON DIFFERENT DATES - 1801100156 on 2026-06-16, 1801100158 on 2026-07-21 - and differ in roughly forty substantive fields, which is only possible if two different program administrations completed them. Examples of divergence: moonlighting allowed true vs false; night float PGY-1 true vs false; paid leave 20 days vs 0; disability benefit 'Institution & Resident Share Cost' vs 'Not Available'; chair letter required true vs false; PGY-1 salary $47,500 vs not reported; years-since-graduation not-applicable true (no cap) vs a 5-year cap; DO percentage 0.0 vs 6.2; IMG percentage 100.0 vs 93.8; interviews conducted 60 vs 40.
(3) SEPARATE PROGRAM DIRECTORS. 1801100156: Wilson C. Cueva, MD (FREIDA field_program_director first/last name 'Wilson' 'Cueva', degree MD; corroborated by NRMP and by the program's own page, which he signs 'Wilson Cueva, M.D., Program Director, Adult Neurology Residency Program, Larkin Community Hospital, South Miami Campus'). 1801100158: Kester Jimmy Nedd, DO (FREIDA degree DO; corroborated by NRMP and the PSC page, 'Kester Nedd, D.O.').
(4) SEPARATE COORDINATORS AND SEPARATE COORDINATOR MAILBOXES. 156: Angelica Hassett, ahassett@larkinhospital.com, and the program page gives neurcoordlch@larkinhospital.com ('lch' = Larkin Community Hospital). 158: Gissel Arregui, garregui@larkinhospital.com, PD contact neurcoordpsc@larkinhospital.com ('psc' = Palm Springs Campus); the PSC page names coordinator Christopher Rivera. The deliberate lch/psc mailbox split is itself institutional evidence of two administratively distinct programs.
(5) SEPARATE APPROVED COMPLEMENTS THAT DO NOT DOUBLE-COUNT. Each program independently reports field_program_size [4,4,4,4] and field_total_positions 16, and each program's own web page states '4' positions at each of PGY-1 through PGY-4. Larkin Health System therefore has 32 approved adult neurology positions across two programs, not 16 counted twice.
(6) SEPARATE AND LARGELY DISJOINT PARTICIPATING-INSTITUTION SETS in FREIDA. 156: Larkin Community Hospital, Nicklaus Children's Hospital, North Shore Hospital Inpatient, Sunrise Medical Group, Carrie Landess MD-Neurology Clinic, Palm Beach Neuroscience Institute, South Florida School of Sleep Medicine, Larkin Imaging Diagnostic Center. 158: Larkin Community Hospital Palm Springs Campus, Advanced Neuroscience Network Physicians-Hialeah, Kidz Pediatric Multispecialty Center, Florida Sleep and Neuro Diagnostic Services, Larkin Community Hospital, Palmetto General Hospital, North Shore Hospital Inpatient, West Gables Rehabilitation Hospital, Design Neuroscience Center, Matthew Kay MD PA. Only 'Larkin Community Hospital' and 'North Shore Hospital Inpatient' appear in both.
(7) SEPARATE, NON-SHARED WEB PAGE SETS. 156 has neurology-home-page, our-curriculum-neurology, our-faculty-neurology, our-residents-neurology, our-alumni-neurology, application-process-neurology. 158 has the parallel '-psc' pages. Most decisively, the two programs publish SEPARATE RESIDENT ROSTERS (our-residents-neurology vs our-residents-neurology-psc) - different named people.
(8) LARKIN'S OWN ACGME PROGRAM LIST shows Neurology TWICE, once under 'South Miami Campus' (21 programs) linking to neurology-home-page, and once under 'Palm Springs Campus' (19 programs) linking to neurology-home-psc.
(9) DIFFERENT PUBLISHED ELIGIBILITY RULES, which would be impossible for a single program: 156 reports no cap on years since graduation, 158 reports a 5-year cap plus a clinical-experience expectation.

WHAT REMAINS UNRESOLVED / THE GENUINE INTERLOCK, preserved rather than flattened: the two programs are not independent silos. (a) Dr. Cueva, the PD of 1801100156, simultaneously serves as 'Medical Director, Comprehensive Stroke Care Program, Larkin Community Hospital, Palm Springs Campus' - i.e. one senior neurologist holds leadership in both campuses' neurology enterprises. (b) The South Miami program's own curriculum page lists 'Larkin Community Hospital Palm Springs - Hialeah Campus (Stroke and Inpatient Services)' as a participating TEACHING HOSPITAL, so residents of 1801100156 rotate at the 1801100158 campus for stroke. (c) Both programs sit under one GME office, one web domain, and one mailing address (7000 SW 62nd Avenue, South Miami) which appears in the footer of BOTH campuses' pages. (d) ACGME's own public accreditation database is CAPTCHA-gated and was not accessed, so the claim of two separate ACCREDITATIONS rests on NRMP's published ACGME cross-walk plus two distinct FREIDA program records - authoritative, but not ACGME's own database. value.determination: No published rule requires a Step 2 CK result before application, initial review, interview invitation, or ranking. Three independent published facts establish this. First, the program's own application-process page lists among required materials 'USMLE Step 2 or COMLEX Level 2 score (if available)' - the parenthetical 'if available' is an explicit statement that a missing Step 2 result does not block the application. Second, FREIDA's 2026 survey for this program (received 2026-06-16) reports field_usmle_step2_req_int = false and field_usmle_step_2_required = false, i.e. Step 2 is not flagged as required for interview. Third, the published calendar leaves room regardless: the program page states 'Applications are reviewed starting in October, with interviews typically held on Fridays in November, December, and January', and the FREIDA survey gives a current-year interview period of 2026-11-01 to 2026-12-31. Alejandra's result is expected mid-October 2026, which lands before interviews begin under either published calendar, and only marginally after review opens. SEPARATELY AND IMPORTANTLY: this does NOT mean Step 2 CK is unnecessary. The same 2026 FREIDA survey flags field_usmle_us_md_pass_ck = true and field_usmle_img_pass_ck = true, i.e. a PASSED Step 2 CK is reported as a requirement - but the timing fields place that requirement after the review/interview stage, most consistently with 'before ranking or before starting'. The requirement and its timing are treated as two separate variables, exactly as instructed. No minimum Step 2 score is published by any source, so score-compatibility cannot be assessed and is not inferred from any timing rule.
value.exact_paraphrase: 'USMLE Step 1 or COMLEX Level 1 score; USMLE Step 2 or COMLEX Level 2 score (if available)' and 'Applications are reviewed starting in October, with interviews typically held on Fridays in November, December, and January.'
value.barrier_reasoning: The only published timing gates are 'review starts in October' and 'interviews in November, December and January' (FREIDA: interview period 2026-11-01 to 2026-12-31). A mid-October 2026 Step 2 CK result arrives before any interview date and before ranking. The program explicitly accepts an application without a Step 2 score ('if available'), so the brief overlap with the opening of file review in October is not a published barrier. RESIDUAL RISK, stated plainly and not converted into a 'No': because review opens in October, a file reaching the program in late September without a Step 2 score may be read once before the score posts; no published rule prevents a later re-read, and none promises one.

summary: No published rule requires a Step 2 CK result before application, initial review, interview or ranking - the program asks for the score only 'if available' and interviews run November to January. Alejandra's mid-October 2026 result should arrive before interviews.

summary: FREIDA reports no cap on years since medical school graduation, and the registry agrees. But the program's own page imposes a different, real screen: applicants more than one year past graduation must already have passed Step 3 or COMLEX Level 3. Alejandra (June 2027 graduation) is unaffected in the 2026-27 cycle.
raw_finding: FREIDA 2026 survey (received 2026-06-16): field_years_since_graduation_na = true and field_years_since_graduation = null, i.e. 'No cap on the number of years'. The registry's 'Medical School Graduation Timeline: No cap on the number of years' is CONFIRMED on this point. For contrast, the sibling program 1801100158 reports field_years_since_graduation = 5 and field_years_since_graduation_na = false - a genuine 5-year cap - which is one of the differentiators between the two Larkin programs. HOWEVER, the program's own application-process page carries a substantive graduation-linked screen that FREIDA does not capture, verbatim: 'Applicants with more than 1 year of graduation must have completed Step 3 or COMLEX-3 to be considered starting the 2026 application period'. This is not a YOG cap but it functions as a hard additional requirement past the one-year mark, and it is newly effective for the 2026 application period. FOR ALEJANDRA: expected graduation June 2027 means that in the 2026-27 ERAS cycle she applies as a senior student, zero years post-graduation, so the Step 3 rule does not engage. It WOULD engage if she were to apply in any cycle beginning more than one year after June 2027 (i.e. a reapplication in the 2028-29 cycle or later), at which point a passed Step 3 would be a precondition. Flagged as a forward-looking eligibility risk, not a current one.
source_date: FREIDA survey received 2026-06-16; program rule effective 2026 application period
conflict_notes: FREIDA and the registry both report 'no cap on years since graduation', which reads as a permissive program. The program's own page adds an uncaptured screen - a mandatory Step 3/COMLEX-3 pass for anyone more than 1 year post-graduation. These are not strictly contradictory but the FREIDA-only reading materially understates the barrier for any non-current-year graduate.

summary: IMGs need a valid ECFMG certificate to begin training (not to apply). This does not apply to Alejandra: Universidad Central del Caribe is LCME-accredited, so she is a U.S. medical graduate and needs no ECFMG certification.
raw_finding: Program's own application-process page, verbatim: 'A valid ECFMG certificate is required to begin residency training' - the requirement attaches to the START of training, not to the application, which is the applicant-friendly version of this rule. FREIDA reports visa sponsorship as 'J-1 through ECFMG', consistent with an IMG-oriented pipeline (FREIDA also reports this program's residents as 100.0% IMG). ALEJANDRA-SPECIFIC FLAG, exactly the ambiguity the contract asks to surface: Larkin's published eligibility framing describes candidates as graduates of medical schools 'accredited in the U.S. or Canada' or else holders of a valid ECFMG certificate, WITHOUT naming Puerto Rico. Universidad Central del Caribe is LCME-accredited and is therefore a United States MD school, so Alejandra falls in the first category and needs no ECFMG certificate. But because the language does not name Puerto Rico explicitly, an application screener unfamiliar with UCC's LCME status could mis-sort her into the IMG bucket and look for an ECFMG certificate she has no reason to hold. This is a real, actionable finding: she should be prepared to state UCC's LCME accreditation explicitly. No source I opened states or implies that this program treats Puerto Rico schools as international.

value.dominant_pipeline: Ecuador - 9 of 16 current residents trained at Ecuadorian medical schools

summary: Every current resident's medical school is published, and all 16 trained outside the United States. Nine of the 16 are graduates of Ecuadorian medical schools, making this an unusually concentrated Ecuadorian and broader Latin American pipeline. No resident attended a U.S., Puerto Rican, or offshore for-profit Caribbean school.
raw_finding:
Schools exactly as published: Universidad de Guayaquil (Proano; Fiallos) - Ecuador; Universidad San Francisco de Quito (Camacho-Olalla) - Ecuador; Kathmandu Medical College (Agrawal) - Nepal; Semmelweis University (Ambrus) - Hungary; Universidad Tecnica de Manabi (Zambrano) - Ecuador; Universidad del Zulia (Soto) - Venezuela; Universidad Central del Ecuador (Cueva) - Ecuador; Universidad de Especialidades Espiritu Santo (Toral) - Ecuador; Anugrah Narain Magadh Medical College (Jaiswal) - India; Universidad Catolica de Santiago de Guayaquil (Mendoza Loor; Sarmiento) - Ecuador; Universidad de Ciencias Medicas de La Habana (Zamora) - Cuba; KIST Medical College (Choradia) - Nepal; Universidad Laica Eloy Alvaro de Manabi (Lopez) - Ecuador; Universidad de los Andes (Suleiman) - country NOT disambiguated by the page.
CLASSIFICATION REASONING, stated because two entries could be mishandled. (1) Universidad de Ciencias Medicas de La Habana is a Cuban national/state medical university. Despite sitting in the Caribbean Sea it is NOT an 'offshore for-profit Caribbean school' in the sense this dossier uses - that bucket denotes institutions such as Ross, St George's, AUC, Saba, Texila and Windsor, which recruit primarily North American students. Havana is classified OTHER_IMG, and the caribbean bucket is therefore zero. Classification is a property of the institution, never of the person. (2) 'Universidad de los Andes' is a name shared by universities in Venezuela (Merida), Colombia (Bogota) and Chile; the page does not say which, so the country is recorded as UNKNOWN while the classification remains OTHER_IMG in all three readings.
No nationality, ethnicity or immigration status has been inferred from any resident's name, and none is reported. FREIDA's 2026 figures corroborate the roster exactly: field_pct_img 100.0, field_pct_usmd 0.0, field_pct_do 0.0.
STRATEGICALLY SIGNIFICANT SHIFT: the alumni page shows the program was DO-heavy as recently as 2020-2022 (Rizk, Tamton, Ruxmohan, Coppola, Walter, Gould, Bui, Liu, Dyess, Saggio all carry D.O.), whereas the current 16-resident roster contains zero DOs and zero U.S. graduates of any kind. The recruitment pipeline has turned over completely within about five years toward international, predominantly Ecuadorian, MD graduates. Alejandra, as a U.S. MD from an LCME-accredited Puerto Rico school, would be a compositional outlier in the current cohort.

The program's 'Our Faculty-Neurology' page publishes 22 named individuals under the heading 'CURRENT DEPARTMENT MEMBERS', nearly all with medical school, residency and fellowship histories. The full structured list is in the core_faculty.faculty[] array. This is materially more disclosure than most community programs provide.
WHY THIS IS PARTIALLY_VERIFIED RATHER THAN VERIFIED: the page's heading is 'CURRENT DEPARTMENT MEMBERS', not 'core faculty', and no individual is labelled with an ACGME core-faculty designation. The list also mixes the neurology department proper with the external preceptors of required rotations (for example Dr Isaacson in Boca Raton, Dr Kay in Aventura, Dr Malik in Fort Lauderdale) and with other Larkin program directors who cover PGY-1 off-service months (Dr Gerardo Ferrer, psychiatry; Dr Michel, internal medicine; Dr Hernandez, infectious disease). The 2026 FREIDA survey still carries field_total_physician = 0, field_total_non_physician = 0, field_ratio_ft_faculty = '0.00', field_part_time_paid_physicians = 0. These are FREIDA NULL SENTINELS - the program left the faculty-count questions unanswered - and must not be read as a program with no faculty, against a published roster of 22 named physicians. SUBSPECIALTY CONCENTRATION: the department's centre of gravity is vascular neurology and neurocritical care - Cueva (neurocritical care, interventional neuroradiology), Sanchez (vascular), Labrada (vascular + neurocritical care) - which aligns with the graduate placement record. value.dedicated_clinic: Yes, but EXTERNAL to Larkin: the Parkinson's Disease and Movement Disorders Center of Boca Raton (Dr Isaacson) and South Miami Neurology (Dr Starosta-Rubinstein). Larkin itself operates a 'Neuroscience Center' and a 'Center for Advanced Neurology' but publishes no in-house movement disorders clinic.
value.resident_elective: Not an elective - REQUIRED. Six movement-disorders-inclusive months are built into the required curriculum: '1 Month - Movement Disorders' plus '1 Month - Cognitive and Movement Disorders' in each of PGY-2, PGY-3 and PGY-4.
value.research: The Boca Raton centre is described by the program as 'a nationally recognized, non-university-based academic center and leading clinical research institution that provides community access to Phase II and Phase III FDA-regulated clinical trials focused on improving symptoms and slowing disease progression in Parkinson's disease.' Dr Isaacson 'has led extensive clinical research and drug development programs, authored hundreds of publications' and promotes education 'through the Parkinson's Research & Education Foundation'.
value.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: These diverge sharply and the distinction is the whole story of this domain. RESIDENT EXPOSURE IS STRONG and, unusually, mandatory: six named movement-disorders months across PGY-2 to PGY-4 in a 48-month curriculum, at a nationally active Parkinson's trial centre, plus hands-on procedural exposure in a separate continuity clinic that includes 'monthly deep brain stimulation (DBS) programming' and 'botulinum toxin injections'. Required DBS programming exposure is rare at community programs and is the single most concrete movement-disorders asset here. INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY IS LIMITED: Larkin Community Hospital itself runs no movement disorders clinic, no movement disorders fellowship and no movement disorders research program. Every one of those months is delivered at an external private practice, and the Isaacson centre is in BOCA RATON - roughly 45 to 50 miles north of the South Miami primary site, which is a real commuting burden a student should price in. OUTCOME COUNTERWEIGHT, and it matters: across 25 published graduates from 2020 to 2026, ZERO entered a movement disorders fellowship. Placements went overwhelmingly to vascular neurology and neurocritical care. So the program reliably delivers movement disorders EXPOSURE but has no track record of converting it into movement disorders CAREERS. Strength is rated MODERATE rather than STRONG for that reason: the required-rotation structure is strong, the owning institution's own capability and the outcome record are not.

raw_finding:
REQUIRED ROTATION: exactly one month, PGY-2, verbatim '1 Month - Multiple Sclerosis'. No further required MS month appears in PGY-3 or PGY-4.
SITE, verbatim from the curriculum page: 'Boca Raton Multiple Sclerosis Center - Brian Steingo, M.D. - (Multiple Sclerosis and Demyelinating Disorders). Location: Boca Raton, FL. The Boca Raton Multiple Sclerosis Center, led by neurologist and MS specialist Brian Steingo, MD, offers Neurology residents comprehensive outpatient training in the evaluation and management of multiple sclerosis and related demyelinating and neuroinflammatory disorders. Through this clinical neuroimmunology rotation, residents develop core competencies in the diagnosis and classification of CNS demyelinating diseases, formulation of differential diagnoses, and appropriate diagnostic workup. Further advancing their skills by initiating and monitoring immunomodulatory therapies, recognizing treatment-related complications, and managing the long-term symptoms of MS and chronic neurologic disease.'
FACULTY, verbatim from the program's faculty page: 'Brian Steingo, MD, is the Medical Director of the Boca Raton Multiple Sclerosis Center and a nationally recognized neurologist specializing in multiple sclerosis and related neurologic disorders... Dr. Steingo is an active member of the American Academy of Neurology, as well as the Broward County and Florida medical associations, and serves as Chairman of the Professional Advisory Committee for the South Florida Chapter of the National Multiple Sclerosis Society. He has been extensively involved in clinical research, including numerous clinical trials evaluating biologic therapies for multiple sclerosis.' He earned his degree at the University of the Witwatersrand, Johannesburg, and 'served as Chief Neurology Resident at Baylor College of Medicine in Houston, Texas'.
*** FORMAL DESIGNATION - CLAIM SEARCHED AND DELIBERATELY NOT MADE. *** This is the highest-consequence judgement in the dossier and the contract's explicit warning case. Web search results asserted that the Boca Raton MS office with Brian Steingo, MD 'is designated as Partners in MS Care' by the National Multiple Sclerosis Society. I did NOT accept this. Search snippets are discovery aids, never evidence. I fetched the National MS Society's own 'Partners in MS Care' page at nationalmssociety.org to verify against the AWARDING BODY's own naming, and that page returned truncated content and did NOT name the Boca Raton Multiple Sclerosis Center, Dr Steingo, or any provider list I could read. I therefore could not open any NMSS page stating the designation in those words, and per the contract the designation is NOT reported. formal_designation is null. What IS verifiable, because I opened the page that says it, is the narrower and different fact that Dr Steingo personally chairs the Professional Advisory Committee of the NMSS South Florida Chapter - a volunteer committee role held by an individual, NOT an institutional 'Partners in MS Care' or 'Center for Comprehensive MS Care' designation held by a clinic, and emphatically not a designation held by Larkin Community Hospital or by this residency. Conflating the two would reproduce exactly the Texas fabrication that a second reader caught.
NO IN-HOUSE FELLOWSHIP: no MS or neuroimmunology fellowship exists at Larkin; its ACGME program list contains no neurology subspecialty fellowship. I did not infer one from Dr Steingo's specialty.
OUTCOME EVIDENCE: one graduate of 25 published, Robert Coppola, DO (class of 2021), entered a 'Neuroimmunology Fellowship at Jackson Memorial Hospital, University of Miami'. This is a real, published pathway outcome - a single instance in seven graduating classes.
conflict_notes: Search snippets assert an NMSS 'Partners in MS Care' designation for the Boca Raton MS office; the National MS Society's own Partners in MS Care page, when fetched, returned truncated content and did not name the centre or Dr Steingo. The designation is therefore UNVERIFIED and is not reported. Only Dr Steingo's personal NMSS chapter committee chairmanship, which appears verbatim on a page I opened, is stated.

raw_finding:
IN-HOUSE, established from Larkin's own ACGME-accredited programs list, which enumerates 21 South Miami Campus programs and 19 Palm Springs Campus programs. NO neurology subspecialty fellowship appears on either list. The relevant multidisciplinary fellowships are Pain Medicine (Multidisciplinary) and Hospice and Palliative Medicine (Multidisciplinary) at South Miami, and Sleep Medicine (Multidisciplinary) at Palm Springs. Corroboration that Pain Medicine is genuinely operating and locally led: Dr Joseph E. Mouhanna's faculty bio states he 'serves as Program Director for Pain Medicine Fellowship at Larkin Community Hospital'.
PROOF OF REAL RESIDENT ACCESS, not merely institutional adjacency: the alumni page shows Jonathan Gomez, MD, class of 2024 and Chief Resident, went to an 'Interventional Spine & Pain Management Fellowship at Larkin Community Hospital, Miami, FL'. A graduate of this residency actually entered a Larkin fellowship, which is stronger evidence of access than a program list alone. The accreditation status of the 'Interventional Spine & Pain Management Fellowship' as named on the alumni page is not published and is recorded as unknown; Larkin's ACGME list names 'Pain Medicine (Multidisciplinary)', which may or may not be the same programme under a different label. Not resolved, not blurred.
AFFILIATED AND EXPLICITLY NOT IN-HOUSE: Palmetto General Hospital vascular neurology (a separate institution, itself ACGME 1801100160 for neurology; two Larkin graduates placed there), Jackson Memorial/University of Miami neuroimmunology, and Nicklaus Children's clinical neurophysiology. The department contains three vascular neurologists, a movement disorders specialist, an MS specialist and two neurophysiologists, and none of that was permitted to imply a corresponding fellowship. Applying the Texas lesson: no fellowship is reported as existing, in development, or aspirational without a source, and none was found. fellows_in_post is null for every entry because no fellow counts are published.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete · Larkin sponsors no neurology subspecialty fellowship. Multidisciplinary Pain Medicine, Hospice and Palliative Medicine and Sleep Medicine fellowships exist in-house, but no fellow counts are published for any of them.

WHY THIS READS AS COMPLETE COHORTS RATHER THAN SELECTED EXAMPLES - the distinction the contract demands. The class sizes (4, 3, 4, 4, 4, 4, 2) match the program's uneven cohort pattern rather than a curated highlight reel, they include unglamorous outcomes that a marketing page would omit ('General Neurology at Miami, FL' three times, 'Neurology Specialist in Fort Myers'), and most decisively the 2026 class of four is exactly the four residents who appear as PGY-4s in the 2026-06-09 Wayback snapshot of the resident roster, with matching fellowship destinations. SUBSPECIALTY SIGNAL RELEVANT TO ALEJANDRA: the outcome record is heavily weighted to vascular neurology and neurocritical care (12 of 19 fellowships), matching the department's faculty concentration. Movement disorders - her stated interest - accounts for ZERO of 25 outcomes despite six required movement-disorders months. MS/neuroimmunology accounts for exactly one. A student whose goal is a movement disorders fellowship would be doing something this program has not yet done.
A DEMOGRAPHIC SHIFT VISIBLE IN THE OUTCOMES: the 2020-2022 classes are largely D.O. graduates while the current roster has no DOs at all, confirming the pipeline turnover noted in Domain 12.

summary: The program does not publish an ABPN board pass rate, though it does confirm graduates are eligible for ABPN certification and reports internally tracking board pass rates as a program-evaluation measure.

No numeric board certification pass rate was found. Searched: the program's own neurology home page, curriculum page, alumni page and application-process page; Larkin's GME-level pages; the full 210-field FREIDA 2026 survey record; and targeted web search for a Larkin neurology ABPN pass rate, which returned only generic national ABPN statistics and no program-level figure.

The registry's 'Board Certification Pass Rate Evaluation: Yes' is CONFIRMED but is a statement that the metric is tracked internally, NOT a published pass rate. The registry field is easily misread as an outcome and is flagged as a semantic mismatch. ABPN does not publish program-level pass rates publicly. This is NOT_PUBLIC, not NOT_FOUND, and must not be read as a poor result.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete · The program does not publish an ABPN board certification pass rate. It confirms graduates are eligible for ABPN certification and reports tracking pass rates internally, but no figure is public and ABPN does not release program-level rates.

All figures from the FREIDA 2026 survey received 2026-06-16, field_graduate_year_statistics: year 1 salary 47500 with 20 paid vacation days; year 2 50000/20; year 3 51750/20; year 4 53500/20; and the record also carries year 5 at 55250/20 and year 6 at 57000 - template artefacts for a 4-year program, noted so they are not mistaken for a 6-year track. field_first_year_salary = 47500 confirms PGY-1.
REGISTRY SUPERSEDED ON EVERY SALARY FIELD: registry 47250/49500/51000/52500 versus current 47500/50000/51750/53500. The registry values are one cycle stale, exactly the defect pattern the contract predicts. Increases of roughly 0.5 to 1.9 percent.
CONTEXT A STUDENT NEEDS: $47,500 for PGY-1 is materially below typical U.S. PGY-1 neurology stipends, and South Miami is a high-cost housing market. The housing stipend and free parking (field_program_offers_2021 = ['Housing stipend', 'Free parking']) partially offset this and are worth asking about in dollar terms, since no amount is published.
DIRECT REGISTRY CONTRADICTION ON WHO PAYS: the registry records 'Salary Paid By: Non-profit institution'. The 2026 survey field is field_salary_paid_nonprofit = 'No'. The program itself answers that the salary is NOT paid by a non-profit institution, which is consistent with Larkin Community Hospital's for-profit ownership. The registry value is contradicted by the program's own newer answer.
BENEFITS DIVERGE FROM THE SIBLING PROGRAM and this is identity evidence as well as benefits data: 156 reports dental and disability as 'Institution & Resident Share Cost' and group life as 'Not Available', while 158 reports dental as 'Available, Not Paid By Institution', disability as 'Not Available' and group life as 'Available, Not Paid By Institution'. 156 also reports 20 paid leave days against 158's 0, and permits moonlighting where 158 does not. DATA-QUALITY ODDITY FLAGGED, NOT LAUNDERED: field_avg_hours_on_duty_y1 = 40 and field_avg_24hr_off_duty_y1 = 1.00. A self-reported 40-hour average duty week for a PGY-1 neurology resident is implausibly low and should be treated as an unreliable self-report rather than a program feature. The registry's 'Average Work Hours: 40 hours/week' inherits the same doubtful value. field_night_float and field_night_float_y1 are both true, and field_call_schedule is ['N/A','N/A','N/A','N/A'] - i.e. the call structure is simply not disclosed, which the registry rendered as 'Year 1: N/A; Year 2: N/A...'.
No Larkin GME-level benefits or stipend page exists; the institution-wide 'Current Residents' and 'Program Information' pages were checked and carry only Orthopaedics content, so FREIDA is the only source and no official HR benefits document was located.

summary: A four-year categorical curriculum with unusually specific subspecialty months - six movement-disorders months, one MS month, four EEG/epilepsy months, four EMG/NCS months, and required sleep, pain and neuro-ophthalmology blocks - delivered across five teaching hospitals and nine named private practices. There is no research rotation and no research track.
raw_finding:
The full month-by-month required rotation grid is quoted verbatim in `value` from the program's own curriculum page. Four hours of didactics per week (FREIDA field_avg_hrs_lecture_conf_y1 = 4), plus case reviews, Grand Rounds, journal club and in-service review; the curriculum page states 'Protected time is built into the curriculum for didactics, research, and academic development'.
STRUCTURAL OBSERVATIONS. The subspecialty exposure is front-loaded from PGY-2 and then REPEATED identically in PGY-3 and PGY-4 (the same EEG/epilepsy, EMG/NCS, Cognitive-and-Movement, and Movement Disorders months recur each year), which gives genuine longitudinal depth in those areas - directly relevant to Alejandra's stated longitudinal-neurology interest. Five elective months total (one in PGY-3, three in PGY-4, plus the PGY-3 elective). Three months of Pediatric Neurology in PGY-3 - this is an ADULT program's required pediatric ROTATION at Nicklaus Children's Hospital, which is legitimate adult-curriculum data; no Child Neurology program material was used anywhere in this dossier.
TEACHING SITES, with quotable institutional characterisations. Larkin South Miami (primary): 'It has been designated an "Area of Critical Need" by both the Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) and the Florida Department of Health', and offers 'the Neuroscience Center, the Center for Advanced Neurology, the Cancer Center, and seven neuroimaging centers located throughout Miami-Dade County'. Larkin Palm Springs - Hialeah: 'a 247-bed statutory teaching hospital... and an ACHC-accredited Comprehensive Stroke Center and Primary Stroke Center' providing 'intravenous thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy' - note ACHC, not Joint Commission, as the accreditor. HCA Florida Kendall Hospital: 'a 447-bed, full-service tertiary-care statutory teaching hospital and an American College of Surgeons-certified Level I Trauma Center', 'a DNV-accredited Comprehensive Stroke Receiving Facility and Joint Commission certified Stroke Center', within 'HCA East Florida's GME consortium'. Wien Center: 'a leading participant in NIH-funded research initiatives, including Florida's Alzheimer's Disease Research Center'.
SITE-LIST CONFLICT WITH FREIDA - a real currency finding. The curriculum page's five teaching hospitals include HCA Florida Kendall Hospital and the Wien Center at Mount Sinai, NEITHER of which appears in FREIDA's participating-institution list for this program. Conversely FREIDA lists North Shore Hospital Inpatient, Sunrise Medical Group, Palm Beach Neuroscience Institute, South Florida School of Sleep Medicine and Larkin Imaging Diagnostic Center, none of which appear on the current curriculum page. The rotation-site network has clearly been reorganised and the program's own website is the newer record. A student should not rely on FREIDA's site list for this program.
RESEARCH IS A GENUINE WEAKNESS: FREIDA field_research_rotation = 'Not available' and field_research_rotation_duration = 0, confirming the registry's 'Research Rotation: Not available' and 'Research Track: No'. The curriculum page's claim of protected time for 'research and academic development' and Larkin's institutional Department of Research and Academic Affairs sit in tension with FREIDA's flat 'not available'; both are recorded. For a candidate with scholarly ambitions in movement disorders this is the clearest structural gap in the program.
Training setting: 80 percent hospital outpatient, 20 percent non-hospital ambulatory (field_training_outpatient_clinic 80, field_train_ambulatory_nonhospit 20) - confirming the registry. Health systems leadership curriculum and off-campus electives are offered; global health, integrative medicine, complementary medicine, healthcare economics, advanced-degree training and Step 3 support are all reported as not offered. field_special_tracks = ['Other'] with no elaboration, so no named track is established.
conflict_notes: Teaching-site lists disagree: the curriculum page names HCA Florida Kendall Hospital and the Wien Center, which FREIDA omits; FREIDA names North Shore, Sunrise Medical Group, Palm Beach Neuroscience Institute, South Florida School of Sleep Medicine and Larkin Imaging, which the curriculum page omits. Also the curriculum page advertises protected research time while FREIDA reports the research rotation as 'Not available'.

But the program publishes NO formal Medical Spanish curriculum - it answers 'no' to that question in its own 2026 AMA survey - no named Spanish-language clinical service, and no interpreter policy.
value.raw_finding:
WHAT COUNTS, all from pages I opened. (1) DOCUMENTED FACULTY SPANISH, verbatim from the program's own 'Our Faculty-Neurology' page: 'Dr. Lalama is bilingual and fluent in both English and Spanish.' and 'Dr. Starosta Rubinstein is fluent in Spanish and committed to delivering comprehensive, patient-centered neurologic care across the lifespan.' This is not incidental biography - both men precept REQUIRED rotations for this residency. raw_finding:
SEARCHED THOROUGHLY: the full current resident roster (16 named residents, every medical school published), the complete 22-member faculty page with training histories, the alumni page (25 graduates, 2020-2026), the leadership records in FREIDA and NRMP, and targeted web search for Larkin plus each of the four Puerto Rico medical schools.
RESIDENT LEVEL - ZERO. None of the 16 current residents attended Universidad Central del Caribe, Ponce Health Sciences University, University of Puerto Rico or San Juan Bautista School of Medicine. Their schools are in Ecuador (9), Nepal (2), Venezuela (1), Cuba (1), Hungary (1), India (1) and one ambiguous 'Universidad de los Andes'. So ucc_residents = 0 and puerto_rico_school_residents = 0, and both are recorded as OVERLAY counts that are NOT added into the five composition buckets. Despite the ticket's reasonable expectation that Larkin's large international and Caribbean-trained applicant pool might yield Puerto Rico representation, the current pipeline is Ecuadorian and South Asian, not Puerto Rican.
FACULTY LEVEL - ONE, AND IT IS THE SINGLE MOST USEFUL FINDING IN THIS DOMAIN. Verbatim from the program's own faculty page: 'Dr. Carrie Landess is a board-certified neurologist specializing in the diagnosis and treatment of disorders of the nervous system. She earned her medical degree from Universidad Central del Caribe and completed neurology residency training at SUNY Downstate Medical Center, followed by advanced fellowship training in neurophysiology and neuromuscular disease at Vanderbilt University. Dr. Landess has extensive clinical experience managing a wide range of neurologic conditions, including migraine, epilepsy, multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease, and neuromuscular disorders.' She is a UCC graduate on this program's faculty - Alejandra's own school. Critically she is not decorative: the curriculum page makes her North Miami practice a required continuity-clinic rotation, and FREIDA independently lists 'Carrie Landess MD-Neurology Clinic' as a participating institution for ACGME 1801100156. Her clinical range also happens to cover both of Alejandra's subspecialty interests, MS and Parkinson's disease.
CLASSIFICATION DISCIPLINE, stated explicitly because getting it wrong would misclassify Alejandra herself: Universidad Central del Caribe is LCME-accredited and is therefore a UNITED STATES MD school. Dr Landess is a US_MD graduate, NOT 'CARIBBEAN' and NOT 'OTHER_IMG'. The same applies to Ponce, UPR and San Juan Bautista. The 'CARIBBEAN' bucket in this dossier denotes offshore for-profit schools only - and two faculty members do fall in that different category by institution: Dr Pamela Youssef (St George's University School of Medicine, Grenada) and Dr Hector Lalama (American University of the Caribbean School of Medicine). Those are institutional facts about schools, not judgements about people, and they are entirely distinct from Puerto Rico's LCME schools despite the shared geography.
ALUMNI LEVEL - NOT PUBLIC. The alumni page gives each graduate's name, class year and fellowship destination but NOT their medical school, so Puerto Rico representation among the 25 published graduates cannot be determined. The Wayback snapshot of the resident roster did allow recovery of the 2026 class's schools (Universidad Catolica de Santiago de Guayaquil, Universidad de Especialidades Espiritu Santo, Cairo University, Pontificia Universidad Catolica del Ecuador - none in Puerto Rico), but earlier classes' schools are not recoverable from published pages.
NO IDENTITY INFERENCE FROM ANY NAME was used in this domain. Dr Landess's UCC tie rests on her bio stating her medical school, not on her surname; no one else was assessed by name.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete · No current resident attended a Puerto Rico medical school, and graduates' medical schools are not published so alumni-level Puerto Rico representation cannot be assessed. One core faculty member, Dr Carrie Landess, is a Universidad Central del Caribe graduate.

summary: The dossier rests on the program's own six neurology pages, a FREIDA survey one full cycle newer than the registry snapshot, and NRMP's program directory. Roster currency was proven rather than assumed via an Internet Archive differential. The registry's listed program website is dead and ACGME's own database was not accessed because it is CAPTCHA-gated.
raw_finding:
FRESHNESS. The decisive gain was recovering the AMA's 2026 survey record from FREIDA's server-rendered '<script id="ng-state">' Angular payload - the technique the contract recommends, which worked on the first attempt for both Larkin programs and yielded a 210-field survey each. This program's survey was RECEIVED 2026-06-16, whereas the registry snapshot (release 2026-07-09) was built on the survey received 2025-07-16. The dossier therefore reflects a survey cycle the registry does not contain, which is what surfaced the flipped accepting-applications status, the four superseded salary figures, the Step-1-to-Step-2-CK requirement shift, the revised gender percentages and the newly published 2026-11-01 to 2026-12-31 interview window.
ROSTER CURRENCY PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED. Because the program's own page warns 'While our website is updated annually', staleness was tested with an Internet Archive CDX query followed by a Wayback differential against the 2026-06-09 snapshot. Every resident had advanced exactly one PGY year and the previous PGY-4 class had moved to the alumni page with matching fellowship destinations, proving a post-July-2026 update.
ACCESS BOUNDARIES RESPECTED. (a) ACGME's public accreditation search is CAPTCHA-gated and was NOT accessed and NOT bypassed; consequently the two-separate-accreditations conclusion rests on NRMP's published ACGME cross-walk plus two distinct FREIDA program records rather than on ACGME's own database, and approved complements were not independently verified against ACGME. (b) NRMP publishes no per-program historical fill or quota data publicly, and its unfilled-programs list is gated to registered users in the R3 system; that boundary was not crossed. (c) The National MS Society's Partners in MS Care page returned truncated content, preventing verification of a purported designation. (d) graduatemedicaleducation.org blocks plain automated requests via Mod_Security; this was handled by sending ordinary browser Accept/Accept-Language/Accept-Encoding headers, which is normal client behaviour and not a control bypass. No login, paywall or CAPTCHA was circumvented anywhere.
AGGREGATORS QUARANTINED. residencyadvisor.com, matcharesident.com, residencyprograms.io, imgprep.com, medresidency.com and residencymatch.ai all appeared in search results and NONE is cited as authority anywhere in this dossier. One surfaced a claim of '5 positions available' against the program's own and FREIDA's consistent figure of 4, and another supplied year-by-year fill counts; both are recorded in fabrication_traps_caught rather than relied upon.
SOURCE MIX: 10 official program/GME pages, 2 FREIDA program records (one of them the sibling program, used only for differentiation), 3 NRMP directory entries, 2 Internet Archive resources, 1 awarding-body page (attempted), and 1 dead-link verification. Unique URLs 19; unique domains 6. All 26 domains are populated and NOT_YET_RESEARCHED appears nowhere.

summary: Applications go through ERAS only, with a November 15 deadline published in the program FAQ, and interviews are conducted in person. The program publishes no ERAS program-signal guidance and requires no supplemental application.
raw_finding: DEADLINE: Program FAQ, verbatim: 'What is your residency program application deadline? The deadline for application is November 15th.' No year is attached, so it reads as a standing annual deadline. The registry's 'Application Deadline: 2025-10-15' is one cycle stale and a month early relative to the program's own published date; FREIDA's field_latest_date_current_year is null in the 2026 survey and field_univ_spec_app_date_use = true, meaning the program tells FREIDA it uses the specialty's universal application date rather than supplying its own. A student should plan to November 15 and treat mid-October as a safe internal target. SERVICE: apply page, verbatim: 'The FAU Neurology Residency Program participates in the Electronic Residency Application Service (ERAS) and National Residency Matching Program (NRMP). Our program does not accept any application materials provided outside of ERAS.' SUPPLEMENTAL: FREIDA field_nxt_supplement = false, field_supplemental_info_details null, matching the registry's 'Required Supplemental Information: No'. SIGNALING: I searched the apply page, the FAQ, the program index, the FAU GME pages and the FREIDA survey for any statement about ERAS program signals, geographic preference signals, signal tiering, or how signals are weighed. There is none. This is a genuine RESEARCHED_NOT_PUBLIC sub-finding rather than an absence of the mechanism — Neurology participates in ERAS program signaling at the specialty level, but this program publishes no guidance on how it uses signals, so a student cannot know whether a signal helps here. LETTERS: apply page requires '3-4 letters recent letters of recommendation' [sic] and FREIDA adds field_min_letters_req=2 / field_max_letters_req=4; the registry's min of 3 came from the survey_2025 cycle, where field_min_letters_req was 3. INTERVIEWS: in-person only, ~40-60 interviewed for 3 positions (FREIDA's seven-year series: 2019 50/3, 2020 50/3, 2021 70/3, 2022 70/3, 2023 70/3, 2024 55/3, 2025 50/3). No virtual option, no second look, no open house, and FREIDA's field_no_visit_event_ind=true. For a Houston-based applicant this means at least one round-trip flight to Palm Beach County to be considered.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete · The program does not publish any guidance on how it uses ERAS program signals.

And: 'Prior to joining Marcus Neuroscience Institute in 2015, Dr. Husain was in private practice as a movement disorder neurologist at the Parkinson's Disease and Movement Disorders Center of Boca Raton. She serves as an assistant professor of neurology at the Charles E. Schmidt College of Medicine at Florida Atlantic University.' Her credentials block records 'Fellowship, Neurology, 2012' and residency at Nova Southeastern University-Osteopathic Medicine, with ABPN certification in 2010. Her profile page carries a role label 'Director of Movement Disorder Neurology'. INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY. The Marcus Neuroscience Institute service page lists 'Movement disorders' among its condition areas; the program's own teaching-hospitals page says the Institute 'is staffed by a team of clinicians highly trained in all facets of the neurosciences, including stroke, movement disorders, neuro-oncology, epilepsy, memory disorders, Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis, and spinal conditions.' FORMAL DESIGNATION — SEARCHED AND NOT FOUND, and I am stating the negative precisely because the contract treats these claims as high-consequence. I searched for a Parkinson's Foundation Center of Excellence, an HDSA Center of Excellence, a CurePSP Center of Care, and any comparable movement-disorder designation attached to Boca Raton Regional Hospital or the Marcus Neuroscience Institute. No page I opened states any such designation in those words, and the Parkinson's Foundation's own Florida chapter material does not list this institution among its Centers of Excellence. I am therefore recording formal_designation = null. I note a specific collision hazard I checked and rejected: the 'Parkinson's Disease and Movement Disorders Center of Boca Raton' is a DIFFERENT, separately operated practice where Dr. Husain Wilson worked before 2015 — it shares the city name and must not be conflated with the Marcus Neuroscience Institute, and its own separate affiliations must not be transferred to FAU. NO FELLOWSHIP: FAU's GME programs page lists every fellowship FAU sponsors and none is in neurology (see domain 18). I did not infer a fellowship from Dr. Husain Wilson's fellowship training, which is exactly the inference the contract forbids.

value.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: The strongest single structural fact here is that the residency's Associate Program Director IS the MS and neuroimmunology service director at the primary teaching site. That collapses the usual gap between institutional capability and resident access: the person who runs the MS service also runs resident education. Resident exposure to MS is nonetheless ELECTIVE rather than required — 'Neuroimmunology/Multiple Sclerosis' appears on the PGY-2-4 elective list, not in the required rotation blocks, unlike Movement Disorders which is a required PGY-2 outpatient rotation. summary: MS and neuroimmunology is a real strength driven by one person: the residency's Associate Program Director is also the Director of Multiple Sclerosis and Neuroimmunology at the primary teaching site, Columbia/NMSS fellowship-trained, and fluent in Spanish. MS exposure for residents is via a named PGY-2 to PGY-4 elective rather than a required rotation, and there is no MS fellowship or formal centre designation.
raw_finding: THE DUAL ROLE, established from two independent official sources. FAU residency pages (both the faculty page and the program-administration page): 'Amy W. Laitinen, M.D. / Associate Program Director / Board Certified in Neurology / Fellowship trained in Neuroimmunology.' Baptist Health's official physician profile for Amy Wei-Hsin Laitinen, MD: 'Amy Laitinen, M.D., is a board-certified neurologist and director of multiple sclerosis and neuroimmunology at Marcus Neuroscience Institute, a part of Baptist Health. She specializes in neuroinflammatory diseases, with a focus on multiple sclerosis (MS). She is fluent in English, Spanish and Mandarin.' Baptist Health's March 28, 2025 patient-story article describes her identically: 'neurologist Amy Wei-Hsin Laitinen, M.D., director of multiple sclerosis and neuroimmunology at Marcus Neuroscience Institute at Boca Raton Regional Hospital, a part of Baptist Health', and refers to 'Dr. Laitinen's MS clinic at Marcus Neuroscience Institute'. Her credentials: 'Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons — Fellowship, Neuroimmunology, 2023'; NMSS-supported Clinical MS Fellow at Columbia; 2023 CMSC MS Mentorship Forum Scholarship. MS SERVICE INFRASTRUCTURE, from the April 5, 2024 Baptist Health / NeurologyLive piece about this Institute: Dr. Thomas Hammond, described in that article as 'an associate professor at Florida Atlantic University', says of the Institute, 'We have a new infusion center in the back of the hallway on the Institute's first ground floor of the building. Infusions are becoming a crucial part of treatment of this disease... They have everything in the same place.' The article also documents an in-house specialty pharmacy with an on-site clinical pharmacist, infusion and triage nurses, a nurse practitioner, a patient navigator, and a working relationship with the Gloria Drummond Physical Rehabilitation Institute across the street, whose physical therapists include some with MS specialty training. Baptist Health's own Marcus Neuroscience Institute service page independently confirms the infusion capability: 'Marcus Neuroscience Institute's infusion lab offers intravenous (IV) medications for a range of neurological conditions, including Alzheimer's disease, headache, multiple sclerosis and muscular dystrophy.' MIAMI-VERSUS-BOCA DISAMBIGUATION, which the contract and my tasking both flag as the critical hazard here. Every MS fact above is tied to the MARCUS NEUROSCIENCE INSTITUTE at BOCA RATON REGIONAL HOSPITAL, and each source names that institute and that hospital explicitly: the 2024 article says 'Marcus Neuroscience Institute, established at Boca Raton Regional Hospital'; the 2025 article says 'Marcus Neuroscience Institute at Boca Raton Regional Hospital'. None of it comes from Baptist Health's Miami-side neuroscience entity. Baptist Health itself draws the same line in its own words in a separate press release: 'Baptist Health's southern neuroscience program, Miami Neuroscience Institute, in conjunction with Baptist Hospital, is a Joint Commission Certified Comprehensive Stroke Center' — a different institute, a different hospital, and a different awarding body from Boca Raton's DNV certification. I have imported nothing from the Miami entity and nothing from any 'Baptist Health Neuroscience Center' page. FORMAL DESIGNATION — DELIBERATELY RECORDED AS ABSENT. I searched for a National MS Society 'Partners in MS Care' designation and for an NMSS 'Center for Comprehensive MS Care' attached to the Marcus Neuroscience Institute or Boca Raton Regional Hospital, and found no page stating either in those words. FABRICATION TRAP I DID NOT FALL INTO: the April 2024 Baptist Health article is headlined 'Diagnosing, Treating, and Preventing Multiple Sclerosis: Marcus Institute Gold Standard Center'. 'Gold Standard Center' is a journalist's headline written by NeurologyLive's editorial staff, not a designation conferred by any awarding body, and the article body contains no designation claim at all. A separate patient review on Dr. Husain Wilson's profile also uses the phrase 'gold standard' colloquially. I refuse to convert either into a formal credential. The only awarding-body credentials I can verify for this hospital are the DNV Comprehensive Stroke Center certification and the Joint Commission Thrombectomy-Capable Stroke Center certification, both of which are stroke credentials, not MS credentials. NO FELLOWSHIP: FAU sponsors no neurology fellowship of any kind (domain 18).
conflict_notes: The April 5, 2024 article names the MS and neuroimmunology program director as 'Amy Yu, MD' while the March 28, 2025 article and the current official profile name 'Amy Wei-Hsin Laitinen, M.D.' in the same role at the same institute. I read this as one physician under a changed surname and have flagged rather than silently merged it.

raw_finding: FAU's GME Residency and Fellowship Programs page is the institution's own complete enumeration of what it sponsors. Under 'Residency Programs' it lists five: Emergency Medicine, General Surgery, Internal Medicine, Neurology, Psychiatry. Under 'Fellowship Programs' it lists six: Cardiovascular Disease, Emergency Medical Services, Geriatric Medicine, Hospice and Palliative Medicine, Pulmonary Critical Care Medicine, Vascular Surgery. No neurology subspecialty fellowship appears. This is a positive institutional enumeration rather than a failed search, which is why the status is VERIFIED and the value is an empty list rather than a null. Corroborating the same conclusion from a different direction: FREIDA's field_match_nrmp_adv_fellow = false for this program, and NRMP's Program Results for 'FAU-Schmidt COM-FL / Boca Raton' across 2021-2026 shows only Emergency Medicine, Internal Medicine, Medicine-Preliminary, Neurology, Psychiatry, General Surgery and Surgery-Preliminary codes — no neurology subspecialty code. FABRICATION TRAP CAUGHT AND REJECTED: a Boca Raton Regional Hospital Foundation giving page states that the Institute 'will create fellowship programs and bring experts to teach cutting-edge therapies for neurologic disorders'. That is donor-facing future intent, in the future tense, with no named fellowship, no accreditation status and no fellows. The Texas wave found two fellowships that were 'in development or aspirational, not operating'; this is the same shape and I am not recording it as a fellowship. I also did NOT infer a movement disorders fellowship from Dr. Husain Wilson's movement disorders fellowship training, nor an MS fellowship from Dr. Laitinen's Columbia neuroimmunology fellowship, nor an epilepsy fellowship from Dr. Patel's epilepsy board certification, nor a vascular neurology fellowship from Dr. Katsafanas's and Dr. Osehobo's vascular training — the contract forbids exactly that inference and all four would have been available to make.

summary: The program has graduated four cohorts since 2022 but publishes no alumni or placement list. Two placements were verified from employers' own pages: a 2025 chief resident is now an attending neurologist at the primary teaching site and an FAU clinical affiliate assistant professor, and another graduate is a movement disorders fellow at the University of Florida.
raw_finding: PROGRAM AGE ESTABLISHES THAT GRADUATES EXIST: FAU's 2018-02-07 announcement states the inaugural class 'will be selected in March through the National Resident Matching Program (NRMP) and will start on July 1', so the first class entered July 1, 2018 and completed the four-year program in June 2022. NRMP Program Results confirm uninterrupted 3-position cohorts through the 2026 Match. Four cohorts (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025) have therefore finished, roughly twelve graduates. NO PLACEMENT PAGE: the program's published site consists of index, rotations, program-admin, apply, contact, conference, residents, faculty, teaching-hospitals, FAQs and scholarly-activity pages. There is no alumni page, no graduate-outcomes page, and no 'where our graduates go' list anywhere on the program or FAU GME site. That is a RESEARCHED_NOT_PUBLIC finding about the program's publishing, not an absence of outcomes. VERIFIED PLACEMENT 1 — Roxana Maria Dragomir, M.D. Baptist Health's own physician profile states: 'Roxana M. Dragomir, M.D., is a board-certified neurologist at Marcus Neuroscience Institute, part of Baptist Health. She specializes in the care of hospitalized patients with neurological conditions that affect the brain, spinal cord and nerves. Her clinical interests include acute pathologies such as stroke, neuromuscular emergencies and headaches... Dr. Dragomir earned her medical degree at Transilvania University, Faculty of Medicine, in Romania where she is also a Ph.D. candidate. She completed her internal medicine internship and neurology residency at Florida Atlantic University Charles E. Schmidt College of Medicine in Boca Raton, serving as chief resident. Dr. Dragomir serves as a Clinical Affiliate Assistant Professor of Neurology at the Charles E. Schmidt College of Medicine.' Her credentials block records 'Residency, Neurology, 2025'. FAU's own scholarly-activity page independently corroborates her as a program trainee: '2023 Alpha Omega Alpha Honor Medical Society - Dr. Roxana Dragomir' and a 2023 AAN poster presentation. This is a strong retention datapoint: a 2025 graduate hired as an attending at the program's own primary teaching site with an FAU academic appointment. VERIFIED PLACEMENT 2 — Octavio Carranza-Renteria. The University of Florida Department of Neurology profile page lists him as 'Jr. Movement Disorders Fellow'. That page does not itself name FAU as his residency, so the linkage rests on FAU's own scholarly-activity page, which lists him as a resident author on multiple AAN and ANA poster presentations and as the '2022 Gold Foundation Humanism & Excellence in Teaching Award' recipient — a resident award. I therefore rate the fellowship fact HIGH and the FAU-graduate linkage MEDIUM, and I note that early search snippets described him as a 'Behavioral Neurology Fellow' whereas the primary UF page says Movement Disorders; I am recording what the primary page says. OTHER NAMED FORMER RESIDENTS visible on FAU's scholarly-activity page, whose current positions I did not establish: Denis Babici (2024 AOA, 2023 Gold Foundation award, first-author publications in Brain Circulation and a first-place SGIM/SHM Florida poster), Adrian Rodriguez-Hernandez (2023 Gold Foundation award), Firas Hindi, Sara Waheed, Ali Bayas, Roxana Dragomir. STALENESS CAVEAT ON THE SCHOLARLY PAGE: its journal articles run 2020-2022, its posters 2022-2023, and its most recent award entry is 2025 (Dr. Willy Gan, a current PGY-4, 2025 Gold Foundation Humanism & Excellence in Teaching Award). The publication list is therefore several cycles behind and should not be read as the program's current research output. RESIDENT RESEARCH IS REAL BUT MODEST: the program index page states 'Our residents have won research competitions, published in peer-reviewed journals, and presented at the American Academy of Neurology Annual Meeting', and the scholarly page substantiates that with named AAN 2022 and AAN 2023 poster presentations and peer-reviewed case reports and reviews.

summary: The program does not publish an ABPN board certification pass rate. It states that it tracks board pass rates as a program-evaluation measure, but no number is public.
raw_finding: Searched the program index, rotations, FAQ, apply, scholarly-activity, program-administration and teaching-hospitals pages, the FAU GME pages, and the full FREIDA 2026 survey payload. No ABPN pass-rate percentage appears anywhere. What the program does publish is an intention and a process, not a number: the index page says 'We are committed to preparing our residents, not only for clinical practice, but for success on the board examination', and FREIDA's field_program_evaluation_2019 for this program lists 'Graduates' board certification pass rates' among the measures used to evaluate the program (alongside 'Aggregate resident Milestone achievements' and 'Performance-based assessment scores (e.g. OSCE, patient or computer simulations)'), which the registry rendered as 'Board Certification Pass Rate Evaluation: Yes'. That registry field means the program USES pass rates as an internal evaluation input; it does not report a pass rate, and it must not be read as one. ABPN publishes aggregate and per-program certification data through its own channels rather than on program sites; nothing I could reach without a paywall or login attached a figure to this program. This is a classic RESEARCHED_NOT_PUBLIC: a small program with four graduating cohorts could publish this and has chosen not to. It is NOT evidence of a poor pass rate and must not be reported as such.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete · The program does not publish a board certification pass rate, though it reports using graduates' board pass rates as an internal program-evaluation measure.
conflict_notes: The registry's 'Board Certification Pass Rate Evaluation: Yes' is a program-evaluation-method flag, not a pass rate. Recorded as SEMANTIC_MISMATCH risk in registry_reconciliation.

raw_finding: FAU's GME 'Salary, Benefits, and Policy' page states, under the heading 'Resident Salaries for FY26 (July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027)': 'Post Graduate Year 1 - $66,433 / Post Graduate Year 2 - $68,829 / Post Graduate Year 3 - $71,482 / Post Graduate Year 4 - $74,791 / Post Graduate Year 5 - $78,049 / Post Graduate Year 6 - $81,064 / Post Graduate Year 7 - $84,184 / Post Graduate Year 8 - $88,545', with the note '*Note: Fellow salaries will be assigned based upon the post graduate level immediately subsequent to the final specialty prerequisite year.' The same page states 'Up to 4 weeks of paid time off provided per academic year', 'Malpractice insurance is provided and paid for by Florida Atlantic University and is limited to activities within the training program', 'Long-Term Disability: Provided at no cost to the trainee', 'HMO and PPO option for individual and family', 'Parking is available at all facilities' and 'Lab coats are furnished at no cost to the trainee'. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION: FREIDA's 2026 survey (received 2026-07-08) carries field_first_year_salary = 66433 and field_graduate_year_statistics = [{salary 66433, paid_vacation 28}, {68829, 28}, {71482, 28}, {74791, 28}], matching the institutional page to the dollar across all four residency years and confirming 28 days of paid vacation at every level. This is a rare clean triangulation between an HR page and FREIDA. STALENESS OF THE REGISTRY: the registry's $61,295 / $63,561 / $66,037 / $68,660 are the survey_2025 figures, which I confirmed directly in the archived FREIDA payload (field_first_year_salary = 61295). Every registry salary year is therefore understated, by $5,138 at PGY-1 and $6,131 at PGY-4. A student shown the registry numbers would be misinformed by roughly 8 percent. REVERSED FIELD: FREIDA's field_allows_moonlighting is true in the 2026 cycle and false in the archived 2025 cycle, so the registry's 'Moonlighting: No' is superseded. FREIDA sentinels handled correctly: field_leave_unpaid = 999 is the AMA's Negotiable sentinel (the registry rendered it 'NGO'), and is not a count of days.
conflict_notes: Registry salaries are one survey cycle stale at all four PGY levels. Registry 'Moonlighting: No' is contradicted by FREIDA's current cycle. Registry 'Vacation: 28' is confirmed.

summary: Eleven student-ready reasons were assembled, each tied to a named clinic, a named faculty role, a specific rotation, or a published number rather than to generic praise.

The strongest mechanisms, in order of relevance to this student: (1) a REQUIRED dedicated outpatient Movement Disorders rotation in PGY-2 plus a Movement Disorders elective in PGY-2 through PGY-4, taught by the Director of Movement Disorder Neurology at the primary teaching site; (2) a Neuroimmunology/Multiple Sclerosis elective whose subspecialty lead is the residency's own Associate Program Director; (3) that same Associate Program Director is documented by her institution as fluent in Spanish; (4) a single categorical NRMP code filled 3 of 3 in each of the last six Match years, meaning one application and no separate preliminary-year match; (5) Step 2 required only before ranking; (6) a current PGY-3 who is a University of Puerto Rico School of Medicine graduate; (7) a guaranteed chief-resident year for every PGY-4; (8) a DNV-certified Comprehensive Stroke Center with a 20-bed neuro ICU as the home base. summary: Spanish has documented program-level standing here rather than merely demographic plausibility: the Associate Program Director is officially documented as fluent in Spanish and simultaneously leads the MS and neuroimmunology service, and two of the twelve current residents are published as fluent in Spanish. There is no formal Medical Spanish curriculum.
raw_finding: WHAT I AM COUNTING, and why each item clears the bar. (1) SPANISH_CLINICAL_SERVICE / mentorship. Baptist Health's official physician profile for Amy Wei-Hsin Laitinen, M.D. states 'She is fluent in English, Spanish and Mandarin' and carries a structured Language block containing 'Spanish' and 'Chinese - Mandarin'. This is an institutional attestation about a practising clinician's clinical language, published by her employer, and the clinician in question holds two relevant roles at once: Associate Program Director of THIS residency and Director of Multiple Sclerosis and Neuroimmunology at the program's primary teaching site. It is therefore program-level, inside the training environment, and situated in exactly the subspecialty Alejandra names. This is the single strongest Spanish datapoint in the dossier. (2) BILINGUAL_CLINICAL_ENVIRONMENT at the trainee level. The program's own roster page publishes, for Eduardo Rodriguez, M.D. (PGY-3), 'He is fluent in Spanish', and for Jessica Canosa, M.D. (PGY-4), 'Dr. Canosa is fluent in English and Spanish.' Two of twelve current residents, published by the program itself. The same page publishes other languages for other residents (Gujarati and Hindi for Dr. Kachhadia, Bengali for Dr. Hossain, Arabic for Dr. Owais, Russian for Dr. Boguslavskiy, Albanian conversationally for Dr. Demiraj), which shows the program is deliberately recording clinical languages rather than incidentally mentioning Spanish. Documented faculty languages follow the same pattern: Dr. Husain Wilson's profile states 'She is fluent in English and Hindi.' (3) SAFETY_NET_SITE. The program's own teaching-hospitals page says of St. Mary's Medical Center, the site of the required pediatric neurology rotation, that it 'provides emergency and injury care for a higher risk urban population and a significant population of underinsured and urban minority patients.' That is a program-published, site-specific statement about the payer and vulnerability profile of a required rotation. I count it as a safety-net exposure finding ONLY. I explicitly do NOT convert it into Spanish-language evidence: the sentence says 'underinsured and urban minority', not Spanish-speaking, and inferring a language from that phrase is exactly the move the contract forbids. WHAT I SEARCHED FOR AND DID NOT FIND. No formal Medical Spanish curriculum, elective, certificate, or language-concordant-care track appears on the program index, rotations, conference, apply, FAQ, residents, faculty, teaching-hospitals or scholarly pages, on any FAU GME page, or anywhere in the 210-field FREIDA 2026 survey payload, which contains zero occurrences of the string 'spanish'. The registry's 'Medical Spanish Curriculum: No' is therefore independently corroborated rather than inherited. No Latino-community clinic, no Spanish-language continuity clinic, no documented Latino-community mission statement, and no residency-level interpreter-training requirement was found. NET ASSESSMENT: MODERATE, not STRONG. Strong would require a structured Spanish or language-concordant care component inside the residency. What exists is a Spanish-fluent Associate Program Director in the student's target subspecialty and two Spanish-fluent co-residents — real, verifiable, program-level, and materially better than nothing, but personnel-dependent rather than curricular.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete · The program does not publish a formal Medical Spanish curriculum. What it does publish is a Spanish-fluent Associate Program Director who also directs the MS and neuroimmunology service, and two current residents documented as fluent in Spanish.
