summary: No Universidad Central del Caribe tie was found anywhere — no resident, faculty member, or program leader. The program does, however, currently train a graduate of the University of Puerto Rico School of Medicine, which is the first Puerto Rico medical school graduate identified in the Florida universe so far.
raw_finding: UCC: ZERO. I checked every named person this program publishes. The twelve current residents' schools are St. George's University (Grenada), Lincoln Memorial DeBusk, Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay (India), Ross (x3, Barbados), American University of the Caribbean (St. Maarten), Burrell COM at NMSU, Nova Southeastern Kiran C. Patel COM, University of Puerto Rico SOM, University of Toledo, and Edward Via COM. None is Universidad Central del Caribe. The sixteen named faculty publish board certifications and subspecialties but not medical schools, so a UCC faculty tie cannot be excluded by the roster alone; however, the three faculty whose full credentials ARE published on official Baptist Health profiles trained elsewhere entirely — Katsafanas at Nova Southeastern COM then University of Florida COM-Jacksonville, Laitinen at University of Vermont then Yale then Columbia, Husain Wilson at Nova Southeastern. A targeted search for any Universidad Central del Caribe, Ponce Health Sciences University, University of Puerto Rico or San Juan Bautista connection to Florida Atlantic University neurology or the Marcus Neuroscience Institute returned nothing linking these institutions. So: ucc_faculty = 0 found, with the caveat that faculty medical schools are mostly unpublished. This is consistent with the Florida-wide tally in my tasking — two UCC faculty ties statewide, one at Larkin South Miami and none elsewhere, and zero UCC residents anywhere. FAU adds zero to both. PUERTO RICO: ONE, AND IT MATTERS. The program's own roster page states: 'Eduardo Rodriguez, M.D. (PGY-3) - Dr. Rodriguez is a graduate of the University of Puerto Rico School of Medicine. He completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Puerto Rico Piedras. He has volunteered with the Caribbean Neurology Center. In his free time, he enjoys Crossfit, running, beach and paddle tennis and being a cat "dad". He is fluent in Spanish.' CLASSIFICATION, stated explicitly because the contract warns that getting this wrong would misclassify Alejandra's own school: the University of Puerto Rico School of Medicine is LCME-accredited and is a UNITED STATES MD school. Dr. Rodriguez is counted in the us_md bucket. He is NOT Caribbean and NOT other-IMG, notwithstanding the geography and notwithstanding that five of his co-residents genuinely are offshore-Caribbean graduates. This program's roster is in fact a clean illustration of the distinction: one Puerto Rico LCME graduate classified US_MD sitting alongside three Ross, one St. George's and one AUC graduate classified CARIBBEAN. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION THAT THE PROGRAM AND FREIDA AGREE WITH THIS CLASSIFICATION: FREIDA's 2026 survey reports field_pct_usmd = 16.7 for a twelve-resident program, which is exactly two people. The only two candidates are Dr. Rodriguez (UPR) and Dr. Gan (University of Toledo). FREIDA's own arithmetic therefore counts the Puerto Rico graduate as a U.S. MD. STRATEGIC WEIGHT FOR ALEJANDRA: this is a demonstrated pathway, not an inference. A program that has already selected, matched and is currently training a Puerto Rico LCME MD graduate has shown that its screening does not treat a Puerto Rico school as foreign or as requiring ECFMG certification. Combined with the absence of any 'LCME-accredited schools in the U.S. and Canada' eligibility phrasing (domain 9), the Puerto Rico pathway at this program is unambiguous. NO ALUMNI UCC/PR TIES: the named former residents recoverable from the scholarly-activity page (Babici, Dragomir, Carranza-Renteria, Rodriguez-Hernandez, Hindi, Waheed, Bayas) include graduates of Romanian and Mexican schools where published, and none of a Puerto Rico school.

raw_finding: THE TWO-LARKIN QUESTION, RESOLVED ON SEVEN INDEPENDENT LINES OF EVIDENCE. (1) TWO LIVE NRMP PROGRAM CODES PUBLISHED SIDE BY SIDE in NRMP's own Main Residency Match program directory. DIFFERENT NRMP INSTITUTION CODES (2238 vs 1481) AND DIFFERENT NRMP PROGRAM CODES. This is the decisive evidence class. (2) TWO SEPARATE ACGME SPONSORING INSTITUTIONS in FREIDA's relationship graph. Mine: 'Neurology Program, 1475 W 49th St, Hialeah, FL 33012-3222', POINT(-80.312304 25.868847), node created 2021-02-12T16:33:57+00:00. Sibling: Program Director 'Wilson C Cueva, MD', program contact 'Angelica Hassett, MD', email ahassett@larkinhospital.com. value.determination: FREIDA's rendered program record for 1801100158 places the Step 2 CK question inside a block explicitly headed 'Medical Exam Licensing Requirements for Interview Consideration', and answers it Yes for every applicant category: 'U.S. MD Applicants | Must Have Passed USMLE Step 2 CK | Yes'; 'IMG Applicants | Must Have Passed USMLE Step 2 CK | Yes'; 'DO Applicants | Must Have Passed COMLEX Level 2 | Yes'. The underlying 2026-07-21 survey booleans are field_usmle_us_md_pass_ck=true, field_usmle_img_pass_ck=true, field_comlex_do_pass_ce=true. Because the requirement is attached by FREIDA's own section heading to INTERVIEW CONSIDERATION rather than to ranking or to the start date, the correct code is REQUIRES_STEP2_BEFORE_INTERVIEW. I did NOT infer this timing from any minimum-score rule -- no minimum score is published (see domain 4). COUNTERVAILING EVIDENCE, PRESERVED RATHER THAN RESOLVED AWAY: the same survey record also carries field_usmle_step2_req_int=false and field_usmle_step1_req_int=false, field names that read as 'Step 2 required for interview'. These two FREIDA fields point in opposite directions. The most likely explanation is that the *_pass_ck family and the *_req_int family are different questions (passage of the exam versus a reported numeric score at the time of the interview offer), and only the *_pass_ck family is rendered on the public page under the interview-consideration heading. But I cannot verify FREIDA's internal question wording, so the tension is recorded as a conflict rather than resolved. Separately, field_usmle_step_1_required=false and field_usmle_step_2_required=false render on the public page as the single line 'Requires the USMLE Step 1 and/or Step 2 CK | No', positioned immediately after the DO block; that line is the DO-USMLE question (field_do_usmle_req_ind=false) and must not be misread as 'Step 2 not required'. The program's OWN Application Process page publishes NO examination requirement of any kind and therefore neither corroborates nor contradicts FREIDA. There is no applicant FAQ and no GME-level application-requirements page for this program. Because the only affirmative published timing statement available places Step 2 CK at interview consideration, the finding is reported at that strength and NOT softened into 'no published barrier'.
value.exact_paraphrase: Under the heading 'Medical Exam Licensing Requirements for Interview Consideration', FREIDA records for this program: U.S. MD applicants 'Must Have Passed USMLE Step 2 CK - Yes'; IMG applicants 'Must Have Passed USMLE Step 2 CK - Yes'; DO applicants 'Must Have Passed COMLEX Level 2 - Yes'.
value.barrier_reasoning: This is the single most decision-relevant finding in the dossier for Alejandra. She sat Step 2 CK in late September 2026 with the result expected mid-October 2026. Two published facts interact badly with that timeline. First, a passed Step 2 CK is required for INTERVIEW CONSIDERATION. Second, FREIDA records this program's 'Program Starts Reviewing Applications' value as 'Application service release date' (survey field field_application_service_releas=true) -- i.e. the program begins reviewing on the ERAS release date in late September 2026, BEFORE her score posts. An application reviewed in that first window would show no Step 2 CK result against a published requirement that one be passed. That is a genuine, program-specific, published barrier and I am recording it as one. Three mitigations should be stated with equal precision, because they are real. (a) The requirement is that Step 2 CK be PASSED, not that a score meet a threshold -- no threshold is published -- so a mid-October pass satisfies the rule as written from mid-October onward. (b) Neurology interview invitations characteristically continue from October into December and January, so the majority of this program's invitation window falls after her result posts; the program conducted only 40 interviews last cycle for 4 positions, which is a small and therefore potentially later-moving invitation set. (c) FREIDA records interview offer dates as following 'Specialty Universal Dates' rather than a program-specific early date. The residual risk is concentrated in the earliest review window, and the actionable consequence is that she should not count on this program reviewing her favourably before mid-October and should confirm the Step 2 timing rule directly with the coordinator (neurcoordpsc@larkinhospital.com) before relying on it. No match-probability or likelihood claim is made or implied.

raw_finding: The 'Our Residents-Neurology-PSC' page lists 16 residents as bare names under PGY headings -- 'Dr. Luisa Figueredo', 'Dr. Deepal Patel' and so on -- with no medical school, no degree designation, no graduation year, no country and no biography or photograph. There are no per-resident sub-pages: the page is a flat list and the only links in its content region are the six program navigation links. RECOVERY TECHNIQUES ATTEMPTED. (1) I read the raw HTML of the roster page rather than only its rendered text, looking for a JS-rendered directory payload of the kind that turned 'roster not provided' into 29 residents with schools in Texas; there is none -- the roster is static WordPress markup with no directory endpoint and no embedded JSON. (2) The site exposes wp-json (the page emits wp-json/oembed/1.0/embed references) but the resident names are page body content, not a custom post type carrying school metadata. (3) There is no alumni-with-schools page either -- the alumni page is likewise names only (domain 19). (4) The Internet Archive holds no capture of this page, so no earlier version with richer detail can be recovered. (5) FREIDA supplies only aggregate three-year-average medical-school-type percentages, never per-person schools. I deliberately made NO attempt to infer any resident's medical school, school country, nationality or ethnicity from their name. Governance law 4 forbids it, and it would be unreliable in any case. Every resident is therefore classified UNKNOWN in the residents[] records, and the consequences for the composition partition are set out in full in domain 13. One name-collision ambiguity is recorded rather than resolved: 'Dr. Syed Naqvi' appears as a PGY-2 on this program's resident roster, while 'Sayed Naqvi, M.D.' appears on the SIBLING South Miami program's 22-member faculty page. freida_three_year_averages.freida_caveat_verbatim: Three year averages. Medical school type does not include graduates of Canadian schools.
freida_three_year_averages.why_not_converted_to_counts: These are THREE-YEAR AVERAGES, not a current-cohort census. Multiplying them against the 16-person current census would splice incompatible units and manufacture per-person counts that no source supports.

summary: All 16 residents are named but none has a published medical school, so every one is classified UNKNOWN and the five buckets are 0/0/0/0/16 against a denominator of 16. FREIDA's separate three-year averages (0.0% US MD, 6.2% DO, 93.8% IMG) describe the program's recent intake pattern but cannot be converted into counts for this cohort.
raw_finding: DENOMINATOR. 16, on the basis of ACTUAL CENSUS: the program's own roster names 16 residents (4 per year, PGY-1 to PGY-4), and FREIDA independently renders 'Current Residents | Year 1 4 | Year 2 4 | Year 3 4 | Year 4 4'. The approved complement is also 16 (field_total_positions=16, field_program_size=[4,4,4,4]). Complement and census coincide here, but they are established separately and the denominator used is the census, per the contract's guard against using complement as a roster denominator. THE FIVE-BUCKET PARTITION AND WHY IT IS 0/0/0/0/16. The roster publishes names only -- no medical school, no degree, no country (domain 12). Governance law 4 forbids inferring anything from a name. There is therefore NO per-person evidence of school or school country for any of the 16, and all 16 fall into `unknown`. us_md + us_do + caribbean + other_img + unknown = 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 16 = 16 = denominator. Sum check passes. WHY I DID NOT USE FREIDA'S PERCENTAGES AS COUNTS -- THIS IS THE CENTRAL JUDGEMENT IN THIS DOMAIN. FREIDA reports field_pct_usmd='0.0', field_pct_do='6.2', field_pct_img='93.8' for this program. It is arithmetically seductive that 6.2% of 16 is 0.99 and 93.8% of 16 is 15.0, which would give a tidy us_do=1 / img=15 split. I rejected that for two independent reasons. FIRST, FREIDA'S OWN CAVEAT: the rendered page heads that block 'Resident / Fellow Characteristics' and states verbatim 'Three year averages. Medical school type does not include graduates of Canadian schools.' These are three-year averages across recent cohorts, NOT a snapshot of the current 16. Multiplying a three-year average by a current head-count is exactly the unit splice the contract warns about (in Texas a '27' was produced by summing FREIDA per-year answers and matched no real year). The product would be a number no source actually asserts. SECOND, THE IMG BUCKET IS NOT DECOMPOSABLE ANYWAY: even if the 93.8% were a current-cohort figure, `caribbean` and `other_img` are distinct buckets and FREIDA never distinguishes offshore Caribbean schools from other international schools. Assigning all IMGs to `other_img` would affirmatively assert 'not Caribbean' about 15 people, and assigning them to `caribbean` would assert the opposite; both are fabrications. For a community program in South Florida with a 93.8% IMG three-year average, offshore Caribbean graduates are plausibly well represented, but plausibility is not evidence and I record none. WHAT THE PERCENTAGES DO LEGITIMATELY SUPPORT, STATED SEPARATELY FROM THE BUCKETS: this program's recent intake has been overwhelmingly international-graduate and has included essentially no U.S. MD graduates (0.0% over three years). That is a real, sourced characterisation of the program's recruiting pattern and it is decision-relevant for Alejandra -- as a U.S. MD graduate she would be an outlier against the program's recent intake profile, which cuts both ways and is discussed in the classification rationale. Registry values 'International Graduates: 87.5%', 'US Graduates: US MD 0.0%; DO 12.5%', 'DO Graduates Percent: 12.5%', 'IMG Graduates Percent: 87.5%' are all SUPERSEDED by the current survey's 0.0% / 6.2% / 93.8%. PUERTO RICO CLASSIFICATION RULE, RECORDED FOR THE INGESTING SYSTEM EVEN THOUGH IT BINDS ON NOBODY HERE: Puerto Rico's LCME-accredited schools (Universidad Central del Caribe, Ponce Health Sciences University, University of Puerto Rico, San Juan Bautista) are UNITED STATES MD schools and their graduates count as US_MD -- never CARIBBEAN, never OTHER_IMG. 'CARIBBEAN' denotes offshore for-profit schools such as Ross, St George's, AUC, Saba, Texila and Windsor. No resident here is identifiable as a PR-school graduate, so ucc_residents=0 and puerto_rico_school_residents=0 -- and those two are OVERLAY counts in any event, deliberately NOT added into the five-bucket sum. GENDER, for completeness: field_pct_female='31.2', field_pct_male='68.8', unchanged from the registry and also three-year averages.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - The program does not publish its residents' medical schools, so no resident can be classified as US MD, DO, Caribbean or other international graduate. FREIDA's 0.0% US MD / 6.2% DO / 93.8% IMG figures are three-year averages and are not a breakdown of the current 16 residents.

summary: The program publishes eight named 'Current Department Members' with training histories. Their strengths are neuro-rehabilitation, vascular/endovascular neurology, epilepsy and neuro-ophthalmology. No movement disorders or MS faculty are listed, and the roster is not labelled as the complete ACGME core faculty.
raw_finding: The 'Our Faculty-Neurology-PSC' page publishes eight individuals under the heading 'CURRENT DEPARTMENT MEMBERS', each with a 'Medical Education' block and a 'Certifications' block. Full details are carried in this domain's faculty[] array; the training histories quoted there are verbatim from that page. REGISTRY DEFECT, EXACTLY THE PATTERN THE CONTRACT NAMED. The registry stored 'Program Faculty Count: 0', 'Faculty Distribution: Physicians: 0; non-physicians: 0' and 'Faculty Resident Ratio: 0.00:1'. Those are FREIDA NULL SENTINELS, not measurements -- FREIDA's own rendered page shows 'Program Faculty | --', 'Female Faculty | --', 'Faculty Distribution | Physicians (--) | Non-Physicians (--)', with the underlying survey fields field_total_physician=0, field_total_non_physician=0, field_ratio_ft_faculty='0.00'. Against a real, published eight-member department roster, '0' is a SEMANTIC_MISMATCH and must never be reported to a student as 'this program has no faculty'. COMPLETENESS IS NOT ESTABLISHED. The page says 'Current Department Members', not 'core faculty', gives no count, no administrative titles beyond the PD, and no indication whether these eight are the ACGME-designated core faculty, the full clinical department, or a selection. Eight core faculty against 16 residents would be plausible for a 4-year community program, but I assert nothing. Hence PARTIALLY_VERIFIED. WHAT THE ROSTER POSITIVELY SHOWS -- A DEPARTMENT BUILT AROUND NEURO-REHABILITATION, STROKE AND EPILEPSY. Three of the eight trained at University of Miami / Jackson Memorial (Nedd residency and fellowship, Rubin fellowship, Oliu residency and fellowship), which is a real and specific institutional lineage rather than a generic claim. Two are fellowship-trained in Neurologic Rehabilitation (Nedd, Rubin), matching the PGY-4 'Inpatient Neurology Rehabilitation' rotation and the West Gables Rehabilitation Hospital training site. One is dual-fellowship-trained in Vascular Neurology and Endovascular Surgical Neuroradiology (Kaushal), matching the ICU/Stroke rotations. Two hold ABPN Epilepsy certification (Oliu; Medaa, who also holds ABPN Special Qualification in Child Neurology), matching the PGY-4 Epilepsy rotation. One is fellowship-trained in Neuro-Ophthalmology (Kay), matching both the PGY-2 Neuro-Ophthalmology rotation and the 'Matthew Kay MD PA-Ophthalmology Office' participating site -- a clean faculty-to-rotation-to-site cross-confirmation. WHAT THE ROSTER CONSPICUOUSLY LACKS, AND WHY IT MATTERS FOR THIS STUDENT. There is NO movement disorders specialist and NO multiple sclerosis or neuroimmunology specialist among the eight -- Alejandra's two stated subspecialty interests. There is also no neuromuscular specialist despite a PGY-3 NCV/EMG rotation, and no sleep-boarded physician despite Sleep Medicine being advertised as a resident subspecialty clinic. ONE NON-NEUROLOGIST IS INCLUDED: Dr. Odalys Frontela's only listed training is Internship/Residency in Internal Medicine at Mayaguez Medical Center and her only listed certification is ABIM; she is presented as a department member but is not a certified neurologist. PUERTO RICO TIE, WHICH IS A GENUINE ALEJANDRA SIGNAL. Dr. Frontela's training site, 'Mayaguez Medical Center', is in Mayaguez, Puerto Rico (410 Hostos Ave, Mayaguez, PR 00680; the ACGME-accredited Internal Medicine program there is the Ramon Betances Hospital-Mayaguez Medical Center/Ponce School of Medicine Consortium). The program's faculty page does not state the location, so I verified independently that no mainland US facility of that name exists; confidence MEDIUM on the location, HIGH on the training claim itself. This is a Puerto Rico GRADUATE-TRAINING tie, not a Puerto Rico medical-school tie, and her medical school is not published. No faculty member is identifiable as a Universidad Central del Caribe graduate. SPANISH: no faculty member's language skills are documented anywhere on this program's pages, so spanish_documented is null for all eight rather than false. I checked whether an HR or provider directory would supply language fields, per the contract's technique; larkinhealth.com's neurology service page documents languages for physicians, but the only neurologist it profiles (Dr. Mohan Deochand, 'English, Spanish') belongs to the SIBLING South Miami program's faculty roster, not to this one, so it cannot be used here.

value.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: This program inverts the usual pattern and the distinction must be stated precisely. RESIDENT EXPOSURE IS ESTABLISHED: the program's own curriculum page lists 'Movement Disorder' as one of seven PGY-2 rotations, so every resident passes through a movement-disorders block. That is documented, required exposure -- materially stronger than a department that merely treats Parkinson's disease. INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY IS NOT ESTABLISHED: none of the eight published department members is a movement-disorders specialist or has any movement-disorders fellowship or certification; no movement-disorders or Parkinson's clinic is named by the program, by Larkin Health System's neurology service page, or by any participating site; there is no movement-disorders fellowship at either Larkin campus; no movement-disorders research, faculty-scholar project or publication is published; and no formal designation of any kind was found. The honest characterisation is therefore: guaranteed rotational exposure, undocumented depth and undocumented mentorship. For an applicant whose stated interest is Movement Disorders, the rotation is a real positive and the absence of an identifiable movement-disorders mentor is a real limitation, and the two should be presented together.

summary: Every resident rotates through a required PGY-2 'Movement Disorder' block, which is genuine documented exposure. But no movement-disorders faculty member, named clinic, fellowship or research program is published, so depth and mentorship are unestablished.
raw_finding: POSITIVE EVIDENCE, FROM THE PROGRAM'S OWN CURRICULUM PAGE. Under 'PROGRAM DESIGN / Rotations By Year', the PGY-2 list reads verbatim: 'Junior Neurology Consults / Ambulatory Neurology / Neuro - Ophthalmology / Inpatient Neurology Junior / ICU / Stroke / Movement Disorder / Sleep Medicine / Inpatient Neurology Junior / General Neurology'. 'Movement Disorder' is listed as a PGY-2 rotation block alongside the other required rotations, with no 'elective' qualifier -- the only blocks labelled 'Elective' anywhere in the four-year schedule are in PGY-3 and PGY-4. Block duration, training site and supervising faculty are not stated. NEGATIVE EVIDENCE, SEARCHED FOR DELIBERATELY AND RECORDED AS NEGATIVE. (1) FACULTY: all eight published department members were checked individually against their stated fellowships and board certifications -- Neurologic Rehabilitation (Nedd, Rubin), Vascular Neurology and Endovascular Surgical Neuroradiology (Kaushal), Epilepsy (Oliu; Medaa with Child Neurology), Neuro-Ophthalmology (Kay), Neurology with no stated subspecialty (Yousseff), Internal Medicine (Frontela). NONE is a movement-disorders specialist. (2) CLINIC: the program advertises exactly three subspecialty clinics on its home page -- 'Our residents have the chance to participate in a wide range of subspecialty clinics, including those dedicated to Sleep Medicine, Neuro-Ophthalmology, and Pediatric Neurology' -- and a movement-disorders clinic is NOT among them, which is a notable omission given the rotation exists. (3) SYSTEM SERVICE LINES: Larkin Health System's own neurology service page names no movement disorders or Parkinson's program; its only named neurology service lines are Sleep Medicine, seizure management and Alzheimer's disease, and its 'Miami Neuroscience Center at Larkin' is attributed to the South Miami campus, not Hialeah. (4) PARTICIPATING SITES: I specifically searched 'Advanced Neuroscience Network Physicians-Hialeah', the most likely local host for the rotation, and found no dedicated movement-disorders or Parkinson's clinic published. (5) FELLOWSHIP: Larkin's own ACGME program list shows no movement-disorders fellowship at either campus. (6) RESEARCH: FREIDA records 'Research rotation | Not available | Not Offered' (field_research_rotation='Not available', field_research_rotation_duration=0) and the registry's 'Research Track: No' is confirmed; no movement-disorders research output is published. FORMAL DESIGNATIONS -- NONE, AND NONE CLAIMED. I searched for and did NOT find any Huntington's Disease Society of America Center of Excellence, CurePSP Center of Care, Parkinson's Foundation Center of Excellence or comparable designation for Larkin Palm Springs Campus. No page I opened used any such words, so no such designation is asserted anywhere in this dossier. This is the specific failure mode the contract flagged from Texas, where an agent fabricated a designation with two real URLs attached; I am recording the negative explicitly so the absence is auditable. A TRAP I DECLINED. Secondary physician directories list 'Parkinson's disease' and 'dementia' among conditions treated by Dr. Kester Nedd. A 'conditions treated' field in a commercial provider directory is not a subspecialty credential, not a clinic, and not resident teaching capacity. Dr. Nedd's published fellowship is in Neurologic Rehabilitation and his stated expertise is traumatic brain injury and concussion. I did not count the directory listing as movement-disorders faculty evidence. A SECOND, LARGER TRAP I DECLINED -- see conflict_notes and the dossier's fabrication_traps_caught: the Larkin system's movement-disorders faculty are published on the SIBLING program's faculty page, not this one.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - The program lists a required PGY-2 Movement Disorder rotation but does not publish any movement-disorders faculty member, named movement-disorders clinic, fellowship, research activity or formal center designation.
conflict_notes: The SIBLING Larkin program (1801100156, South Miami) publishes on its own faculty page 'Stuart H. Isaacson, M.D., FAAN' and 'Leonard L. Sokol, M.D.', both associated with movement disorders. Neither appears on THIS program's faculty page. Larkin Health System therefore appears to have movement-disorders faculty depth, but it is published as belonging to the South Miami accreditation, not the Palm Springs Campus accreditation. I did not import them. Whether Palm Springs residents receive any teaching from them during their PGY-2 Movement Disorder block is NOT established either way, and the two programs do share two other clinical faculty, so cross-coverage cannot be excluded - it simply is not documented.

raw_finding: SEARCHED AND NOT FOUND, across every available source. (1) CURRICULUM: the complete four-year rotation schedule was read in full. PGY-1: Internal Medicine, MICU, Emergency Medicine, Junior Neurology Consults, Ambulatory Neurology, Psychiatry. PGY-2: Junior Neurology Consults, Ambulatory Neurology, Neuro-Ophthalmology, Inpatient Neurology Junior/ICU/Stroke, Movement Disorder, Sleep Medicine, Inpatient Neurology Junior/General Neurology. PGY-3: Neurology Consults Senior, NCV/EMG, Ambulatory Neurology, Pediatric Neurology, Inpatient Neurology Senior/ICU/Stroke, Inpatient Neurology Senior/General Neurology, Elective. PGY-4: Epilepsy, Inpatient Neurology Rehabilitation, Ambulatory Neurology, Pediatric Neurology, Inpatient Neurology Senior/General Neurology, Inpatient Neurology Senior/ICU Stroke, Elective. There is NO multiple sclerosis, neuroimmunology, demyelinating disease or neuro-infusion block anywhere in the four years. Compare movement disorders, which IS named -- so the absence of MS is a meaningful contrast within the same document rather than a generic silence. (2) FACULTY: none of the eight department members lists MS or neuroimmunology training or certification; their subspecialties are neuro-rehabilitation, vascular/endovascular, epilepsy, child neurology and neuro-ophthalmology. (3) ADVERTISED CLINICS: the home page names only Sleep Medicine, Neuro-Ophthalmology and Pediatric Neurology. (4) SYSTEM: Larkin Health System's neurology service page names no MS clinic or infusion centre. (5) FELLOWSHIP: Larkin's own ACGME program list contains no MS or neuroimmunology fellowship at either campus. (6) PARTICIPATING SITES: none of the nine is an MS centre. FORMAL DESIGNATIONS -- NONE FOUND AND NONE CLAIMED. I searched specifically for a National Multiple Sclerosis Society 'Comprehensive Care Center' or 'Partners in MS Care' designation for Larkin Palm Springs Campus and found none. No page I opened contains those words in relation to this institution, so no such designation appears anywhere in this dossier. Given that the contract records a Texas agent fabricating exactly this designation with real URLs attached, and separately records an NMSS designation migrating 80 miles on a brand-string collision, I am stating the negative explicitly and with the search recorded. STATUS REASONING. This is RESEARCHED_NOT_FOUND rather than RESEARCHED_NOT_PUBLIC because the claim itself was searched against a source that WOULD have carried it if it existed: the program publishes a complete rotation-by-rotation four-year schedule and a faculty roster with individual fellowship training, and MS is absent from both while other subspecialties are present. That is evidence bearing on the claim, not merely silence. It still falls short of an affirmative 'this program has no MS exposure', because the PGY-3 and PGY-4 Elective blocks are undescribed and general ambulatory neurology will inevitably include some MS patients. The defensible statement is that no MS-specific training component is published. CONTAMINATION NOTE, IMPORTANT. The Larkin system's MS expertise is published on the SIBLING program's pages. See conflict_notes.

summary: Larkin's Palm Springs Campus sponsors multidisciplinary Sleep Medicine, Pain Medicine and Addiction Medicine fellowships that a neurology graduate could be eligible for. There are NO neurology subspecialty fellowships at either Larkin campus - no movement disorders, MS, vascular neurology, epilepsy or clinical neurophysiology.
raw_finding: SOURCE AND METHOD. Larkin's own institutional page 'ACGME Accredited Programs' enumerates its accredited programs grouped by campus: 21 under 'South Miami Campus' and 19 under 'Palm Springs Campus'. This is an official institutional source and is the correct one for separating in-house from affiliated, because the two campuses are separate ACGME sponsoring institutions (see domain 1). IN-HOUSE TO THIS ACCREDITATION -- i.e. sponsored by Larkin Community Hospital Palm Springs Campus, the same sponsoring institution as this residency. The 19 Palm Springs Campus programs are: Addiction Medicine (Multidisciplinary), Cardiovascular Disease, Dermatology, Family Medicine, Gastroenterology, Geriatric Medicine (Internal Medicine), Hematology and Medical Oncology, Infectious Disease, Internal Medicine, Micrographic Surgery and Dermatologic Oncology, Neurology, Osteopathic Neuromusculoskeletal Medicine, Pain Medicine (Multidisciplinary), Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation, Plastic Surgery - Integrated, Rheumatology, Sleep Medicine (Multidisciplinary), Sports Medicine (Family Medicine). Of these, the ones a neurology graduate could realistically enter are the three MULTIDISCIPLINARY fellowships -- Sleep Medicine, Pain Medicine and Addiction Medicine -- because 'multidisciplinary' in ACGME usage means the fellowship accepts graduates of more than one primary specialty, neurology included for Sleep and Pain. The Sleep Medicine fellowship is the most substantively connected: this residency independently advertises a Sleep Medicine subspecialty clinic and lists 'Florida Sleep and Neuro Diagnostic Services Inc' as a participating site and a PGY-2 Sleep Medicine rotation. That is a coherent in-house pipeline and it is the strongest fellowship story this program has. AFFILIATED BUT NOT IN-HOUSE -- same health system, different sponsoring institution. The South Miami campus adds Pain Medicine (Multidisciplinary) and Hospice and Palliative Medicine (Multidisciplinary), among others. Because South Miami is a separate ACGME sponsoring institution (FREIDA institution 119101 versus 119718), these are recorded as affiliated and NOT described as in-house, even though Larkin Community Hospital South Miami is a participating training site for this residency. THE CENTRAL NEGATIVE FINDING. NEITHER CAMPUS SPONSORS A SINGLE ACGME NEUROLOGY SUBSPECIALTY FELLOWSHIP. Across all 40 listed programs there is no Movement Disorders fellowship, no Multiple Sclerosis or Neuroimmunology fellowship, no Vascular Neurology fellowship, no Epilepsy fellowship, no Clinical Neurophysiology fellowship, no Neuromuscular Medicine fellowship, no Neurocritical Care fellowship and no Neuro-oncology fellowship. A resident here who wants any neurology subspecialty must match externally. I DID NOT INFER ANY FELLOWSHIP FROM A FACULTY MEMBER'S SPECIALTY -- the contract's explicit prohibition, and the temptation was concrete here: the department includes two ABPN Epilepsy-certified physicians, a dual vascular/endovascular-trained physician and a neuro-ophthalmology fellow, none of which implies a fellowship exists. I checked the institutional program list rather than reasoning from credentials, and the list shows no such fellowships. Likewise I treated none of these as 'in development' or aspirational, because no source claims they are. FELLOWS IN POST: not published for any fellowship. Status is PARTIALLY_VERIFIED because the fellowship inventory comes from the institution's own list rather than from each fellowship's own page, and because current fellow counts and each fellowship's accreditation dates are unpublished.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - Larkin sponsors no neurology subspecialty fellowship at either campus, and does not publish the number of fellows in post for the multidisciplinary Sleep Medicine, Pain Medicine or Addiction Medicine fellowships that a neurology graduate could enter.

summary: The program names 11 graduates across three cohorts (2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25) but publishes no fellowship placements, employers or career destinations for any of them. The expected 2025-26 cohort is missing, so the page appears one cycle behind.
raw_finding: The 'Our Alumni-Neurology-PSC' page publishes under the heading 'OUR GRADUATES': '2024 - 2025' -- Dr. Sam Kara, Dr. Marisol Trejos, Dr. Jordon Prosapio, Dr. Solomon Nittala (4). '2023 - 2024' -- Dr. Jeremy Eckes, Dr. Rusdany Collado, Dr. Sadek Debwan, Dr. Michael Wilson, Dr. Patrick Mercho, Dr. Michael Alosilla (6). '2022 - 2023' -- Dr. Diyan Raza (1). Eleven named graduates in total. For each, the page gives a name and nothing else: no fellowship, no institution, no practice, no city, no photograph, no board status. OUTCOMES ARE THEREFORE RESEARCHED_NOT_PUBLIC EVEN THOUGH THE COHORTS ARE VERIFIED. This is the NOT_PUBLIC/NOT_FOUND line applied within a single domain: the existence and membership of the graduating cohorts is VERIFIED from the program's own page, while graduate placement is the kind of thing a program could publish and has not. I did not attempt to trace individual graduates through external physician directories to construct a placement list -- that would compile personal information across sources about identified private individuals, which the governance rules forbid, and would produce an unverifiable list attributed to the program. TWO STRUCTURAL OBSERVATIONS, REPORTED AS FACTS WITHOUT INFERENCE. (1) COHORT SIZES ARE IRREGULAR AGAINST A COMPLEMENT OF 4 PER YEAR: 1, then 6, then 4. A 4-position-per-year program that graduated 1 and then 6 did not graduate steady-state classes in those years. Consistent explanations include off-cycle entries, transfers in at advanced levels during the program's build-out, or extended training; FREIDA records field_beyond_accredited_length=false, which argues against routine extensions. I cannot determine which applies and do not guess. It is corroborated, though, by FREIDA's own historical interview data (2020: 0 interviews; 2021: 0 interviews against 4 positions; 2022: 90; 2023: 90; 2024: 60) and by the FREIDA node's creation date of 2021-02-12 -- together these indicate a program that was building out its cohorts in the early 2020s rather than running four steady classes. (2) THE PAGE APPEARS ONE CYCLE STALE. Today is September 2026. A 2025-2026 class of roughly four should have graduated in June 2026 and is NOT listed. Meanwhile the current resident roster shows a full PGY-4 of four. The most likely reading is simply that the alumni page has not been updated since the 2024-25 graduation; that is a staleness observation about the page, not a finding about the program's graduates. I could not test it with a Wayback differential because the Internet Archive holds no capture of our-alumni-neurology-psc (it does hold the sibling program's our-alumni-neurology from 2024-09-06). BOARD CERTIFICATION OUTCOMES for these graduates are treated separately in domain 20 and are not published.

summary: No board certification or board pass rate is published for this program, and FREIDA records that the program does not even use graduates' board pass rates as one of its own program-evaluation measures.
raw_finding: SEARCHED AND NOT PUBLISHED. The program's six pages -- home, curriculum, faculty, residents, alumni, application process -- contain no board pass rate, no first-time pass rate, no certification statistics and no ABPN data of any kind. The alumni page lists 11 graduates by name with no board status. Larkin Health System's site publishes none either. A DIRECTLY RELEVANT AND SOMEWHAT STRIKING FREIDA DATA POINT. FREIDA's 'Evaluations' block for this program, from the survey received 2026-07-21, reads: 'Program Evaluations | Aggregate resident Milestone achievements | Yes | Graduates board certification pass rates | No | Performance-based assessment scores (e.g. OSCE, patient or computer simulations) | No'. The underlying field is field_program_evaluation_2019 = ['Aggregate resident Milestone achievements', 'Graduates board certification pass rates'] -- note that the array still contains the board-pass-rate string while the rendered page reports 'No' for it, an internal FREIDA inconsistency I record rather than resolve. On the rendered reading, the program does not use its graduates' board certification pass rates as a program-evaluation measure at all, which makes it correspondingly unlikely that a rate is computed for publication. Resident evaluation methods are given as field_evaluate_res_fellow_2019 = ['Patient surveys']. WHY NO EXTERNAL SOURCE FILLS THE GAP. The American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology does not publish first-time board pass rates broken out by individual residency program, so there is no authoritative external source to substitute. ACGME's public program search, which can carry accreditation-linked data, is CAPTCHA-gated and was not bypassed per governance law 3. CONTEXT THAT MATTERS FOR INTERPRETING THE SILENCE: the program's first graduating cohort was 2022-2023 and consisted of a single resident, with 11 graduates in total across three years. A board pass rate computed on 1, then 6, then 4 graduates would be statistically fragile even if published. This is stated as context, not as an excuse for the absence. This is RESEARCHED_NOT_PUBLIC, not RESEARCHED_NOT_FOUND: a board pass rate is precisely the kind of figure a program could publish and has not. It must NOT be reported to a student as a poor result or as any result.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - The program does not publish a board certification pass rate, and the ABPN does not publish pass rates by individual residency program.
conflict_notes: Internal FREIDA inconsistency: field_program_evaluation_2019 still lists 'Graduates board certification pass rates' in its array while the rendered public page reports 'No' against that same item. Both readings preserved; neither yields an actual pass rate.

raw_finding: SALARY IS NOT PUBLISHED. FREIDA's rendered Compensation block reads 'Compensation | -- | -- Vacation Days | -- Sick Days' and its Salary Compensation block reads '-- | --'. The underlying survey field is field_graduate_year_statistics = [{'salary': null, 'paid_vacation': null, 'paid_sick': null}] -- an explicit null, from the survey received 2026-07-21. The program's own six pages publish no stipend table. Larkin's GME site has no benefits page at all: I probed /benefits/, /salary-benefits/, /house-staff-benefits/, /resident-benefits/, /stipends-benefits/ and /gme-benefits/ and every one soft-404s to the site homepage with an identical 132,182-byte response, so the absence is structural rather than a search failure. Per the contract's technique I also considered that salary tables are often images; there is no benefits page on which such an image could sit. REGISTRY DEFECT: the registry stored 'Salary PGY1: 0'. That is a FREIDA NULL SENTINEL rendered by FREIDA itself as '--', not a salary of zero. Reporting it as $0 to a student would be a serious error. Classified SEMANTIC_MISMATCH. A TRAP I DECLINED, AND IT WAS A NEAR MISS. A search for this program's salary returned a concrete figure -- PGY-1 $43,000, PGY-2 $45,000, PGY-3 $47,000, with health, dental, malpractice with tail coverage and lab coats -- which belongs to a LARKIN FAMILY MEDICINE program, a different residency with a different ACGME ID and a three-year length. Importing it would have been textbook cross-program contamination and it would have looked plausible because it is same-institution, same-system data. It is NOT this program's salary and it appears nowhere in this dossier's values. BENEFITS, FROM FREIDA'S RENDERED BLOCKS AND THE 2026-07-21 SURVEY FIELDS. Major medical for residents: 'Institution & Resident Share Cost' (field_benefit_major_residents), which SUPERSEDES the registry's 'Available, Not Paid By Institution' and is a materially better term for the resident. Major medical for dependents: 'Available, Not Paid By Institution'. Domestic partners: 'Not Available'. Dental: 'Available, Not Paid By Institution'. Group life: 'Available, Not Paid By Institution'. Disability: 'Not Available'; disability-HIV: 'Not Available'. Outpatient mental health: 'Not Available'; inpatient mental health: 'Not Available'. The pattern -- several benefits offered but not funded by the institution, and disability and mental health coverage recorded as unavailable -- is a real and student-relevant weakness and should be presented plainly rather than softened. VACATION AND SICK DAYS are null in the survey and render as '--'; the registry's NGO sentinels correspond to FREIDA's 'Negotiable' code. FAMILY AND MEDICAL LEAVE renders as 'Maximum # of paid days | 0 days | Maximum # of unpaid days | 0 days' (field_leave_paid=0, field_leave_unpaid=0). A literal reading -- zero paid AND zero unpaid family/medical leave -- is not credible for an ACGME-accredited program, since ACGME institutional requirements mandate leave policies and Florida programs are subject to federal FMLA where applicable. This is almost certainly a non-response coded as 0 rather than a real policy, and it is classified SEMANTIC_MISMATCH. It must not be reported to a student as 'this program offers no family or medical leave'. MOONLIGHTING: 'Program Allows Moonlighting (Beyond PGY-1) | No' (field_allows_moonlighting=false). This SUPERSEDES the registry's 'Moonlighting: Yes' and is a genuine reversal -- notably, the sibling South Miami program's 2026 survey answers true to the same field, so this is a real program-level difference and not a system-wide change. SALARY PAYER IS INTERNALLY CONTRADICTORY IN FREIDA. The rendered page states 'Salary paid by a non-profit institution.' while the underlying survey field reads field_salary_paid_nonprofit = 'No'. The registry stored 'Salary Paid By: Non-profit institution', following the rendered text. Because the two disagree within one source I treat the payer as unestablished. EMPLOYMENT POLICIES: FREIDA's 'Employment Policies & Benefits' block reads 'Data not provided by program'.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - The program does not publish a resident salary. FREIDA carries an explicit null for salary, vacation and sick days, records 'Data not provided by program' for employment policies, and Larkin's GME site has no benefits page.
conflict_notes: Four conflicts recorded. (1) Registry 'Salary PGY1: 0' versus FREIDA's explicit null rendered '--' - sentinel, not a value. (2) Registry 'Major Medical Residents: Available, Not Paid By Institution' versus current FREIDA 'Institution & Resident Share Cost'. (3) Registry 'Moonlighting: Yes' versus current FREIDA 'No'. (4) Within FREIDA itself, the rendered line 'Salary paid by a non-profit institution.' contradicts field_salary_paid_nonprofit='No'. A fifth item, family/medical leave of 0 paid and 0 unpaid days, is recorded as an implausible sentinel rather than a policy.

summary: The program publishes a complete four-year block schedule with named subspecialty rotations including Movement Disorder, Sleep Medicine, Neuro-Ophthalmology, Epilepsy, NCV/EMG, Pediatric Neurology and Neuro-Rehabilitation, plus PGY-3 and PGY-4 electives. There is a night float system, no moonlighting, and no research rotation or research track.
raw_finding: ROTATION SCHEDULE, verbatim from the program's own 'Our Curriculum-Neurology-PSC' page under 'PROGRAM DESIGN' and 'Rotations By Year'. The page's framing sentence reads: 'Rotations are designed to provide residents with a well-rounded experience in a vast diversity of neurological techniques. Residents rotate through different hospital systems during certain rotations to obtain appropriate experience.' The four-year block list is carried in full in this domain's value object. WHAT THE SCHEDULE SUBSTANTIVELY DELIVERS. A conventional PGY-1 with Internal Medicine, MICU, Emergency Medicine and Psychiatry alongside early neurology consults and ambulatory neurology. Subspecialty breadth concentrated in PGY-2 (Movement Disorder, Sleep Medicine, Neuro-Ophthalmology) and PGY-4 (Epilepsy, Inpatient Neurology Rehabilitation). Neuromuscular technique exposure via a dedicated PGY-3 NCV/EMG block. Stroke and neuro-ICU exposure in each of PGY-2, PGY-3 and PGY-4. Pediatric neurology in both PGY-3 and PGY-4 -- which, per governance law 2, is legitimate ADULT-program curriculum data because it is a rotation inside this adult residency, and is supported by the department's child-neurology-certified member (Dr. Ramzy Medaa) and by the 'Kidz Pediatric Multispecialty Center' participating site. One unspecified elective block in each of PGY-3 and PGY-4. MULTI-SITE STRUCTURE IS REAL AND DOCUMENTED. The curriculum page's statement that residents rotate through different hospital systems is corroborated by FREIDA's nine participating institutions, several of which map cleanly onto named rotations: West Gables Rehabilitation Hospital to 'Inpatient Neurology Rehabilitation'; Florida Sleep and Neuro Diagnostic Services to 'Sleep Medicine'; Matthew Kay MD PA-Ophthalmology Office to 'Neuro-Ophthalmology'; Kidz Pediatric Multispecialty Center to 'Pediatric Neurology'; Design Neuroscience Center (the Program Director's own practice) and Advanced Neuroscience Network Physicians-Hialeah to outpatient neurology. Palmetto General Hospital (a 250-average-daily-census Hialeah hospital with 92,270 annual ED visits) and Larkin Community Hospital South Miami supply additional inpatient volume. This rotation-to-site mapping is an inference of correspondence, clearly labelled as such, but every rotation name and every site name is independently sourced. A FACILITY DATA POINT WORTH FLAGGING WITH CARE. FREIDA's institutional record for the primary teaching site, Larkin Community Hospital Palm Springs Campus (institution 119718), reports field_mri=False and field_positron_emission=False, alongside average daily census 83, 7,941 annual admissions and 6,644 annual ED visits. For a neurology residency, an MRI flag of false at the primary teaching site would be significant. I report it as what it is -- a FREIDA institutional facility flag -- and flag that these flags are frequently incomplete and that several participating sites do carry imaging, including Larkin Community Hospital South Miami (institution 119101), which FREIDA records as having both MRI and PET. Confidence on the facility flags themselves is LOW and an applicant should ask the program directly about on-site neuroimaging. WORK ENVIRONMENT. 'Program Start Dates | July 1'. 'Night Float System | Yes' (field_night_float=true) -- this SUPERSEDES the registry's 'Night Float: No', and field_night_float_y1=false indicates night float does not apply in the first year. 'Program Allows Moonlighting (Beyond PGY-1) | No', superseding the registry's 'Yes'. Average hours per week, maximum consecutive hours and 24-hour-off-duty periods all render '--' and are unpublished. Call schedule is 'N/A' for all four years (field_call_schedule four N/A entries), which FREIDA's own legend explains as 'NA = Not Applicable' -- consistent with a night-float model replacing traditional call, though the program does not say so. DIDACTICS: 'Structured Didactic Activities | 4 Hours' per week in PGY-1 (field_avg_hrs_lecture_conf_y1=4), superseding the registry's 5. AMBULATORY MIX: 'Non-Hospital Ambulatory Care | 17%' and 'Hospital Outpatient | N/A'. The registry's 'NGO' for hospital outpatient corresponds to FREIDA's 999 sentinel for Negotiable, correctly noted in the registry's own evidence notes. RESEARCH IS A CLEAR NEGATIVE: 'Research rotation | Not available | Not Offered' (field_research_rotation='Not available', field_research_rotation_duration=0), 'Research track/non-accredited fellowship track | No'. The registry's 'Research Track: No' and 'Research Rotation: Not available' are CONFIRMED. Note that Larkin's GME site does advertise an institution-level 'Department of Research' with Faculty-Scholar and Resident-Scholar pages, but the neurology program itself reports no research rotation and no research track, and I do not attribute institutional research infrastructure to this residency's curriculum. EDUCATIONAL FEATURES -- SIX REGISTRY REVERSALS IN ONE BLOCK. Offered: health systems leadership curriculum, formal interprofessional teamwork program, off-campus electives, and 'Another track | Yes' (field_special_tracks=['Other']) whose content is nowhere described. Not offered, each an explicit 'No' on the current FREIDA page: integrative medicine, INSTRUCTION IN MEDICAL SPANISH OR OTHER NON-ENGLISH LANGUAGE, alternative/complementary medicine, ECONOMICS OF HEALTH CARE SYSTEMS, DEBT MANAGEMENT/FINANCIAL COUNSELING, ACADEMIC SUPPORT FOR USMLE STEP 3 / COMLEX LEVEL 3, INTERNATIONAL EXPERIENCE/GLOBAL HEALTH, RESIDENT/FELLOW RETREATS, hospice/home care, and advanced degree training. The registry recorded 'Yes' for Medical Spanish, Healthcare Economics, Debt Counseling, Step 3 Support, Global Health Experience and Resident Retreats -- all SIX are now 'No'. All tracks are 'No' except the unnamed 'Another track'. EVALUATION: program evaluations use 'Aggregate resident Milestone achievements'; resident evaluation uses 'Patient surveys'.
conflict_notes: Registry 'Night Float: No' versus current FREIDA 'Yes'. Registry 'Moonlighting: Yes' versus 'No'. Registry didactic hours 5 versus 4. And six registry curriculum 'Yes' values - Medical Spanish, Healthcare Economics, Debt Counseling, Step 3 Support, Global Health, Resident Retreats - all now answered 'No' by the program's own 2026-07-21 survey. The registry's curriculum block derives from the 2025-07-16 cycle and is substantially superseded.

program_name: Larkin Community Hospital Palm Springs Campus Program

value.title: A required PGY-2 Movement Disorder rotation, named in the published block schedule
value.student_explanation: The program's own curriculum page lists 'Movement Disorder' as one of seven PGY-2 rotations, alongside Sleep Medicine and Neuro-Ophthalmology. It is a required block rather than an elective, so every resident rotates through it. For someone with existing Parkinson's and movement-disorder exposure this is guaranteed, timetabled contact with the subspecialty in the second year - though be aware the program does not publish who supervises it or where it takes place, and no movement-disorders specialist appears on its faculty list.

value.title: Interviews are conducted virtually, which removes a 1,190-mile trip
value.student_explanation: FREIDA's current record lists this program's applicant interview format as Virtual. Because Hialeah is roughly 1,190 road miles from Houston and Florida is a secondary market rather than a first preference, a virtual interview means this program can be explored at no travel cost and without competing against Texas interview dates. Note this is a change from older data, which listed in-person interviews.

value.title: A genuinely multi-site rotation structure across nine named training locations
value.student_explanation: Rather than training in one building, residents rotate across nine named sites recorded with ACGME: the Palm Springs Campus hospital in Hialeah, Palmetto General Hospital, Larkin Community Hospital in South Miami, North Shore Hospital, West Gables Rehabilitation Hospital, Design Neuroscience Center in Doral, Advanced Neuroscience Network in Hialeah, Florida Sleep and Neuro Diagnostic Services, and a neuro-ophthalmology practice in Aventura. Several map directly onto named rotations, so the variety is structural rather than aspirational. Expect meaningful local travel between sites.

value.title: A dedicated PGY-3 NCV/EMG block and a PGY-4 Epilepsy block, taught by ABPN-subspecialty-certified faculty
value.student_explanation: The schedule sets aside whole blocks for nerve conduction studies and EMG in PGY-3 and for Epilepsy in PGY-4. Two department members hold ABPN certification in Epilepsy (Dr. Carlos Oliu, and Dr. Ramzy Medaa who is also certified in Child Neurology), so the epilepsy block is matched to identifiable expertise. Procedural neurophysiology time like this is not guaranteed at every community program.

value.title: Stroke and neuro-ICU exposure in each of the final three years, with a dual-fellowship-trained vascular neurologist on faculty
value.student_explanation: Inpatient Neurology with ICU and Stroke appears in PGY-2, PGY-3 and PGY-4, so cerebrovascular and neurocritical exposure recurs rather than being a single rotation. Dr. Ritesh Kaushal trained at the University of Chicago in Neurology and then completed two fellowships at St Louis University, in Vascular Neurology and in Endovascular Surgical Neuroradiology - an unusually specific credential for a community program's faculty list.

value.title: A neuro-rehabilitation thread, including a PGY-4 inpatient rehabilitation block and two rehabilitation-fellowship-trained faculty
value.student_explanation: The PGY-4 year includes an Inpatient Neurology Rehabilitation block, West Gables Rehabilitation Hospital is a formal training site, and two department members completed Neurologic Rehabilitation fellowships at University of Miami / Jackson Memorial - the Program Director, Dr. Kester Nedd, and Dr. Bruce Rubin. This is the program's most distinctive and best-supported clinical identity, and it is relevant to movement disorders in that gait, balance and functional recovery are shared ground.

value.title: A department with a clear University of Miami / Jackson Memorial training lineage
value.student_explanation: Three of the eight published department members trained at University of Miami / Jackson Memorial Hospital - the Program Director in both residency and fellowship, Dr. Rubin in fellowship, and Dr. Carlos Oliu in both residency and an epilepsy fellowship. A fourth trained in Neurology at Columbia's Neurological Institute and a fifth at the University of Chicago. That is a specific, checkable mentorship lineage rather than a general claim about faculty quality.

value.title: An in-house multidisciplinary Sleep Medicine fellowship connected to an actual PGY-2 sleep rotation
value.student_explanation: The Palm Springs Campus sponsors an ACGME Sleep Medicine (Multidisciplinary) fellowship, and this residency independently has a PGY-2 Sleep Medicine rotation, advertises a sleep subspecialty clinic and lists a sleep and neurodiagnostic centre as a training site. Multidisciplinary sleep fellowships accept neurology graduates, so this is a real internal progression route. The campus also sponsors Pain Medicine and Addiction Medicine fellowships on the same basis.

value.title: A published five-year graduation window and no gap-experience requirement for current graduates
value.student_explanation: Eligibility requires graduation from medical school within the past five years, which a June 2027 graduate applying in the 2026-2027 cycle satisfies easily. The program's clinical-experience condition applies only to applicants with a gap of a year or more between graduation and residency, so it does not apply to someone entering directly. A Houston away rotation therefore counts as a strengthening credential, not a compliance requirement.

value.title: A named Puerto Rico training tie inside the published department
value.student_explanation: Dr. Odalys Frontela, listed among the program's current department members, completed her internship and Internal Medicine residency at Mayaguez Medical Center in Mayaguez, Puerto Rico. For a Universidad Central del Caribe graduate this is a small but genuine point of shared background in a department of eight, and the only Puerto Rico connection identifiable anywhere in this program. Note she is certified in Internal Medicine rather than Neurology.

summary: Ten student-ready reasons, each tied to a named rotation, a named faculty member with checkable training, a named training site or a published number. The strongest are the required PGY-2 Movement Disorder block, the neuro-rehabilitation thread, virtual interviews and the in-house multidisciplinary Sleep Medicine fellowship.
raw_finding: Each item is anchored to a specific verifiable mechanism: a named rotation block from the program's own published four-year schedule; a named faculty member with a stated residency or fellowship from the program's own faculty page; a named ACGME participating training site from FREIDA's relationship graph; a named fellowship from Larkin's own institutional ACGME program list; or a published number or policy statement from the FREIDA record received 2026-07-21. THE CONTRACT'S BANNED PHRASES WERE ACTIVELY AVOIDED. Nothing here rests on 'diverse patient population', 'strong academics', 'supportive faculty' or 'collegial environment'. In particular the program's own home-page phrase 'rich and diversified clinical experiences' was deliberately NOT converted into a selling point; where variety is claimed (item 3) it is expressed as nine specifically named training sites. ITEMS I CONSIDERED AND DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, because they would have been unsupported or misleading: any Spanish-language or bilingual-training advantage (the program answers 'No' to medical Spanish instruction - domain 24); any multiple sclerosis mentorship (nothing published - domain 17); any research opportunity (FREIDA records no research rotation and no research track); any movement-disorders or MS faculty mentorship (those individuals are published on the SIBLING South Miami program's faculty page, not this one); any board pass rate or graduate placement record (neither is published); any salary or benefits advantage (no salary is published, and disability and mental-health coverage are recorded as Not Available); and any claim about the Hialeah community, which would have rested on demographics. COUNTERWEIGHTS THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THIS LIST IF IT IS SHOWN TO A STUDENT: a passed Step 2 CK is required for interview consideration and review begins at the ERAS release date; no MS training component is published; no movement-disorders faculty member is published despite the rotation; no research rotation or track exists; no salary is published; moonlighting is not permitted; and the program's recent intake shows 0.0% U.S. MD graduates over three years.

(1) HIALEAH'S DEMOGRAPHICS. Hialeah is among the most heavily Spanish-speaking cities in the United States. Governance law 5 forbids inferring Spanish-language training value from city demographics, and the contract names Florida as the place where this temptation is maximal. A city's language profile is a fact about the city, not a curriculum, not a rotation and not a training commitment. Rejected outright. It would have been the easiest and most persuasive-sounding claim in this dossier and it is worth nothing. (2) THE HOSPITAL'S 'LARGELY BILINGUAL' CHARACTERISATION. A secondary encyclopedia source states that the hospital became largely bilingual in Spanish and English, and in Haitian Creole, because of demographic influx. Rejected on three independent grounds: it is a secondary source, not official; it describes the HOSPITAL'S general operating environment rather than the residency's training environment; and its own stated basis is demographic influx, which law 5 excludes. (3) RESIDENT AND FACULTY SURNAMES. The 16-resident roster and the 8-member faculty list contain names that a careless reader would treat as evidence of Spanish-language capability. Governance law 4 forbids inferring anything from a name, and I inferred nothing. No name anywhere in this dossier is used as evidence of language, nationality, ethnicity or immigration status. (4) A PHYSICIAN-DIRECTORY LANGUAGE FIELD FROM THE WRONG PROGRAM. Larkin Health System's neurology service page documents that Dr. Mohan Deochand offers services in 'English, Spanish'. Rejected twice over: he appears on the SIBLING South Miami program's faculty roster and not on this program's, so using him would be cross-program contamination; and in any case an individual physician's directory language field is not a residency curriculum, a formal Medical Spanish program or a documented service. (5) A GENERIC 'DIVERSE PATIENT POPULATION' FRAMING. The program's own home page speaks of 'rich and diversified clinical experiences'. That is boilerplate about case mix, says nothing about language, and is on the contract's banned-phrase list. Rejected. WHAT WOULD HAVE COUNTED, AND DOES NOT EXIST HERE: a named Spanish-language clinical service or clinic; a formal Medical Spanish curriculum or elective; a bilingual training track; a published interpreter-services policy governing the residency; or a documented community partnership tied to this residency. None was found, and the program itself answers No to the closest published question.

summary: No resident or faculty member is identifiable as a Universidad Central del Caribe graduate, and no Puerto Rico medical school is represented on the roster. One department member, Dr. Odalys Frontela, completed her internship and Internal Medicine residency in Mayaguez, Puerto Rico. The program's eligibility wording says 'United States/Canada' without naming Puerto Rico - an ambiguity worth flagging.
raw_finding: UCC AND PUERTO RICO SCHOOL REPRESENTATION: NONE IDENTIFIABLE, AND THE REASON MATTERS. ucc_residents=0 and puerto_rico_school_residents=0 are recorded as zero BECAUSE NO RESIDENT'S MEDICAL SCHOOL IS PUBLISHED AT ALL (domain 12), not because schools were published and UCC was absent. The distinction is important: these zeros mean 'not identifiable', not 'verified none'. All 16 residents are classified UNKNOWN. Governance law 4 was observed throughout - no resident's school, nationality or background was inferred from a name. Likewise no faculty member's medical school is published, so ucc_faculty is empty on the same basis. These are OVERLAY counts and are deliberately NOT added into the five-bucket composition sum in domain 13. THE ONE GENUINE PUERTO RICO TIE. Dr. Odalys Frontela, listed among the eight 'CURRENT DEPARTMENT MEMBERS', has her training recorded verbatim as 'Mayaguez Medical Center - Internship / Residency - Internal Medicine', with certification 'American Board of Internal Medicine'. Mayaguez Medical Center is in Mayaguez, Puerto Rico (410 Hostos Ave, Mayaguez, PR 00680); the ACGME-accredited Internal Medicine program at that facility is the Ramon Betances Hospital-Mayaguez Medical Center / Ponce School of Medicine Consortium. The program's faculty page does NOT state the location, so I verified independently that the name corresponds to a Puerto Rico facility and that no mainland US facility of that name exists; confidence on the location is MEDIUM, on the training claim itself HIGH. Two precise limits on this finding: it is a GRADUATE-TRAINING tie, not a medical-school tie, and her medical school is not published; and she is board-certified in Internal Medicine, not Neurology, so she is unlikely to be a neurology-subspecialty mentor. It remains the only Puerto Rico connection identifiable anywhere in this program, and in a department of eight it is not trivial. THE ELIGIBILITY AMBIGUITY, WHICH THE CONTRACT ASKED TO BE FLAGGED AND WHICH IS PRESENT HERE. The program's own Application Process page defines its first eligibility category verbatim as: 'Graduate of a School of Medicine in the United States/Canada accredited by the Liaison Committee on Graduate Medical Education (LCME).' It says 'United States/Canada' and DOES NOT NAME PUERTO RICO. Universidad Central del Caribe is LCME-accredited and located in a United States territory, so on any correct reading Alejandra falls inside this category and is NOT an IMG requiring ECFMG certification. But the wording leaves room for a screener unfamiliar with Puerto Rico's status to route a UCC application into the third, international category. Two further features of the same sentence compound the concern: the page misnames the accreditor as the 'Liaison Committee on GRADUATE Medical Education' rather than the Liaison Committee on Medical Education, which indicates the eligibility text is not carefully maintained; and no page anywhere on the site clarifies the treatment of U.S. territories. The practical consequence is concrete: Alejandra should state explicitly in her application, and confirm with the coordinator at neurcoordpsc@larkinhospital.com, that Universidad Central del Caribe is an LCME-accredited United States medical school, so that she is assessed under the first category rather than the international one. value.determination: Four independent checks were run and all four point the same way. (1) The program's own admissions page lists Step 2 among application materials as 'Step 2 CK and CS results/scores (if available)' — an explicit conditional, set against '(required)' for Step 1 on the same line. (2) FREIDA's 2026 survey record for this program (field_date_received 2026-06-30) sets field_usmle_step2_req_int = false, i.e. the program answered NO to requiring USMLE Step 2 before an interview; field_comlex_lvl2_req_int is likewise false. (3) field_usmle_step_2_required = false, so Step 2 is not flagged as required for consideration at all; only the separate 'pass' booleans (field_usmle_us_md_pass_ck / field_usmle_img_pass_ck = true) indicate that a passing Step 2 CK is eventually expected. (4) The MHS institutional 'Resident/Fellow Recruitment and Selection' policy (revised May 2026) lists selection criteria including 'Performance on standardized medical, podiatric, or dental knowledge tests' but attaches no examination deadline to screening, interview or ranking, and its eligibility section imposes no Step 2 milestone. No program page, GME page, applicant FAQ or policy PDF anywhere on mhs.net states a date or stage by which Step 2 CK must be reported. Therefore: Step 2 is not required with the ERAS submission, not required before initial review, not required before an interview invitation, and no ranking-stage requirement is published. A passing Step 2 CK is expected of US MD and IMG applicants at some point, most plausibly before appointment, but NO published sentence establishes that stage, so 'before start' is NOT asserted. Critically, the timing conclusion was NOT inferred from the minimum-score rule: 'We do not have a minimum USMLE score' was read as a score statement only and contributes nothing to timing.

Because Puerto Rico is part of the United States and UCC is LCME-accredited, this wording resolves in a UCC graduate's favour and is arguably broader than the common 'LCME-accredited schools in the U.S. and Canada' formulation. The absence of an explicit Puerto Rico reference is recorded as a real, if low-severity, finding — it is the sort of wording that can cause a coordinator to mis-route an application to the IMG pathway. value.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: THE TWO ARE SHARPLY DIFFERENT HERE, AND THE GAP RUNS AGAINST THE RESIDENT. INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY IS REAL AND RECENTLY STRENGTHENED: a named Movement Disorders Program, a fellowship-trained movement disorders neurologist (Casey Young, MD, Mount Sinai movement disorders fellowship completed 2025) hired into the division, an active DBS pathway with neurosurgery, dedicated Parkinson's exercise and therapy rehabilitation programs, and a stated scope covering Huntington's disease, dystonia and Tourette syndrome. DOCUMENTED RESIDENT EXPOSURE IS ESSENTIALLY ABSENT FROM THE PUBLIC RECORD: movement disorders is NOT among the six subspecialty strengths the program names for itself ('vascular neurology, epilepsy, neuroimmunology, neuromuscular disease, headache, and cognitive/behavioral neurology' — the program's own sentence, which omits movement disorders); there is no movement disorders rotation, clinic or elective in the published PGY-1 to PGY-4 grid; Casey Young does not appear on the residency faculty page at all; the Movement Disorders Program page names no residents, fellows or trainees; and the program sponsors no movement disorders fellowship. The honest reading is that a resident here would have institutional access to movement disorders patients and to a fellowship-trained specialist, but the program has published no structured movement disorders training experience. For an applicant whose stated interest is movement disorders this is the single most important gap in this dossier and it should be raised directly with the program.
value.summary: Institutional movement-disorders capability is genuine — a named Movement Disorders Program, a DBS pathway, Parkinson's rehabilitation programs, and a movement-disorders-fellowship-trained neurologist hired in 2025. Documented resident exposure is not: there is no movement disorders rotation, clinic or elective in the published four-year grid, movement disorders is absent from the program's own list of its strengths, and the movement specialist is not on the residency faculty page. No Parkinson's Foundation, HDSA or CurePSP designation exists.

raw_finding: INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY, from pages opened and read: the Memorial Neuroscience Institute 'Programs and Services' list names a 'Movement Disorders Program' alongside the Epilepsy Center, Headache and Migraine Program, Multiple Sclerosis Center, NeuroInterventional Surgery, Neuromuscular Disorders Program, Spine Center and Comprehensive Stroke Center. The Movement Disorders Program page lists conditions treated as Parkinson's disease, essential tremor, dystonia, Huntington's Disease and Tourette syndrome; offers nonsurgical and surgical options including Deep Brain Stimulation; and names three providers — Christopher DeMassi MD (neurosurgery), George Diaz MD and Casey Young MD (Movement Disorder, Neurology). Rehabilitation adjuncts at Memorial Regional Hospital South include a supervised Parkinson's Disease Exercise Program and a Parkinson's Disease Therapy program. Casey Young MD's institutional profile establishes genuine subspecialty training: Mount Sinai Downtown Movement Disorders Fellowship 2025, Columbia University Irving Medical Center neurology residency 2023, John A. Burns School of Medicine 2019, with research on 'genetic Parkinson's Disease, particularly motor and non-motor phenotyping of GBA Parkinson's Disease' and presentations at the Silverstein Foundation Fellow Research Update Meeting (Montreal, June 2025) and the GBA1 Canada Meeting at the Montreal Neurological Institute-Hospital (June 2024). RESIDENT EXPOSURE, searched and not established: the published PGY-1 to PGY-4 rotation grid contains no movement disorders block — PGY-2 is inpatient consult, consult and stroke, ambulatory/specialty clinics, night float, neuroradiology, EEG/EMU and neuro-rehabilitation; PGY-3 is inpatient consult, ambulatory/specialty clinics, neurology ICU, night float, EMG/neuromuscular, EEG/EMU and pediatric neurology; PGY-4 is inpatient consult, consult and stroke, ambulatory/specialty clinics, night float, EEG/EMU, pediatric neurology, neuropathology and three elective blocks. The didactic list (case presentation, CONTINUUM and board review, journal club, basic sciences course, anatomy, EEG workshop, EMG workshop, grand rounds, tumor board/neuro-oncology, stroke case review, neuroscience peer case review M&M, Understanding Healthcare GME course) contains no movement disorders conference. The program's own statement of strengths omits movement disorders entirely: 'The strengths of our program are in the fields of vascular neurology, epilepsy, neuroimmunology, neuromuscular disease, headache, and cognitive/behavioral neurology.' Casey Young is absent from the residency faculty page (lastmod 2026-05-07), consistent with a 2025 fellowship completion and recent hire. FORMAL DESIGNATION — ACTIVELY CHECKED AND NOT FOUND: there is NO Parkinson's Foundation Center of Excellence at Memorial. The Parkinson's Foundation Florida chapter's designated Centers of Excellence are the University of Florida Center for Movement Disorders and Neurorestoration, the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine, and the University of South Florida — three centers, none of them Memorial. No HDSA Center of Excellence and no CurePSP Center of Care claim appears on any Memorial page, and none was found at the awarding bodies. Nothing of the kind is asserted in this dossier. FELLOWSHIP: none, and none inferred from Casey Young's training.

value.dedicated_clinic: Yes — the 'Memorial Neuroscience Institute Multiple Sclerosis Center', a named center within the institute. Its page states it 'offers leading-edge treatments for MS and other neuroimmune disorders' and lists medication therapy management, neuropsychology, rehabilitation, disease-modifying medications, neurorehabilitation, integrative therapies and emotional support. value.resident_elective: Not itemised as an MS block. value.research: The Program Director's own research interests are in MS symptom control and treatment options. FREIDA's 2026 survey sets field_research_rotation = 'Not available' with field_research_rotation_duration = 0, although the program page states 'Our Office of Human Research will assist residents with the development of research projects and submission to the IRB.'
value.formal_designation: The institution states a National MS Society designation. VERBATIM from the Memorial Neuroscience Institute Multiple Sclerosis Center page, fetched and read directly: 'Memorial Neuroscience Institute has been recognized by the National MS Society as a Center for Comprehensive MS Care.' And on the same page: 'As a recognized Center for Comprehensive MS Care, we offer a wide range of treatments, including the latest disease-modifying medications.' AWARDING-BODY CHECK — PARTIAL ONLY, AND STATED AS SUCH: 'Center for Comprehensive MS Care' is the correct name of the National MS Society's top tier under its Partners in MS Care program — the identical phrase is used in designation announcements by UNC Department of Neurology, UC Davis Health, UAB and Hackensack Meridian, which corroborates the naming. HOWEVER, the National MS Society's own site is a JavaScript single-page application that returns only a 2.2 MB shell with no rendered content to non-browser clients, and its partner directory could not be reached; three candidate directory URLs returned 404 or an empty shell. Memorial's specific listing in an NMSS-hosted directory was therefore NOT independently confirmed. The designation is reported as an institutional claim whose wording matches the awarding body's official tier name, with the verification gap named openly rather than papered over.
value.resident_exposure_vs_institutional_capab: CAPABILITY AND RESIDENT EXPOSURE ARE UNUSUALLY WELL ALIGNED HERE, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE MOVEMENT DISORDERS PICTURE AT THE SAME PROGRAM. Institutional capability: a named MS Center with an asserted National MS Society Center for Comprehensive MS Care recognition, disease-modifying therapy, infusion coordination, MS-focused neuropsychology (Jada Santos PsyD) and rehabilitation. The mechanism that connects it to residents is structural rather than inferred: the PROGRAM DIRECTOR HERSELF is the MS and neuroimmunology specialist, so residents are supervised and evaluated by the institution's MS lead, and 'neuroimmunology' is one of only six subspecialty strengths the program names for itself on its welcome page. What is still MISSING, and why this is MODERATE rather than STRONG: no MS or neuroimmunology block appears by name in the published four-year rotation grid; the MS Center page mentions no residents, fellows or trainees; there is no MS or neuroimmunology fellowship; and no resident MS scholarly output is published. So the alignment is real but unquantified — a resident's MS exposure here depends on the ambulatory/specialty clinic assignment and on the PD's own clinic, neither of which is published in detail.
