This distinction reflects the deep expertise of our neurologists, our team-based approach and care based on the latest research and guidelines.' and, earlier on the same page, 'As a recognized Center for Comprehensive MS Care, we offer a wide range of treatments, including the latest disease-modifying medications.' The page headline reads 'At our nationally recognized MS Center, you'll find the latest therapies and compassionate support.' AWARDING-BODY VERIFICATION ATTEMPTED AND PARTIALLY SUCCESSFUL: 'Center for Comprehensive MS Care' is the National MS Society's official top-tier designation name under its Partners in MS Care program, corroborated by the identical phrase appearing in designation announcements from UNC Department of Neurology, UC Davis Health, UAB and Hackensack Meridian Neuroscience Institute. That defeats the brand-string-collision hazard on the NAME. It does NOT confirm Memorial's own listing: nationalmssociety.org is a JavaScript single-page application that served a 2.2 MB shell with zero rendered content, and the candidate directory paths /resources-support/find-a-doctor and /partners-in-ms-care-directory both returned 404. Memorial's presence in an NMSS-hosted directory is therefore UNCONFIRMED and is reported that way. NAMED MS/NEUROIMMUNOLOGY FACULTY: Buse Sengul MD — the PROGRAM DIRECTOR — is the institution's MS and neuroimmunology specialist. Her own profile states 'I am a neurologist and neuroimmunologist at Memorial Neuroscience Institute. I specialize in caring for patients with multiple sclerosis and neuroimmunologic disorders, such as neuromyelitis optica, stiff person syndrome, neurosarcoidosis, acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM) and transverse myelitis.' Training: Dokuz Eylul University 2013, Temple University Hospital neurology residency 2018, University of Florida College of Medicine MS-focused fellowship 2019; awards include two Gordon Multiple Sclerosis Research Awards (Temple, 2017 and 2018). Vineet Nadkarni MD lists 'Neuroimmune diseases: Cares for multiple sclerosis and other diseases that affect how the brain and immune system interact' among his areas of focus. Jada Santos PsyD lists Multiple Sclerosis among her neuropsychology areas of focus. The residency faculty page additionally lists Fawad Yousuf MD as 'Neurohospitalist, Neuroimmunology' with a University of Miami / Jackson Memorial fellowship, but he is absent from the institution's current division cross-links so his present status is uncertain and is flagged rather than asserted. RESIDENT EXPOSURE VS CAPABILITY: the connecting mechanism is that the PD is the MS lead and the program names 'neuroimmunology' as one of six self-declared strengths on its welcome page. Against that, there is no MS or neuroimmunology block by name in the four-year grid, the MS Center page names no trainees, and there is no MS fellowship. MODERATE, not STRONG, for those reasons. NO DESIGNATION WAS INVENTED OR UPGRADED: the Society's tier is reported exactly as the institution words it, and the unverified half is named.

raw_finding: No neurology subspecialty fellowship of any kind is sponsored by Memorial Healthcare System. The complete MHS GME program inventory was enumerated two independent ways — the public 'Residency and Fellowship Programs' index page and a full parse of the 4,164-URL mhs.net sitemap, which yields every GME program directory on the site: allergy and immunology fellowship, anesthesiology residency, cardiac critical care fellowship, cardiovascular disease fellowship, emergency medicine residency, general surgery residency, hematology and medical oncology fellowship, infectious disease fellowship, internal medicine residency, NEUROLOGY RESIDENCY, non-operative pediatric orthopedics, obstetrics and gynecology residency, pediatric cardiology fellowship, pediatrics residency, pharmacy residency (PGY-1 and eight PGY-2 tracks), physical medicine, podiatry residency, psychiatry residency and transitional year residency. There is no vascular neurology, epilepsy, clinical neurophysiology, neuromuscular, neurocritical care, movement disorders, MS/neuroimmunology, headache, sleep or neuro-oncology fellowship. FREIDA's 2026 survey corroborates with field_match_nrmp_adv_fellow = false. NO FELLOWSHIP WAS INFERRED FROM A FACULTY MEMBER'S SPECIALTY — the division contains fellowship-trained epileptologists, vascular neurologists, neuromuscular specialists and a movement disorders specialist, and none of that was allowed to imply a fellowship program exists. Consequence for residents: subspecialty fellowship training must be pursued externally, which the program itself frames as the expectation ('Our program prepares graduating residents to become competitive candidates for fellowship programs or competent general neurologists'), and which the one traceable graduate outcome bears out (a Class of 2025 graduate completed a vascular neurology fellowship at the University of Florida). Additional corroboration: the program's own welcome page frames external fellowship as the pathway — 'Our program prepares graduating residents to become competitive candidates for fellowship programs or competent general neurologists.' And the one traceable graduate outcome confirms the external route in practice: Sydney Oraham, MD, whose institutional provider profile lists 'Residency: Memorial Regional Hospital, 2025, Neurology' followed by 'Fellowships: UF, Office Of The Registar, 2026, Vascular Neurology', completed her subspecialty year at the University of Florida and then returned to Memorial Division of Neurology as a neurohospitalist. NO AFFILIATED FELLOWSHIPS ARE CLAIMED: the program is affiliated with FAU, FIU and Nova Southeastern for undergraduate medical education, but no neurology fellowship at any of those institutions was found to be open to or shared with Memorial residents, and none is asserted as 'affiliated' — the contract's in-house/affiliated distinction is respected by leaving both arrays empty rather than blurring an academic affiliation into fellowship access.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete · Memorial Healthcare System sponsors no neurology subspecialty fellowship. The full GME program inventory was enumerated twice — from the public programs index and from a complete parse of the 4,164-URL mhs.net sitemap — and neurology appears only as the residency. Subspecialty fellowship training would be pursued at another institution.

One placement was reconstructed independently: a Class of 2025 graduate completed a vascular neurology fellowship at the University of Florida in 2026 and is now a neurohospitalist at Memorial.
raw_finding: The alumni page 'Meet Our Neurology Residency Alumni' lists exactly 12 graduates in three labelled classes of four, each with degree and medical school and nothing else — no fellowship, no current position, no city. Class of 2023 being the first graduating class is consistent with FREIDA's field_historical_interview_stats beginning at 2019 (a four-year program whose first PGY-1 cohort entered in 2019 graduates in 2023). NOTABLE COMPOSITION SHIFT, reported as an observation about the program's recruiting history: the 12 alumni include four American University of Antigua graduates, one St. Matthew's University (Grand Cayman) graduate and one International University of the Health Sciences graduate — six offshore-Caribbean graduates out of 12 — plus graduates of Hashemite University, University of Damascus, B.J. Medical College and Universidade Federal da Bahia. Only two of the twelve (Besser, VCOM; Rizvi, LMU-DeBusk) are U.S. DO graduates and none is a U.S. MD graduate. The current 16-person roster is the mirror image: 11 U.S. DO, 3 U.S. MD, 2 non-Caribbean IMG, zero offshore Caribbean. The program's applicant profile has shifted substantially toward U.S. DO graduates, most heavily from its Nova Southeastern affiliate, across roughly six years. TRACEABLE PLACEMENT, with its identity caveat stated openly: the institution's provider directory contains Sydney Oraham, MD, whose profile lists 'Residency: Memorial Regional Hospital, 2025, Neurology', 'Fellowships: UF, Office Of The Registar, 2026, Vascular Neurology', medical education 'American University of Antigua College of Medicine, 2020', and her present role as a Neuro-Hospitalist at Memorial Division of Neurology. The alumni page's Class of 2025 contains no 'Oraham' but does contain 'Sydney Shaffer, MD — American University of Antigua College of Medicine'. Same first name, same medical school, same graduation year from this program — almost certainly the same person under a changed surname. This is reported as a MEDIUM-HIGH identity match rather than as certainty, because the program has not published the connection. The substantive finding stands independently of the name question: a 2025 graduate of THIS program completed a University of Florida vascular neurology fellowship and was then hired by the sponsoring institution. BOARD-STYLE OUTCOMES AND PLACEMENT RATES ARE NOT PUBLISHED and are not estimated here.

summary: Resident salaries run from about $61,755 at PGY-1 to about $69,118 at PGY-4, with 25 days of paid leave that covers vacation, sick time AND holidays combined. An important change from the registry: in the program's 2026 FREIDA survey, health, dental, disability and mental-health coverage are now 'Institution & Resident Share Cost' rather than fully institution-paid; only group life remains fully paid.
raw_finding: SALARY, two official sources with a small discrepancy preserved: the MHS GME Benefits page lists PGY1 $61,755.20, PGY2 $64,688, PGY3 $66,518.40, PGY4 $69,118.40, PGY5 $71,656, plus fellow scales FY1 $75,192, FY2 $78,000, FY3 $80,912. FREIDA's 2026 survey field_graduate_year_statistics gives [{salary 61734, paid_vacation 25}, {64688, 25}, {66518, 25}, {69118, 25}] and field_first_year_salary 61734. PGY-2 through PGY-4 agree to the dollar; PGY-1 differs by $21.20 ($61,755.20 vs $61,734), which is a rounding or effective-date artifact, not a material conflict, and both figures are recorded. The GME Benefits page does NOT state which academic year its table applies to — a real gap — but because the independent FREIDA survey received 2026-06-30 carries the same numbers, the table is treated as current-cycle rather than stale. LEAVE — SEMANTIC CORRECTION TO THE REGISTRY: the benefits page says verbatim 'Paid leave: 25 days (including vacation, sick and holidays)'. The registry stores this as 'Vacation: 25', which a reader will naturally take to mean 25 vacation days. It is not: it is 25 days of ALL paid time off, holidays included. That is a materially worse benefit than 'Vacation: 25' implies and is logged as a SEMANTIC_MISMATCH. FREIDA field_leave_paid = 25 and field_leave_unpaid = 999 — 999 is FREIDA's null/negotiable sentinel, which the registry correctly rendered as 'NGO'; that sentinel behaviour is confirmed here. BENEFITS DOWNGRADE — THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL REGISTRY CORRECTION IN THIS DOSSIER: the registry snapshot (built on the survey received 2025-06-11) records Major medical residents, Major medical dependents, Outpatient mental health, Inpatient mental health, Group life, Dental and Disability ALL as 'Fully Paid by Institution'. The 2026 survey (received 2026-06-30, published 2026-08-20) records field_benefit_major_residents, field_benefit_major_dependents, field_benefit_dental, field_benefit_disability, field_benefit_inpatient_mental and field_benefit_outpatient_mental as 'Institution & Resident Share Cost', with only field_benefit_group_life still 'Fully Paid by Institution'; field_benefit_major_domestic = 'Not Available' and field_benefit_disability_hiv = 'Not Available'. raw_finding: The full block grid and didactic list are published on the program's 'Education' page (sitemap lastmod 2026-07-01) and are quoted verbatim in the value object above. STRUCTURAL OBSERVATIONS THAT MATTER: (1) EEG / epilepsy monitoring unit is the single most heavily weighted subspecialty rotation at 4 blocks (PGY-2 one, PGY-3 two, PGY-4 one), which is coherent with the institution holding an NAEC-verified Level 4 adult epilepsy center; there is also a dedicated 'EEG workshop and review' in the didactic series. (2) Neuromuscular is second at 2 EMG blocks with its own 'EMG workshop and review'. (3) There is NO named movement disorders, MS/neuroimmunology, headache, sleep, cognitive/behavioral or neuro-oncology block; those experiences, if they exist, sit unlabelled inside the 7 ambulatory/specialty clinic blocks or the 3 PGY-4 elective blocks. value.title: An NAEC-verified Level 4 adult epilepsy center, and four resident blocks inside it
value.student_explanation: Memorial Comprehensive Epilepsy Program is listed in the National Association of Epilepsy Centers' own public directory as a 'Level 4 Adult Epilepsy Center' at 3501 Johnson Street, Hollywood — the address of Memorial Regional Hospital. That is the highest NAEC accreditation level, and it was confirmed in NAEC's own listing rather than taken from the hospital's word. The residency puts four 4-week blocks in the EEG / epilepsy monitoring unit across PGY-2 to PGY-4 and runs a dedicated EEG workshop in the didactic series, so this is the one subspecialty where institutional accreditation and resident rotation time line up exactly.

value.title: The Program Director is a fellowship-trained MS neuroimmunologist
value.student_explanation: Buse Sengul, MD completed MS-focused fellowship training at the University of Florida and describes herself as 'a neurologist and neuroimmunologist at Memorial Neuroscience Institute,' treating multiple sclerosis, neuromyelitis optica, stiff person syndrome, neurosarcoidosis, ADEM and transverse myelitis. Her research interests are in MS symptom control and treatment. For someone who wants MS as a career, the person who runs the residency is the person who does the MS. 'Neuroimmunology' is also one of only six subspecialty strengths the program names for itself.

value.title: A Universidad Central del Caribe graduate is on the adult neurology faculty
value.student_explanation: Ana Coronado, MD earned her medical degree at Universidad Central del Caribe in 2017 and did her internal medicine internship at Universidad Central Del Caribe Escuela De Medicina in 2018, then completed neurology residency at Hahnemann and Temple and a headache fellowship at Ohio State. She now practises headache medicine at Memorial Division of Neurology's Weston clinic and is listed on the residency's own faculty page. She is the only UCC-trained faculty member identified at any Florida adult neurology program in this research wave, and she is a concrete person who took the same route out of the same school.

value.title: A second Puerto Rico medical school is represented on the faculty
value.student_explanation: Axel Baez-Lugo, MD earned his medical degree at Ponce Health Sciences University in 2020, completed neurology residency at the Medical College of Georgia in 2024 and a pain medicine fellowship at the University of South Florida in 2025, and practises at Memorial's Pembroke Pines neurology clinic. Two of the eighteen clinicians in this adult neurology division trained at LCME-accredited Puerto Rico medical schools.

value.title: The Associate Program Director speaks Spanish and runs the satellite clinic network
value.student_explanation: George Diaz, MD is Associate Program Director of this residency and simultaneously 'Director, Outpatient Satellite Neurology Clinics.' The institution's own provider directory documents his languages as Spanish and Portuguese. He is board certified in neurology, vascular neurology, neuromuscular medicine, brain injury medicine and clinical neurophysiology, and writes that he 'worked in tele-neurology to improve access to care to patients in areas underserved by neurologists.' He practises at the Miami, Aventura and Hialeah satellite clinics — the outpatient system that the residency's seven ambulatory blocks draw on.

value.title: Seven of eighteen adult neurology clinicians have Spanish documented by the institution
value.student_explanation: Memorial's provider directory publishes a languages field for each clinician. Within Memorial Division of Neurology, Spanish is documented for George Diaz MD, Axel Baez-Lugo MD, Maike Blaya MD, Sean Kenniff MD, Madiley Broz PsyD, Amina Rivero-Barba PsyD and Jada Santos PsyD — seven of eighteen, including the Associate Program Director and all three neuropsychologists. This is the institution's own published record of who speaks Spanish, not an assumption from anyone's name or medical school.

value.title: A single Active categorical NRMP code with no eligibility trap
value.student_explanation: The program's own admissions page states 'NRMP Number: 2085180C0' and 'We offer 4 categorical positions for years PGY1 to PGY4.' The NRMP Program Directory lists that one code as Active and categorical. There is no Advanced track requiring you to separately match a preliminary year, and no 'R' (reserved/physician) code — R positions are reserved for applicants with prior graduate medical education and are not available to senior medical students. FREIDA's 2026 survey confirms it: PGY-1 categorical true, prelim false, PGY-2 advanced false, PGY-2 reserved false, and previous GME not required. One code, one application, no barrier for a graduating senior.

value.title: No minimum USMLE score, and no published Step 2 timing barrier
value.student_explanation: The program states plainly 'We do not have a minimum USMLE score.' Its application-requirements list marks Step 1 as '(required)' but asks for Step 2 results only '(if available)' — and in its 2026 FREIDA survey the program answered No to requiring Step 2 before an interview. If your Step 2 CK result arrives in mid-October, nothing this program has published stands between you and application review or an interview invitation.

value.title: Puerto Rico graduates enter through the U.S. eligibility pathway, with no ECFMG certificate needed
value.student_explanation: The MHS GME 'Resident/Fellow Recruitment and Selection' policy, revised May 2026, sets out its first eligibility pathway as 'Be a graduate of an accredited medical, podiatric, or dental school in the United States or Canada.' Puerto Rico is part of the United States and Universidad Central del Caribe is LCME-accredited, so that pathway applies and the separate ECFMG requirement — which the program limits to 'a graduate of a foreign medical school' — does not. Worth knowing because the policy never names Puerto Rico explicitly, so it is a point to state clearly in your own application materials.

value.title: Six training sites inside ten miles, including a Level 1 trauma center
value.student_explanation: The program page lists Memorial Hospital West, Memorial Regional Hospital, Joe DiMaggio Children's Hospital, Memorial Regional Hospital South, Memorial Miramar Hospital and Memorial Pembroke Hospital, 'all within 10 miles.' FREIDA's institution records show Memorial Regional Hospital at 1,013 beds with an average daily census of 653, 32,611 annual admissions and a Level 1 trauma center designation, and Memorial Hospital West at 486 beds. Multiple sites without long commutes, and case volume that a four-resident-per-year program does not have to share widely.

value.title: Four residents a year and a faculty-to-resident ratio of 0.80:1
value.student_explanation: The program writes that 'Our four resident per year program allows us to get to know each of our residents on a personal level.' FREIDA's 2026 survey puts the full-time faculty-to-resident ratio at 0.80:1 with 13 physician faculty and 2 non-physician faculty against 16 residents. This is a small-cohort program where a resident with a specific subspecialty interest can realistically ask one of thirteen attendings to supervise it.

value.title: A public safety-net system where residents would train, not a rotation elsewhere
value.student_explanation: Memorial Healthcare System is the South Broward Hospital District, a public special taxing district — FREIDA's own institution records name the sites 'Memorial Regional Hospital-South Broward Hospital District' and 'Memorial Hospital West-South Broward Hospital District.' Memorial Regional reported 7,560 Medicaid discharges against 32,611 admissions and 145,461 emergency visits. The admissions page states 'We require 100% of your training to occur at MHS,' so this is where all four years happen rather than a block rotated into.

summary: Twelve verifiable, mechanism-specific reasons, led by an NAEC-verified Level 4 adult epilepsy center matched to four resident EMU blocks, a Program Director who is herself a fellowship-trained MS neuroimmunologist, a Universidad Central del Caribe graduate on the adult neurology faculty, and a single Active categorical NRMP code with no minimum score and no published Step 2 timing barrier.
raw_finding: Each of the twelve items is tied to a named clinic, a named person, a published block count, a quoted policy sentence or a verified external designation. BANNED GENERICS WERE ACTIVELY EXCLUDED: the program's own welcome page supplies 'Great patient diversity and an exciting range of pathology' and 'a learning environment rich with camaraderie', and the admissions page supplies a 'Sunny Lifestyle' feature about South Florida. None of that is used as a reason. Where a claim about cohort size or faculty attention is made, it is anchored to FREIDA's field_ratio_ft_faculty 0.80 and field_total_physician 13 against field_total_positions 16 rather than left as 'supportive faculty'. Items deliberately NOT included because they could not be substantiated: any movement disorders reason (no resident exposure is published — see domain 16); any research reason (FREIDA 2026 sets field_research_rotation = 'Not available'); any in-house fellowship reason (none exist); any board pass rate reason (not published); and any claim about the National MS Society designation being independently confirmed (it is not — see domain 17). The MS reason as written rests on the Program Director's own documented fellowship training and self-description, which is verified, rather than on the unverified Society listing.

value.summary: There is real, documented Spanish-language clinical capacity inside this residency's own training environment: the institution's provider directory publishes a languages field, and Spanish is documented for 7 of the 18 clinicians in Memorial Division of Neurology — including the Associate Program Director of the residency and all three neuropsychologists. Set against that, there is NO formal Medical Spanish curriculum, NO named Spanish-language clinic or service line, and NO bilingual track. Rated MODERATE: a genuinely bilingual clinical workplace with bilingual residency leadership, but no structured Spanish-language training product.
value.raw_finding: WHAT WAS COUNTED, AND WHY IT QUALIFIES. (1) BILINGUAL CLINICAL ENVIRONMENT — the strongest evidence, and it is documentary rather than inferential. Each mhs.net provider profile carries a JSON-LD 'knowsLanguage' property plus a rendered 'Languages' list. Fetching all 18 profiles in Memorial Division of Neurology individually yields Spanish documented for: George Diaz MD (Spanish, Portuguese), Axel Baez-Lugo MD (English, Spanish), Maike Blaya MD (Portuguese, Spanish), Sean Kenniff MD (Spanish, French), Madiley Broz PsyD (Spanish), Amina Rivero-Barba PsyD (Spanish), Jada Santos PsyD (Spanish). That is 7 of 18 (38.9%), and it includes every one of the division's three neuropsychologists — which matters clinically because cognitive and neuropsychological testing is the assessment most degraded by working through an interpreter. (2) THE RESIDENCY LEADERSHIP TIE — this is what lifts the finding above 'the hospital happens to employ Spanish speakers.' George Diaz, MD is the Associate Program Director of THIS residency (his profile headline reads 'Director, Outpatient Satellite Neurology Clinics and Associate Program Director, Memorial Neurology Residency Program'), the institution documents his languages as Spanish and Portuguese, and he directs the outpatient satellite neurology clinic network (Miami, Aventura, Hialeah) that the residency's seven ambulatory/specialty clinic blocks draw on. His own bio states 'I have also worked in tele-neurology to improve access to care to patients in areas underserved by neurologists.' A Spanish-speaking resident would be supervised in ambulatory clinic by a Spanish-speaking associate program director. (3) INTERPRETER SERVICE — institutional, 24/7, and documented in the institution's own words: 'providing foreign language and American Sign Language interpreter services, 24 hours a day'; 'Our interpreters include bilingual employees or volunteers who receive training to serve as medical interpreters'; 'We also use contracted over-the-phone and video interpreter services.' Counted at low weight: it is a patient-services program, not resident training. (4) SAFETY-NET SITE — Memorial Healthcare System is the South Broward Hospital District, a public special taxing district; FREIDA's own institution records name the training sites 'Memorial Regional Hospital-South Broward Hospital District' and 'Memorial Hospital West-South Broward Hospital District'. Memorial Regional reported 7,560 Medicaid discharges of 32,611 admissions and 145,461 annual emergency visits. This is a verifiable governance and payer fact about the training sites, not a demographic inference. WHAT IS ABSENT, STATED PLAINLY. No formal Medical Spanish curriculum: FREIDA's 2026 survey field_resident_fellow_offer_2019 lists six offerings (integrative medicine curriculum; health systems leadership curriculum; interprofessional teamwork program; debt management/financial counseling; USMLE Step 3 academic support; resident/fellow retreats) and does NOT include FREIDA's 'Medical Spanish curriculum' option; independently, the program's own curriculum page and 12-item didactic list contain no Spanish-language element. No named Spanish-language clinic, clinica, or Spanish-language service line exists anywhere in Memorial Neuroscience Institute's published programs. No bilingual track, no Spanish-language proficiency requirement or incentive, and no interpreter-certification pathway for residents. No documented Latino or Hispanic community health programming tied to the neurology residency: MHS's community health programs page lists an Adult Mobile Primary Care Health Center, a Children's Mobile Health Center and Community Care Plan alongside roughly twenty general community offerings (bike safety, CPR certification, health fairs, Safety Town and similar), names no Spanish-language program, and mentions no GME trainee participation.
value.explicitly_rejected_evidence: Five categories of evidence were available and were refused. (1) BROWARD COUNTY AND HOLLYWOOD/HIALEAH DEMOGRAPHICS — refused outright under governance law 5 and contamination guard 7. No population percentage for Broward County, Hollywood, Hialeah, Miami-Dade or South Florida appears anywhere in this dossier as evidence of Spanish-language training value. The temptation was concrete: the Associate Program Director's satellite clinics include a Hialeah site, and it would have been easy to reach for Hialeah's Hispanic population share. That figure is not evidence about this residency and was not used. (2) THE 46% HISPANIC PATIENT-MIX FIGURE FOR SOUTH BROWARD COMMUNITY HEALTH SERVICES — a search result attributed to an MHS Community Health Needs Assessment reports that SBCHS serves a population that is 46% Hispanic with 84% uninsured. Refused for two independent reasons: the source is a 2016-2018 CHNA document and is plainly out of cycle, and more importantly there is NO evidence that neurology residents rotate at SBCHS or on the mobile health centers — the published four-year rotation grid contains no community clinic block, and the admissions page states all training occurs at MHS facilities. A patient-mix statistic for a clinical service the residents do not demonstrably staff is not evidence about their training. (3) SURNAMES — refused under governance law 4. Several division clinicians and residents have Spanish surnames. In particular Ana Coronado MD (a Universidad Central del Caribe graduate practising in Weston) publishes NO language field at all, and Seth Tarras MD and Casey Young MD likewise publish none; for all three, Spanish is recorded as unknown rather than true. It would have been trivially easy, and wrong, to credit Dr Coronado with Spanish on the strength of her name and her medical school. Similarly, no resident's language ability was inferred from a name — the program publishes no resident language data at all. (4) GENERIC DIVERSITY LANGUAGE — the program's own welcome page says 'Great patient diversity and an exciting range of pathology' and the interpreter services page says Memorial 'is located within a vibrant multicultural community in South Florida.' Neither is evidence of Spanish-language clinical training and neither was counted toward strength; the interpreter page was counted only for its concrete operational statements about 24-hour service and trained bilingual staff interpreters. (5) A LANGUAGE FILTER ON THE PUBLIC 'FIND A DOCTOR' SEARCH — the institution's provider search offers a languages filter, which could have been used to generate a system-wide count of Spanish-speaking physicians across all of Memorial Healthcare System. That number would describe a 4,000-plus-employee multi-hospital system, not a neurology residency, so the count was deliberately restricted to the 18 clinicians of Memorial Division of Neurology, each profile opened individually.

raw_finding: SEARCHED: the full resident roster (16 named, all with medical schools), the full alumni roster (12 named across classes of 2023-2025, all with medical schools), the residency faculty page in its entirety across all seven teaching departments, all 18 adult neurology provider profiles individually, and the leadership records in FREIDA. RESIDENTS AND ALUMNI: zero Puerto Rico school graduates among the 16 current residents and zero among the 12 published alumni — no Universidad Central del Caribe, no Ponce Health Sciences University, no University of Puerto Rico, no San Juan Bautista. FACULTY — THE STRONGEST FINDING IN THIS DOMAIN: Ana Coronado, MD is a Universidad Central del Caribe graduate (2017) who ALSO completed her internal medicine internship at Universidad Central Del Caribe Escuela De Medicina (2018), establishing a deeper institutional tie than a degree alone. She is a practising adult neurologist and headache specialist at Memorial Division of Neurology's Weston clinic, and — importantly for an applicant — she is listed on the residency's OWN faculty page under Neurology, not merely somewhere in the hospital. raw_finding:
NO NAMED ROSTER EXISTS PUBLICLY. Searched: (a) https://palmettogeneral.org/graduate-medical-education-program/ - HTTP 200, renders the heading 'Graduate Medical Education' and nothing else; the sibling 'Pharmacy Residency' page is equally empty. (b) The URL the program gives ERAS 2027 applicants, www.palmettogeneral.org/about-us/graduate-medical-education-program/neurology-residency - HTTP 404. (c) pghgme.com, the former 'Palmetto Graduate Medical Education' site - live fetches refused (ECONNREFUSED 154.220.19.201:443); Wayback CDX for the whole domain shows content captures only through 2021, 301s through 2024, and 2025 captures that are a bare redirect to /lander, i.e. domain parking. The CDX index for the entire domain contains NO resident-roster URL at any point in its history (pages captured: home, medical-education-programs and eight program subpages, about-palmetto-general-hospital, about-south-florida, new-applicants, contact-us, policy pages) - so this program appears never to have published a roster. (d) palmettogeneral.org/wp-json/wp/v2/pages - HTTP 403, a genuine access boundary on the WordPress REST API that would otherwise have enumerated every page. (e) Nova Southeastern University KPCOM's affiliated-programs page lists Palmetto General's postgraduate programs and program directors but no residents. (f) An apparently program-run account @PGHneurology exists on X; fetching it returned HTTP 403 (platform access boundary), so nothing from it is used. (g) No named individuals were sought or taken from name-based inference of any kind.

COMPLEMENT VS CENSUS, kept separate as the contract requires. APPROVED COMPLEMENT: FREIDA 2026 field_total_positions = 8 and field_program_size = [2, 2, 2, 2]; field_first_year_positions = 2. The registry's 'Total Residents: 8' is this complement, not a head-count - the classic COMPLEMENT_VS_CENSUS defect. DERIVED CENSUS: FREIDA's 2026 self-reported resident characteristics are field_pct_female = '33.3', field_pct_male = '66.7', field_pct_do = '50.0', field_pct_img = '50.0', field_pct_usmd = '0.0'. A denominator of 6 resolves all four exactly (2 female / 4 male; 3 DO / 3 IMG); 8 does not resolve 33.3/66.7 at all. This is corroborated by the registry's per-year head-counts 'Current Residents PGY1: 2; Current Residents PGY2: 2; Current Residents PGY3: 2' with no PGY4 row, which also sums to 6 and is consistent with a program that only moved from 1 to 2 positions per year in the 2025 Match (NRMP: quota 1 in 2021-2024, quota 2 in 2025 and 2026). So the census estimate of 6 is arithmetically and historically coherent - but it is DERIVED, not published, and could also be 3 or 12 on the percentages alone. It is not a roster and is not presented as one.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - the program does not publicly list a current named resident roster, and its residency website is offline, so there is no page on which one could appear. The approved complement is 8 positions; the current head-count appears to be about 6, derived from the program's own FREIDA survey percentages rather than from a published list.

summary: Against a derived census of 6, the five buckets are 0 US MD, 3 US DO, 0 Caribbean, 0 other IMG and 3 unknown, summing exactly to 6. The three international graduates FREIDA reports are held in 'unknown' rather than assigned to a bucket, because no school names are published and 'IMG' alone cannot distinguish an offshore for-profit Caribbean school from any other international school.
raw_finding:
DENOMINATOR. Two candidate denominators exist and are deliberately kept apart. APPROVED COMPLEMENT = 8 (FREIDA field_total_positions = 8; field_program_size = [2,2,2,2]); this is what the registry stores in 'Total Residents: 8' and it is NOT used as the roster denominator, per contamination guard 3. ACTUAL CENSUS = 6, derived: FREIDA's 2026 self-reported percentages field_pct_female '33.3' / field_pct_male '66.7' and field_pct_do '50.0' / field_pct_img '50.0' / field_pct_usmd '0.0' all resolve exactly at n = 6 (2 female, 4 male, 3 DO, 3 IMG) and 33.3/66.7 cannot be produced by n = 8 at all; the registry's per-year counts PGY1 2, PGY2 2, PGY3 2 with no PGY4 row sum independently to 6; and NRMP program results show a quota of 1 per year for appointment years 2021-2024 rising to 2 for 2025 and 2026, which is exactly the history that yields a partially-filled 8-line complement. The census is therefore reported as 6 with status PARTIALLY_VERIFIED and an explicit statement that it is derived, not published.

BUCKETS. us_md = 0 (FREIDA field_pct_usmd = '0.0'). us_do = 3 (50.0% of 6). caribbean = 0 and other_img = 0: FREIDA reports 50.0% IMG, i.e. 3 people, but 'IMG' in FREIDA means only 'medical school outside the US and Canada'. Assigning those 3 to OTHER_IMG would affirmatively assert that none attended an offshore for-profit Caribbean school, and assigning them to CARIBBEAN would assert the reverse; neither is established, because no school names are published anywhere. Per the contract's rule against converting an unknown into an affirmative answer, all 3 are placed in `unknown`. unknown = 3. Sum 0 + 3 + 0 + 0 + 3 = 6 = denominator. PASS.

PUERTO RICO OVERLAYS. ucc_residents = 0 and puerto_rico_school_residents = 0 mean 'none identified', not 'none exist' - with no roster and no school list, a UCC, Ponce, UPR or San Juan Bautista graduate in this cohort could not be detected. These are overlay counts and are excluded from the five-bucket sum. For the record, and because it governs how any future finding must be coded: graduates of Universidad Central del Caribe, Ponce Health Sciences University, University of Puerto Rico and San Juan Bautista are graduates of LCME-accredited UNITED STATES MD schools and belong in us_md - never in caribbean and never in other_img. 'CARIBBEAN' in this schema denotes offshore for-profit schools such as Ross, St George's, AUC, Saba, Texila and Windsor. FREIDA's institution-level medical-school relationships for Palmetto General are four osteopathic schools (Pacific Northwest University, Midwestern Arizona, Kansas City University, West Virginia SOM) with no Puerto Rico school among them.

OTHER REPORTED CHARACTERISTICS. Gender: 33.3% female / 66.7% male (2026 cycle), against 50.0% / 50.0% in the 2025 cycle - a shift consistent with a small cohort turning over. No identity characteristic was inferred from any name.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - because the program publishes no resident roster and no list of resident medical schools, three of its six residents are recorded as 'unknown' school type rather than being assigned to a category. The program reports 0% US MD graduates in its current cohort.

raw_finding:
PROGRAM DIRECTOR. FREIDA's survey record for 1801100160 (field_date_received 2026-07-21) embeds a paragraph--program_individual with parent_field_name 'field_program_director': field_first_name 'Ariol', field_last_name 'Labrada', field_degrees 'MD', field_email 'ariol.labrada@hsahospitals.com', field_phone '3058235000', address 'Med Education Dept Ste 311, 2001 W 68th St, Hialeah FL 33016-1801, Palmetto General Hospital'. Independently corroborated twice: NRMP's public program directory page for 2121180C0 lists 'Program Director: Ariol Labrada'; and Nova Southeastern University KPCOM's affiliated-programs page, under 'Palmetto General Hospital - Hialeah, FL', lists 'Neurology PD: Ariol Labrada, MD' alongside Family Medicine (PD Peter Cohen, DO), Internal Medicine (PD Anais Cortes, MD), Cardiology (Raul Alonso, MD), Critical Care Medicine (Alex Morizio, MD), Infectious Diseases (Ann MacIntyre, DO, MHS) and Interventional Cardiology (Miguel Diaz, MD). The hsahospitals.com address is itself evidence that GME administration has migrated to the current operator, Healthcare Systems of America.

PROGRAM CONTACT. FREIDA paragraph with parent_field_name 'field_program_contact': 'Tangela' 'Tarver-Matthews', phone 3058235000 ext 7761, e-mail 'labra40@gmail.com' as recorded in the 2026 survey (a personal-domain address, reproduced as found); the same individual appears on the sibling Vascular Neurology fellowship record with the institutional address tangela.tarver@hsahospitals.com. Two older coordinator identities recur in third-party caches and are recorded only to date the sources that carry them: 'Carol Siu, carol.siu@tenethealth.com' (Tenet era, on the 2020 archived program page) and 'Francesca A Villanueva, francesca.villanueva@steward.org' (Steward era).

ASSOCIATE PROGRAM DIRECTORS. None named. Searched the registry-listed program website (empty), the ERAS-listed program URL (404), the archived pghgme.com program page and block-schedule PDF, FREIDA's full survey, NRMP's directory and the Nova KPCOM page. FREIDA exposes only a program-director and a program-contact slot and both are filled as above. Status for this sub-section is RESEARCHED_NOT_PUBLIC.

TRAINING HISTORY AND A CONTAMINATION HAZARD HANDLED IN THE OPEN. The only prose biography of Dr Labrada I could open sits on https://www.graduatemedicaleducation.org/our-faculty-neurology/ - the GME site of LARKIN COMMUNITY HOSPITAL, a different institution whose two neurology programs (1801100158 Palm Springs Campus, Hialeah; 1801100156 South Miami) are explicitly out of scope for this dossier. That page lists, under the heading 'CURRENT DEPARTMENT MEMBERS', both 'Ariol Labrada, M.D.' and 'Roberto Sanchez, M.D.' - i.e. the two physicians FREIDA records as Palmetto General's neurology program director and vascular neurology fellowship director are simultaneously presented as current Larkin neurology department members. I verified that neither man is Larkin's program director: FREIDA gives Larkin Palm Springs Campus PD as Kester Nedd, DO and Larkin South Miami PD as Wilson Cueva, MD. The most likely explanation is concurrent hospital appointments, which are ordinary in South Florida community neurology; a migration away from Palmetto cannot be excluded, but it is contradicted by the 2026-07-21 FREIDA survey carrying Labrada at an hsahospitals.com address. I have used the Larkin page ONLY for the personal training history of named individuals - a property of the person, not of the program - and have imported NO Larkin curriculum, roster, faculty-count, subspecialty or designation content into this dossier. Labrada, per that page: 'board-certified neurologist with subspecialty training in vascular neurology and neurocritical care. He completed one year of internal medicine and three years of neurology residency training at Louisiana State University Health Sciences Center, where he was selected as Chief Resident and recognized as Neurocritical Care Resident of the Year. Dr. Labrada completed a vascular neurology fellowship at the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine. Dr. Labrada is board-certified in general neurology, vascular neurology, and neurocritical care.' He therefore did NOT train at Palmetto General. No medical school is stated for him on any source I opened. No Puerto Rico tie was found for any member of leadership.

Both sources are credible and recent. Concurrent appointment is the most probable reconciliation; the possibility that one or both have moved to Larkin cannot be excluded from public evidence. No Larkin program content was imported. Larkin's own program directors are different people (Kester Nedd, DO at Palm Springs Campus; Wilson Cueva, MD at South Miami), verified in FREIDA.

raw_finding:
NO ROSTER. Searched the registry-listed program website (renders the heading 'Graduate Medical Education' and nothing else), the ERAS-listed program URL (HTTP 404), the whole Wayback history of pghgme.com (the domain's CDX index contains no faculty page at any point - only home, medical-education-programs plus eight program subpages, about-palmetto-general-hospital, about-south-florida, new-applicants, contact-us and policy pages), the palmettogeneral.org WordPress REST API (HTTP 403), NRMP's program directory and FREIDA's 210-field survey. No complete core-faculty list has ever been published by this program as far as the public record goes.

FACULTY COUNT CONFLICT, PRESERVED. FREIDA survey received 2026-07-21: field_total_physician = 1, field_total_non_physician = 0, field_part_time_paid_physicians = 0, field_part_time_paid_non_physicians = 0, field_ratio_ft_faculty = '0.10', field_pct_ft_female = '0.00'. The rise registry snapshot from the survey received 2025-07-16: 'Program Faculty Count: 5', 'Faculty Distribution: Physicians: 5; non-physicians: 2', 'Faculty Resident Ratio: 0.60:1', 'Female Faculty Percent: 0.00%'. One full-time physician faculty member against an eight-position, four-year neurology residency would be an extraordinary figure, and a 0.10 faculty-to-resident ratio is at the extreme low end of anything FREIDA reports; the 2025 figures are far more plausible for a programme of this size. Two readings are available and neither can be eliminated from public evidence: (a) a survey data-entry artifact in one of the two cycles, or (b) a genuine contraction of paid faculty during the ownership transition described in domain 1, in which a key vendor said the operator was 'significantly behind in payments' and the anesthesia group TeamHealth withdrew for nonpayment. Both are recorded; neither is asserted. Note also that the registry's 'Program Faculty Count: 5' is NOT the FREIDA-null-sentinel-as-zero defect warned about in the contract - here the suspect value is the 2026 '1', and the direction of the anomaly is the reverse of the Texas pattern.

INDIVIDUALLY IDENTIFIED TEACHING PHYSICIANS (three, none from a faculty page). (1) Ariol Labrada, MD - program director, FREIDA 2026, ariol.labrada@hsahospitals.com; training history from a cross-institution source, see domain 14 conflict_notes. (2) Roberto Sanchez (Sanchez Perez), MD - program director of Palmetto General's own ACGME Vascular Neurology fellowship, per FREIDA's 2026 survey for 1881118001; physician directories give his medical school as Instituto Superior de Ciencias Medicas de Villa Clara (1992), a neurology residency 2006-2009 and a vascular neurology fellowship at University of Miami / Jackson Health System 2009-2010, an office at 2001 W 68th St (the hospital address), and English and Spanish; those directory attributes are SECONDARY and are reported at LOW confidence. (3) Jose Simon Canellas, MD - named in the program's own block-schedule PDF as the attending whose private office hosts the residents' continuity clinic; directories describe him as board-certified in neurology and clinical neurophysiology with epilepsy and headache experience, affiliated with Palmetto General among other hospitals, and speaking Spanish, French and English (again SECONDARY, LOW confidence). CONTAMINATION NOTE: Larkin Community Hospital's neurology faculty page carries a longer roster including Wilson Cueva MD, Pamela Youssef MD and Adam Nassery MD; NONE of those individuals are imported here, and Larkin's faculty count is not used to fill Palmetto's gap.

There is no dedicated movement-disorders clinic, no named movement-disorders faculty member, no fellowship and no formal designation of any kind.
raw_finding:
WHAT WAS FOUND. The program's own 'Neurology Residency Block Schedule' PDF (filename Neurology-Block-Diagram-3.12.20.pdf, i.e. dated 12 March 2020, retrieved from the Wayback capture of pghgme.com) contains this elective list verbatim: 'For rotations listed as "Elective" on the block schedule, residents may select from a list of clinical experiences on either the inpatient or outpatient setting. Elective options include: EEG, EMG, Psychiatry, Pediatric Neurology, Neuroimaging, Neurosurgery, Neuroopthalmology, Pain Management, Neuropathology, Neuromuscular, Infectious Disease, NICU, Neurogenetics, Neuropsychology, Interventional Neurology, Sleep Disorders Clinic, Movement Clinic and Vascular Clinic.' The identical list appears in the archived FAQ on the program's own page. 'Movement Clinic' is therefore a program-published elective option, with elective blocks concentrated in PGY-3 (blocks 8 and 11 on the grid) and PGY-4 (blocks 9, 10 and 11). That is the whole of the affirmative evidence.

RESIDENT EXPOSURE VERSUS INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY - kept separate as the contract demands. INSTITUTIONAL CAPABILITY: Palmetto General's live neurology service page describes only cerebrovascular and neurosurgical capability - 'BrainPath', 'Stroke Treatment', 'Endovascular Neurosurgery', Comprehensive Stroke Center - and does not mention movement disorders, Parkinson's disease, deep brain stimulation, botulinum toxin clinics or a neuromodulation programme. The archived FAQ does list botulinum toxin among resident procedures, but only in the context of 'Botox for chronic migraine', which is a headache indication, not a movement-disorders one. The institution's ACGME programme portfolio (verified through FREIDA's institution API for ID 119676: Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Cardiovascular Disease, Critical Care Medicine, Infectious Disease, Interventional Cardiology, Neurology, Vascular Neurology - eight programmes, no more) contains no movement-disorders fellowship. RESIDENT EXPOSURE: a one-month elective in a 'Movement Clinic', available in PGY-3/PGY-4, selectable but not required, described in a document six years old whose host site is now a parked domain. PRIMARY SOURCE. The program's own 'Neurology Residency Block Schedule' PDF (Neurology-Block-Diagram-3.12.20.pdf, dated 12 March 2020) gives a complete 12-block grid for each of PGY-1 through PGY-4 with per-block percent-outpatient and percent-research annotations, plus prose sections 'Program Overview', 'Program Participating Sites', 'Required Rotations' and 'Electives'. Verbatim from Program Overview: 'The Neurology Medicine Program is primarily located at Palmetto General Hospital in Hialeah Florida. Each rotation is 1 month (4 weeks) in length over four years, with one year being primarily Internal Medicine. Throughout the duration of the program, residents will complete one half-day a week of continuity clinic experience thus exposing them to a diverse patient panel. Residents will complete at least 40 half day sessions of continuity clinic per year throughout their training and be immersed in several disciplines of Neurology.' Verbatim from Participating Sites: '1- Palmetto General Hospital - Inpatient Neurology, Neuro Consult, Outpatient Neurology, Neuro ICU, Adult Emergency Medicine, Electroencephalography (EEG), Electromyography (EMG), Clinical Psychiatry, Neuroimaging. 2- Kidz Medical Services - Pediatric Neurology.' Verbatim from Required Rotations: 'During the first year of the program, Neurology residents will work with an Internal Medicine attending primarily, with exposure in emergency medicine... Palmetto General Hospital's Neurology attending will be the primary care provider when neurology-related patients arrive to the Hospital. The resident will work alongside the attending and his/her team for admission, discharge, writing orders, and follow up... For Neuro consults, the attending and resident will provide guidance to other primary services separate from the inpatient neurology patients on their service. Continuity Clinic will occur at the clinical office of Dr. Jose Simon Canellas at Simon, MD, PA.' The PGY-2 block 7 and PGY-3 block 6 and PGY-4 block 5 entries are 'Peds Neuro' at SITE 2, i.e. the Kidz Medical Services rotation - a PEDIATRIC NEUROLOGY ROTATION INSIDE AN ADULT PROGRAM, which is legitimate adult-curriculum data and is not Child Neurology programme content.

SUPPORTING PROGRAM FAQ (pghgme.com, archived 2020-08-06), verbatim highlights: 'The PGY-1 schedule is an intensive year that is focused on inpatient medicine as this is the foundation for neurology. The PGY-1 year will consist of 7 inpatient medicine blocks, 3 inpatient neurology blocks, and emergency medicine block, and an elective block. In addition, there is one half-day of neurology continuity clinic per week.' 'Do I apply to the internal medicine program for the PGY-1 year or the neurology program? You only need to submit one application for the Neurology program. This application serves for the four years of training.' 'Each PGY2-4 year will be on a monthly block schedule, with 12 blocks per academic year... In addition to inpatient and outpatient neurology there are blocks for: pediatric neurology, neuro-imaging, EEG, clinical psychiatry, research, and neurosurgery. PGY 3 and PGY 4 residents will have more elective blocks so that they may fine tune their training for their specific interests and potential fellowship.' 'Where is the clinic located? The clinic is outside of the hospital and located in Miami.' 'Due to the space limitations of the clinic, no more than one resident per day will be scheduled at a time.' 'Residents on inpatient rotations will be on call every 3-4 days of the block. Residents will not be on call on their continuity clinic days. On call days, residents will be expected to be at the hospital from 7a to 7p and will take all code strokes, new consults, and pages.' 'Is there a night float? The program currently does not have a night float as there are not enough residents for this coverage. However, residents may be expected to have night call once there are enough residents to cover the service.' 'Yes, Residents will have opportunity to perform procedures such as central lines, lumbar punctures, arterial lines, nerve conduction studies, EMG, Botox for chronic migraine, steroid infiltration, and others.' 'Residents participate in monthly grand rounds held through the advanced neuroscience network.' 'All PGH residents are provided with the New Innovations system for easy logging and tracking of their duty hours, procedures, scholarly activity, continuity clinic patients, conferences, and more.' 'Yes. Residents are expected to participate in scholarly activity throughout their residency. This includes morning report lectures, didactic lectures, leading grand rounds, presenting at the PGH research symposium, presenting at local, regional, and national conferences, getting a case report, research, or article published, among others.'

value.title: An in-house ACGME Vascular Neurology fellowship at the same sponsoring institution
value.student_explanation: Palmetto General sponsors its own ACGME-accredited Vascular Neurology fellowship (ACGME 1881118001, one position, program director Roberto Sanchez, MD), which filed a current FREIDA survey on 2026-07-21 and is accepting applicants. A resident here trains inside an institution that also trains a stroke fellow, which is unusual for a community program of this size and gives you an internal pathway if stroke becomes your direction.

value.title: Six consecutive fully-matched years in the NRMP Main Match
value.student_explanation: NRMP's published program-level results show this program offered and filled every position it had in six straight appointment years: 1 of 1 in 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024, then 2 of 2 in 2025 and 2 of 2 in 2026. For a small community program that came through two ownership changes and a parent-company bankruptcy in that same window, an unbroken fill record is a concrete stability signal.

value.title: Categorical four-year appointment on a single application
value.student_explanation: The NRMP code is 2121180C0 - a C, meaning categorical. You apply once and the appointment covers all four years including the PGY-1 internal medicine year at the same hospital. The program's own FAQ says it directly: 'You only need to submit one application for the Neurology program. This application serves for the four years of training.' There is no Advanced or Reserved code here, so you do not have to separately match a preliminary year and you are not caught by NRMP's rule that Reserved positions are not available to senior medical students.

value.title: One-to-one teaching by design, in the program's own words
value.student_explanation: In its 2026 FREIDA survey the program describes itself as providing 'an excellent one-to-one teaching experience while in service at the hospital or clinics.' That is structurally credible rather than just a slogan: with two residents per year and a single continuity clinic that schedules no more than one resident per day, you are rarely competing for procedures, consults or attending attention.

value.title: High-acuity stroke volume at a certified Comprehensive Stroke Center, with code-stroke responsibility as a resident
value.student_explanation: The hospital's neurology page states it 'is a Comprehensive Stroke Center' certified by The Joint Commission and the AHA/ASA, and lists endovascular neurosurgery and a 'BrainPath' subcortical approach among its services. The program's FAQ puts residents at the front of that work: on call you 'take all code strokes, new consults, and pages' from 7am to 7pm. Verify the certification's current status with the program, because the hospital's page also contains dated phrasing from an earlier ownership era.

value.title: A required 8-week research rotation and a named research outlet
value.student_explanation: FREIDA records the research rotation as 'Required' with a duration of 8 weeks, and the block grid shows dedicated research blocks in PGY-2 and PGY-4 marked 100% research. The program also names its own venue: residents are expected to present at 'the PGH research symposium' as well as at local, regional and national conferences. Protected research time is written into the schedule rather than left to be negotiated.

value.title: Elective-heavy senior years, including a 'Movement Clinic' elective
value.student_explanation: The program's block schedule gives PGY-3 two and PGY-4 three elective blocks, and says PGY-3 and PGY-4 residents 'will have more elective blocks so that they may fine tune their training for their specific interests and potential fellowship.' The published elective list includes a 'Movement Clinic' and a 'Vascular Clinic' alongside EEG, EMG, neuro-ophthalmology, neuromuscular, sleep and interventional neurology. For a movement-disorders interest this is the one available lever - but it is one elective line in a 2020 document, not a movement-disorders program, and you should ask whether the Movement Clinic elective still runs.

value.title: A documented graduate placement into a Weill Cornell subspecialty fellowship
value.student_explanation: A 2024 graduate of this residency, who served as its chief resident, completed a neuro-ophthalmology fellowship at Weill Cornell Medicine in 2025 and is now on faculty at Hackensack Meridian Health - documented on his employer's own provider profile. One graduate is not a placement rate, but it establishes that a resident from this program has cleared a competitive academic subspecialty bar.

value.title: No required away rotation, no supplemental application, and an explicit no-score-cutoff stance
value.student_explanation: FREIDA records no required away rotation and no supplemental ERAS application for the next cycle, and the program's own FAQ states 'We do not have a certain cutoff for scores in regards to Board exams' and that applicants who did not pass on the first attempt are 'not excluded', with each application 'evaluated on an individual basis'. That is a low-friction application and a stated whole-file review, which matters when a Step 2 CK result will land in mid-October.

value.title: Interview odds that are unusually favourable for the specialty
value.student_explanation: The program reports 15 interviews conducted for 2 first-year positions in the most recent cycle - roughly 7.5 interviews per position, where competitive neurology programs commonly run many times that. If you receive an interview here, the conditional odds are materially better than at a large academic department.

value.student_explanation: Rather than leaving breadth to chance, the block schedule assigns pediatric neurology to a named second site, Kidz Medical Services, in PGY-2, PGY-3 and PGY-4, and schedules a clinical psychiatry block in PGY-3. Those are ACGME-required neurology competencies delivered through identified rotations rather than as ad hoc coverage.

summary: Eleven student-ready reasons, each tied to a specific named mechanism: an in-house ACGME stroke fellowship, six straight fully-filled Match years, a categorical single-application appointment, a required 8-week research rotation, elective-heavy senior years including a Movement Clinic elective, roughly 7.5 interviews per position, and one documented graduate placed into a Weill Cornell fellowship. Every item names a clinic, code, number, rotation or document.
raw_finding: Each item above is anchored to a specific verifiable mechanism - an ACGME ID, an NRMP code, a published quota-and-fill row, a survey field, a named rotation site, a named symposium, or a named individual's employer-published profile. Banned generic language ('diverse patient population', 'strong academics', 'supportive faculty', 'collegial environment') was deliberately avoided; note in particular that the program's own FREIDA free text offers 'An extensive population to learn from, with a very diverse range of neurological diseases', and that phrase was NOT promoted into a reason for exactly that reason. The honest counterweights a student must hear alongside these eleven items are carried in alejandra_rationale and difficulty_notes: no working program website, no published roster or faculty list, contradictory faculty counts between survey cycles, a for-profit operator under documented financial strain, no MS training pathway, and a PGY-1 that is seven-twelfths internal medicine.

program_name: Palmetto General Hospital Program
summary: There is no formal Medical Spanish curriculum and no bilingual track - the program itself answers 'no' to FREIDA's Medical Spanish question in both survey cycles. What can be documented is weaker and indirect: a hospital-wide free interpreter service, a safety-net patient mix, and a residency continuity clinic run out of the private office of a named Spanish-speaking neurologist. None of the city's demographics were counted as evidence.
raw_finding:
WHAT WAS ACCEPTED, AND HOW WEAK IT IS. (1) FORMAL MEDICAL SPANISH - ABSENT, on the program's own answer. FREIDA's offering list (field_resident_fellow_offer_2019) for the survey received 2026-07-21 contains exactly four items - integrative medicine curriculum, health systems leadership curriculum, academic support for USMLE Step 3 preparation, off-campus electives - and Medical Spanish, which is a selectable FREIDA option, is not among them. The registry's 'Medical Spanish Curriculum: No' is therefore CONFIRMED from the program's own survey response in two consecutive cycles rather than inherited from the registry, which is the verification the contract demands after the Texas defect rate. (2) INTERPRETER_SERVICE - documented but institutional and ADA-framed. https://palmettogeneral.org/interpreter-language-services/ states verbatim: 'To ensure effective communication with patients and their companions who are non-English speaking or speak Limited English, are deaf or hard-of-hearing, and/or are blind or vision impaired, this hospital provides interpreter services, sign language interpreting services, text telephones (TTY), and other aids and services. These services are provided by the hospital free of charge. For assistance, please ask your nurse or other hospital personnel.' The named contact is Michele Thoman, MBA, BSN, RN, NEA-BC. This is real and it is at the training site, so residents work inside a hospital with free interpreting - but it names no language, is written as ADA/Section-1557 compliance, and says nothing about resident education. It is counted at the lowest possible weight. (3) BILINGUAL_CLINICAL_ENVIRONMENT - one named, residency-tied clinical site. The program's own block-schedule PDF states 'Continuity Clinic will occur at the clinical office of Dr. Jose Simon Canellas at Simon, MD, PA', and the FAQ adds that this clinic 'is outside of the hospital and located in Miami' and schedules 'no more than one resident per day'. Physician directories describe Dr Simon Canellas as fluent in Spanish, French and English; that language attribution is SECONDARY-source and is why this whole domain sits at PARTIALLY_VERIFIED rather than VERIFIED. The same directories describe the vascular neurology fellowship director, Roberto Sanchez Perez, MD, as speaking English and Spanish, and the Hackensack Meridian faculty profile of the program's own 2024 graduate lists his languages as 'English and Spanish' - that last one is an official institutional page, and it is a graduate rather than faculty, so it evidences the training environment only obliquely. (4) SAFETY_NET_SITE - Palmetto General is characterised in a hospital-ratings index as a '200-399 bed acute care safety net for-profit urban hospital', and FREIDA's institution record reports 5,170 Medicaid discharges and 92,270 annual emergency department visits against 360 beds. A high-Medicaid, high-ED-volume community hospital is a safety-net training environment; that is a real structural fact about the patient population, and it is the sturdiest of the four items here.

EXPLICITLY REJECTED - see the explicitly_rejected_evidence field. The single most tempting piece of 'evidence' in this entire dossier was refused.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - this program has no formal Medical Spanish curriculum, no bilingual track and no named Spanish-language clinical service. It answers 'no' to the Medical Spanish question on its own AMA survey. What exists is indirect: a free hospital-wide interpreter service, a safety-net patient population, and a continuity clinic based in a named Spanish-speaking neurologist's private office.

summary: No connection to Universidad Central del Caribe or to any Puerto Rico medical school could be established - not among residents, not among the identifiable faculty, and not at the institutional level. The program publishes no eligibility language at all, so there is also no ambiguous wording that might inadvertently exclude a Puerto Rico LCME graduate. | [value relocated from `value` field, which the contract requires to be null for absence states] {"ucc_residents_identified": 0, "puerto_rico_school_residents_identified": 0, "puerto_rico_schools_represented": [], "ucc_faculty_identified": [], "puerto_rico_faculty_identified": [], "institutional_puerto_rico_affiliation": null, "eligibility_language_ambiguity_found": false, "eligibility_language_note": "No eligibility statement of any kind is published, so there is no 'LCME-accredited schools in the U.S. and Canada' phrasing here to flag - the absence of an eligibility page is the finding."}
raw_finding: SEARCHED AND NOT FOUND, with the search path stated. (1) RESIDENTS: no named roster exists anywhere (domain 11), so no UCC, Ponce Health Sciences University, University of Puerto Rico or San Juan Bautista graduate could be identified or excluded. FREIDA's aggregate for the 2026 cycle is 0.0% US MD, 50.0% DO, 50.0% IMG; since a UCC graduate would count as US MD, a reported 0.0% US MD is at least consistent with there being no Puerto Rico LCME graduate currently in the program, though a percentage is not a roster and this is not asserted as a headcount of zero. (2) FACULTY: the three individually identifiable neurology teaching physicians are Ariol Labrada MD (trained at LSU Health Sciences Center and University of Miami per a cross-institution bio), Roberto Sanchez Perez MD (Instituto Superior de Ciencias Medicas de Villa Clara, Cuba; University of Miami / Jackson vascular fellowship) and Jose Simon Canellas MD (no training history published on any page I opened). None has an identified Puerto Rico tie. No complete faculty roster exists to search further. (3) INSTITUTIONAL LEVEL: FREIDA's institution record for Palmetto General (ID 119676) lists exactly four medical-school relationships and all four are mainland osteopathic schools - Pacific Northwest University of Health Sciences COM, Midwestern University Arizona COM, Kansas City University COM, West Virginia School of Osteopathic Medicine. Nova Southeastern University KPCOM separately names Palmetto General an affiliated GME site for its own DO students. No Puerto Rico school appears in any institutional relationship. (4) ELIGIBILITY LANGUAGE: the contract asks me to flag programs that write eligibility as 'LCME-accredited schools in the U.S. and Canada' without naming Puerto Rico. This program publishes no eligibility criteria whatsoever - the registry-listed GME page renders no content, the URL it gives ERAS applicants returns 404, and its former residency site is a parked domain - so there is no such sentence to flag. That is not reassurance; it means a UCC applicant has no published basis on which to confirm her own eligibility and would have to ask the coordinator directly. FOR THE RECORD, because this governs how any future finding must be coded: Universidad Central del Caribe is an LCME-accredited United States MD school, and its graduates are US_MD in this schema - never CARIBBEAN and never OTHER_IMG. 'CARIBBEAN' here means offshore for-profit schools such as Ross, St George's, AUC, Saba, Texila and Windsor.
student_facing_absence_message: Research complete - no link to Universidad Central del Caribe or any Puerto Rico medical school was found among this program's residents, identifiable faculty or institutional affiliations. The program also publishes no eligibility criteria at all, so a UCC applicant would need to confirm eligibility with the coordinator directly.

raw_finding:
FRESHNESS LADDER, newest first. 2026-09-12: live fetches of palmettogeneral.org pages, the CMS provider dataset, the Wayback CDX index, and confirmation that the ERAS-listed program URL returns 404 and pghgme.com refuses connections. 2026-09-04: AAMC ERAS 2027 Participating Specialties & Programs page posting date, carrying the 'Participating' status row for 1801100160. 2026-08-20: FREIDA program node and survey node last-changed timestamps. 2026-07-21: FREIDA survey field_date_received for both this residency and its sibling Vascular Neurology fellowship - this is the single most important freshness fact in the dossier, because it is a full survey cycle newer than the 2025-07-16 instrument the rise registry was built from, and it is what allows the registry's Step-2, faculty-count, start-month, preliminary-positions, nonprofit-salary and resident-demographics values to be reclassified. 2026-03: NRMP Program Results 2022-2026, giving appointment-year-2026 quota and fill. 2025-03: NRMP Program Results 2021-2025, giving appointment years 2021-2024. 2025-02-13: Miami Herald / AOL report naming Healthcare Systems of America as operator since roughly September 2024 and documenting vendor nonpayment. 2024-07-02: WLRN report on the Steward bankruptcy's effects at this hospital. 2020-08-06 and 2020-03-12: the archived program FAQ and block-schedule PDF - stale, but the only sources in existence for curriculum detail, the attempts policy and the no-score-cutoff statement, and flagged as such in every domain that leans on them.

ACCESS BOUNDARIES, recorded rather than bypassed. (1) ACGME ADS public program search at apps.acgme.org is a reCAPTCHA-gated form; I did not attempt to solve it. I did test the public detail endpoint legitimately - apps.acgme.org/ads/Public/Programs/Detail?programId=1801100160 - which 302-redirects to /ads/Errors/Http404?errorMsg=No%20Results%20Found because ADS keys that route on an internal identifier rather than the public ten-digit ACGME ID, so no accreditation-status string is obtainable without the gated search. Accreditation status is therefore UNAVAILABLE_DUE_TO_ACCESS_BOUNDARY. (2) palmettogeneral.org/wp-json/wp/v2/pages returns HTTP 403 - the WordPress REST API is blocked, which would otherwise have enumerated every page on the hospital site. (3) qualitycheck.org, The Joint Commission's own certification directory, returns HTTP 403 to both its search page and its search API, so the Comprehensive Stroke Center certification could not be verified against the awarding body's own record. (4) x.com/pghneurology, an apparently program-run account, returns HTTP 403. (5) NRMP's List of Unfilled Programs and its program-level SOAP records are behind Match registrant authentication; pre-2021 program-level NRMP results could not be located in any public PDF. None of these was circumvented.

COMPLETION. 26 of 26 domain keys are populated and every one carries a substantive research state; the forbidden placeholder state appears nowhere in this record. Actual status distribution across the 26 domains: VERIFIED 5 (domains 1, 7, 18, 21, 26); PARTIALLY_VERIFIED 10 (domains 3, 8, 10, 13, 14, 16, 19, 22, 23, 24); RESEARCHED_NOT_PUBLIC 7 (domains 2, 5, 9, 11, 12, 15, 20); RESEARCHED_NOT_FOUND 2 (domains 17, 25); CONFLICT 1 (domain 4); STALE_NEEDS_REFRESH 1 (domain 6); NOT_APPLICABLE 0. No domain was marked NOT_APPLICABLE, because every one of the 26 genuinely applies to this program - it is active rather than closed. UNAVAILABLE_DUE_TO_ACCESS_BOUNDARY does not appear as a domain-level status because accreditation status is not itself one of the 26 domain keys; the ACGME reCAPTCHA boundary is recorded inside domain 1, in this domain, and in the conflicts list instead. Source accounting: 32 distinct URLs are catalogued in sources[], of which 30 are cited at domain level and 2 (the hospital pharmacy-residency page and the hospital news index) were opened for corroboration and are recorded without a domain citation. summary: The program sponsors J-1 visas through ECFMG only. H-1B sponsorship is explicitly unavailable for residency applicants at this institution.
raw_finding: FREIDA 2026 survey field_visa_status=['J-1 through ECFMG']; field_F1_OPT first year = No. The UFCOM-J GME 'Trainee Eligibility and Selection Policy' (current document, uploaded 2026/07) states under GENERAL APPOINTMENT REQUIREMENTS, verbatim: 'All medical graduates must be one of the following: United States citizen; or Lawfully employable (i.e., valid EA, PR or RA card - see definitions below); or, Eligible for an ECFMG sponsored J-1 Visa; or, Eligible for H1B sponsorship...' and then narrows it verbatim: 'Applicants to a UFCOM-J residency program are not eligible for H1B visa sponsorship due to the processing timeline outlined by Immigration Compliance Services.' value.determination: The program's own current FREIDA answer places a passed USMLE Step 2 CK at the INTERVIEW CONSIDERATION stage, not merely before the start date. FREIDA renders the answer under the verbatim section heading 'Medical Exam Licensing Requirements for Interview Consideration', and under that heading the rows read 'Must Have Passed USMLE Step 2 CK - Yes' for U.S. MD applicants and 'Must Have Passed USMLE Step 2 CK - Yes' for IMG applicants. This answer comes from the program's own survey received 2026-06-16, rendered on a page last updated 2026-08-20, so it is current for the 2026-2027 cycle. Separately determined, point by point: (a) REQUIRED WITH ERAS SUBMISSION - not stated; the program's How to Apply page lists 'USMLE or COMLEX score report' among ERAS documents but does not name Step 2 or set a submission date, and the program does not require supplemental information (field_nxt_supplement=false). (b) BEFORE INITIAL REVIEW - not separately published; FREIDA's 'Program Starts Reviewing Applications' row defers to 'Specialty Universal Dates' rather than naming a program date. (c) BEFORE INTERVIEW INVITATION - YES, this is the published position, per the FREIDA section heading above. (d) BEFORE RANKING - not separately published, though the institutional policy expressly contemplates programs adopting a rank-list prerequisite. (e) BEFORE START DATE - also true as an institutional floor: the UFCOM-J 'Medical Licensing Examination Policy' states verbatim 'All incoming residents will be required to pass all components of USMLE Step 2, COMLEX Level 2, or NBDE 2 in order to be appointed as a PRG-1 trainee' and adds verbatim 'Programs may choose to have a more stringent policy, i.e. they may require passage of Step 2/Level 2 as a prerequisite for an interview, or for being included on their rank order list.' The FREIDA answer is the program exercising exactly that stricter option. (f) NO CLEAR TIMING - rejected; the FREIDA heading supplies the timing. (g) CONFLICT - rejected; the program website is silent on timing rather than contradictory, and silence is not a conflict. CYCLE-OVER-CYCLE CHECK: the registry snapshot (release 2026-07-09, carrying the older survey received 2025-06-25) recorded 'US MD Step 2 passed: Yes; IMG Step 2 passed: Yes' - the same answer. So this program did NOT move in either direction between FREIDA cycles; the requirement is stable across both surveys. What changed between the two surveys is other content (demographics, faculty count, interview volume, accepting-applications flag), not the Step 2 answer. I did NOT infer this timing from a minimum-score rule, and indeed no minimum score exists.
value.exact_paraphrase: FREIDA, under the section heading 'Medical Exam Licensing Requirements for Interview Consideration': U.S. MD Applicants - 'Must Have Passed USMLE Step 1: Yes'; 'Must Have Passed USMLE Step 2 CK: Yes'. IMG Applicants - 'Must Have Passed USMLE Step 1: Yes'; 'Must Have Passed USMLE Step 2 CK: Yes'. DO Applicants - 'Must Have Passed COMLEX Level 1: Yes'; 'Must Have Passed COMLEX Level 2: Yes'; 'Requires the USMLE Step 1 and/or Step 2 CK: No'.
value.barrier_reasoning: YES, but a narrow and time-limited one rather than a disqualification. Alejandra sat Step 2 CK in late September 2026 with a result expected mid-October 2026, and she is applying in this very cycle (expected graduation June 2027, March 2027 Match). The OPDA Guide for Residency Applicants - Adult Neurology, 2026-2027 states verbatim that 'Applications open September 2, 2026 and programs begin reviewing applications September 23, 2026', and its Interviews table lists 'Universal interview offer date(s)' as a dash - there is NO coordinated neurology interview-offer date this cycle, so programs may release invitations from late September onward. Against a published requirement of a passed Step 2 CK for interview consideration, that leaves roughly a three-week window (about September 23 to mid-October 2026) in which her file does not yet satisfy this program's own stated interview-consideration standard. TWO STRONG MITIGANTS, both program-specific and published: (1) this program's own application deadline is December 31 - stated verbatim on its How to Apply page as 'The deadline for submitting your completed application is Dec. 31.' - which is materially later than the typical program and leaves a long runway after her result arrives; and (2) the OPDA guide gives the specialty's 'Typical interview offer window' as 'October 2026 - January 2027', so a mid-October result lands at the very start of the normal offer window, not after it. The program also interviews at volume relative to its size (56 interviews for 4 positions in 2025; 80 in 2024; 110 in each of 2021-2023), so invitations are not concentrated in a single early burst. NET: the barrier is real in form and should be planned around - not assumed away - but it is a short early-season gap rather than a bar, and this program's late deadline makes it one of the more forgiving places for a mid-October score to land. No probability or likelihood of matching is expressed or implied.

summary: The program publishes that a passed Step 2 CK is required for interview consideration. Alejandra's mid-October 2026 result creates a short early-season gap, but the program's December 31 deadline and the specialty's October-January interview window leave substantial runway.
