The immediately following, more specific sentence sets the actual deadline at rank-list submission and explicitly contemplates interviewing an applicant with no Step 2 score uploaded. The specific rule is taken as operative; the ambiguity is recorded rather than erased.

Against a denominator of 12 those percentages do not resolve to whole people. COMPLEMENT VS CENSUS, the defect the contract warns about: FREIDA field_total_positions = 12 and field_program_size = [4,4,4] are APPROVED COMPLEMENT; the registry stored these as 'Total Residents: 12' and 'Current Residents PGY1: 4; PGY2: 4; PGY3: 4', which a reader would take as a head count. The real published head count is 10. A second, compounding registry defect: because this is an Advanced program, FREIDA indexes its three accredited years as years 1-3, so the registry's 'Current Residents PGY1' label denotes the program's first neurology year, which is PGY-2 in ACGME terms. summary: The curriculum runs on 13 four-week modules a year. PGY-2 is inpatient-heavy with EEG/epilepsy and neuroradiology; PGY-3 is where the subspecialty outpatient blocks sit, including required movement disorders and multiple sclerosis; PGY-4 carries pediatric neurology at Nicklaus Children's in Miami, psychiatry in Tamarac, neurosurgery and 3.5 elective modules. A weekly half-day longitudinal clinic runs with the same preceptor for all three years, and neuropathology and neuro-ophthalmology are done at Cleveland Clinic in Ohio.
raw_finding: All rotation structure is quoted or closely paraphrased from the program page's Rotations section. PGY1, verbatim: 'The ACGME requires that the PGY1 year be spent in an ACGME or Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada-accredited general internal medicine training program.' PGY2, verbatim: 'Cleveland Clinic Florida uses a module system with 13 four-week modules making up the academic year. In total, a PGY2 resident has 8 inpatient modules, 2 general neurology outpatient modules, 2 EEG/Epilepsy (outpatient/inpatient) modules, and 1 neuroradiology module.' and 'Longitudinal outpatient clinic is scheduled one-half day per week with a staff preceptor who will work with the resident throughout the three years of training.' and 'The inpatient team consists of a neurology attending, a senior neurology resident, junior neurology resident, and occasionally a rotating medical and/or psychiatry resident and several medical students. Teaching/hospital rounds are held 7 days/week, 365 days/year. The on-call schedule averages every 6th night for PGY2 and PGY3 residents.' PGY3, verbatim: 'As a senior PGY3 resident, 4 modules are spent in the inpatient service, 4 1/2 in the outpatient service, 2 in EMG, 5 weeks in Neuropathology with Mondays spent in Neuro-ophthalmology, and 1/2 module in Sleep Medicine. Each outpatient rotation beyond the first year is spent in a subspecialty service including movement disorders, neuromuscular disease, multiple sclerosis, and cognitive/behavioral neurology. The Neuropathology and Neuro-ophthalmology rotations take place at Cleveland Clinic in Ohio.' PGY4, verbatim: 'As a senior PGY4 resident, 3 1/2 modules are spent in Pediatric Neurology, 3 1/2 modules in electives, 2 modules in the outpatient service, 1 module in Psychiatry, 1 module in Neurosurgery, and 2 inpatient module. The Pediatric Neurology rotation takes place at Nicklaus Children's Hospital in Miami; the Psychiatry at University Hospital and Medical Center in Tamarac.' ADULT-PROGRAM SCOPE NOTE, per contract law 2: the PGY-4 pediatric neurology block at Nicklaus Children's Hospital is a rotation inside this ADULT neurology curriculum and is legitimate adult-program curriculum data; no child neurology program's own page, roster or curriculum was used anywhere in this dossier. BRAND-STRING RESOLUTION on the psychiatry site: the program page names 'University Hospital and Medical Center in Tamarac', while the FREIDA 2026 participating-institution record for this program lists 'HCA Florida Woodmont Hospital', Tamarac FL 33321, 7201 N University Dr. These are the same Tamarac facility under its former and current names; both are recorded rather than silently merged. Conferences, verbatim: 'These include but are not limited to Grand Rounds, Emergency Neurology, Subspecialty lectures, Neuroradiology, Ethics, Psychiatry, CPC, Chairman Rounds, Journal Club, RITE review sessions, Continuum sessions, and Basic Neuroscience. The residents are responsible for preparing and presenting some of these lectures or conferences. In addition, residents are also responsible for completing regular COMET on-line and other web-based learning modules.' FREIDA 2026 duty-hour and structure fields: field_avg_hours_on_duty_y1 = 75, field_max_hours_on_duty_y1 = 24, field_avg_24hr_off_duty_y1 = '2.00', field_avg_hrs_lecture_conf_y1 = 5, field_training_outpatient_clinic = 20, field_train_ambulatory_nonhospit = 999 (Negotiable sentinel), field_research_rotation = 'Optional', field_research_rotation_duration = 0, field_special_tracks = ['Research track/fellowship (non-ACGME accredited)'], field_beyond_accredited_length = false, field_or_acgme_aoa = false (no osteopathic recognition), field_resident_fellow_offer_2019 = ['Integrative medicine curriculum','Debt management/financial counseling','Off-campus electives']. That last list is the field from which a Medical Spanish curriculum would be reported if one existed; it is absent, which corroborates the registry's 'Medical Spanish Curriculum: No' — see domain 24. FREIDA's own free-text special features, verbatim: 'One of the defining features of our neurology residency program is its comprehensive and hands-on clinical training. Residents are exposed to a broad spectrum of cases across divers patient populations, ensuring that they graduate with the experience and confidence necessary to manage complex medical scenarios. The programs affiliations with leading institution and specialty centers further enrich the clinical learning environment. Frequent didactic lectures and support for scholarly activity.'

raw_finding: SOURCE HIERARCHY DISCIPLINE: every substantive claim traces to an official program, GME, institutional, faculty-biography, benefits, NRMP, FREIDA, AAMC or awarding-body page. Twelve aggregator and physician-review domains surfaced repeatedly in search results (residencyadvisor.com, matcharesident.com, residencymatch.ai, doximity.com, healthgrades.com, webmd.com, vitals.com, medifind.com, md.com, healthcare6.com, health.usnews.com, beattheboards.com) and none was opened or cited. One aggregator-sourced search summary asserted that 'Cleveland Clinic Florida's neurology program is located at 2950 Cleveland Clinic Blvd in Weston, Florida 33331, with ACGME Code 1401121528' — 1401121528 is the ACGME identifier of the Cleveland Clinic Florida INTERNAL MEDICINE program, not the neurology program, as the NRMP directory pages for both programs confirm side by side. That is logged in fabrication_traps_caught. FRESHNESS RANKING OF SOURCES USED: NRMP Program Results (March 2026) > Parkinson's Foundation listing (April 2026) > FREIDA survey (received 2026-06-15, node changed 2026-08-20) > Cleveland Clinic Florida GME Benefits (AY2026-2027 table) > NRMP program directory and Cleveland Clinic provider records (retrieved 2026-09-12, with individual conflict-of-interest attestation dates of 2026-07-24 for Lugo-Sanchez and 2026-08-12 for Agyei) > the program's own residency page (content unchanged since at least 2026-07-08 and one academic year behind on its roster) > the registry snapshot (2026-07-09 release carrying a 2025-06-11 survey, i.e. the oldest substantive source in the set). PRIVATE WORK DIRECTORY DISCIPLINE: every fetched page, PDF, JSON payload and helper script created during this research was written only to this program's private working directory. No file written by any other agent was read, grepped, globbed or listed; no shared scratch root and no other w2_* or wave-1 archive directory was touched. The only files read outside the private directory are the two named in the prompt: the Florida research contract and this program's own registry JSON.
